### A failed mechanism expectation stops the optimization screen

The first immutable worker-proof candidate kept the full constructor and every
live authority, epoch, source and kernel check. Inside the same checked owner,
revalidation compared the original trust and context, hashed the signed envelope,
then hashed the retained canonical projection against the original body pin.
Under the existing SHA256 integrity assumption this could reuse the constructor's
signature proof without caching current authority. No field or retained buffer
was added. The exact old method was retained as a private test-only oracle.

The focused tests agree with that oracle across 128 seeded input/trust/context
cases, sixteen top-level projection mutations and four independent concurrent
owners. A single-owner mechanism test first observes ten full verifications,
then one after the change. All four platform/compiler lanes pass those four
tests, and 177 static contracts constrain the exact substitution and unchanged
live guards. Those results establish a local proof boundary, not a timing gain.

The [preregistered screen](../testing/performance/0.74/diagnostic-worker-proof-reuse-plan-20261016.md)
requires five alternating pairs and an upper 95% bootstrap ratio bound of 0.80
for both publication and binding. It does not complete. The first baseline
passes, but the first candidate fails the exact Setup counter: two full
verifications instead of the predicted one. Inspection of the unchanged fixture
explains the extra constructor: it verifies a policy to initialize modeled
authority, then creates the separate original kernel-bound policy owner.
The single-owner mechanism test did not model that second construction site.

The response is to stop, preserve the failure and revert the isolated candidate,
not silently change the expectation and continue the same experiment. No later
pair is run, no confidence interval is calculated and the failed invocation's
shorter elapsed time is not a speedup. The hypothesis remains unmeasured rather
than disproved; a corrected proposal must fix its construction-site accounting
before collecting a new screen, with the same practical floor and signed windows.
The [negative packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/worker-proof-reuse-20261016/README.md)
retains both binary hashes, the candidate patch, development reds and its rollback.

Separately, the candidate's current IPC regression repeats the old Host(Busy):
23 passes and one failure, without a retry. MSRV IPC passes all 24, and both
compilers pass the 99-test original-input group, 29 kernel tests, four-case manual
causal proof and 28 compile-fail examples. These greens neither explain the IPC
lock lifetime nor close the historical Time/Kernel(Invalid) causes. Product
throughput, Starting and server admission remain outside this local tooling step.

### Reusing immutable proof without caching current authority

The separately [preregistered second screen](../testing/performance/0.74/diagnostic-worker-proof-reuse-v2-plan-20261016.md)
accounts for both construction sites before implementation or measurements.
A new two-owner test first observes eighteen full verifications for two
constructors and sixteen revalidations, then requires exactly two. The prior
single-owner test still requires one. This protects the distinction between
reusing an owner's original proof and sharing admission between independent owners.

The resulting change is deliberately inside the immutable document boundary.
Construction still checks the complete signed canonical document. Revalidation
retains exact trust/key/body-pin/epoch and host-context equality, original envelope
SHA256 and sticky refusal. It also hashes the retained canonical projection to
detect internal corruption. Only the repeated document parse and signature proof
are removed. The retained owner gains no field or buffer. Live source files,
authority epochs, kernel/peer observations and signed time windows still execute
through the unchanged enclosing owners; no current revocation result is cached.

Five independently started pairs now complete in B/C, C/B, B/C, C/B, B/C order,
without a failed invocation, retry or sample exclusion. The two binaries keep the
same before/after hashes. Request-authentication and request-signature counts match
at every stage. Full worker-document verifications change from
99/72/908/308/2696/652 to 2/0/0/0/0/0 across the six stages: both constructors
survive, while repeated publication and binding work disappears.

| Local debug stage | Baseline seconds | Candidate seconds | Paired C/B ratio | 95% interval |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Reserved publication | 23.45–24.02 | 5.31–5.68 | 0.232739 | 0.228305–0.236526 |
| Heartbeat binding | 5.48–5.83 | 1.29–1.40 | 0.236497 | 0.228309–0.243068 |

The geometric paired-ratio estimator and seeded 10000-resample percentile
bootstrap are unchanged; both upper bounds clear the fixed 0.80 rule. These are
elapsed times from local unoptimized Rust 1.94 WSL fixtures, including diagnostic
instrumentation, not production CPU/op or native/RESP throughput. No measured
allocation reduction is inferred from removing parsing, and the separate stage
gains are not added together. The [second packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/worker-proof-reuse-v2-20261016/README.md)
retains all ten raw stage reports and independently reproduces their statistics;
the first failed screen and rollback remain separate immutable evidence.

All five portable proof tests pass on four platform/compiler lanes, with the
exact old method retained as a private test-only oracle. Eight build/strict-Clippy
lanes and 177 static contracts pass. Current and MSRV each pass 99 ordinary
original-input tests, 29 kernel tests, all 24 IPC tests, the unchanged four-case
causal proof and 28 compile-fail examples. Neither green IPC run retries a failed
invocation in this screen. They do not explain historical Host(Busy), Time or
Kernel(Invalid), or establish arbitrary shared-load safety.

The useful outcome is narrower than release qualification: repeated immutable
verification is a confirmed local tooling owner, and its isolated replacement
clears the preregistered debug floor without dropping live observations. The next
cost investigation must preserve that boundary. Authenticated original-start,
autonomous all-writer cessation, completion/later cells, real trust enrollment
and server rehearsal still need their own implementations and fault evidence.

### A completed transaction must release its own lock

The occasional IPC Host(Busy) needed a causal experiment, not a successful rerun.
The short host-root helper returned a raw File. On Linux a flock belongs to an
open file description shared by fork aliases: closing the parent's descriptor
does not release it while a child retains the same description. An explicit
unlock acts on that description. These are the relevant [kernel semantics](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html),
not evidence that a particular old failure had that owner. CLOEXEC is set in our
fixture, but the controlled child deliberately stays before exec.

Before changing ownership, a preregistered private checkpoint forks exactly one
owned child after successful acquisition. Pipe acknowledgements establish that
the original descriptor is still retained when the parent returns. The raw-File
control remains Busy until the child explicitly unlocks. Three regressions fail
on the baseline: ordinary short-owner drop, admission-construction error and a
real corrupt-ledger transaction followed by recovery. The last fails at variant
zero with Host(Busy); it does not establish seven baseline failures. This proves
a reachable mechanism, without reconstructing the missing PID/fd observations of
either historical incident.

The correction is a private non-cloneable short-fence owner. It wraps the File
only after successful flock and before fallible admission, and explicitly unlocks
that original description on drop. It adds no retry, sleep, wider deadline, marker
removal or new admission predicate. Production has no descriptor extraction or
borrow accessor. Existing private tests receive only a test-scoped borrow; exact
source-restoration contracts preserve their assertions and the original runtime
body outside the guard substitution. Long-lived campaign claims are unchanged.

All four causal controls now pass on Linux Rust 1.94 and 1.88. The corrupt/pending
ledger test traverses all seven variants, recovers the original revision while
the child still holds the old descriptor, and preserves file bytes, inode and
mode without a backend call. A separate control proves that failed contenders
and an old child's late unlock/close cannot unlock a new independent owner.
The child uses raw async-signal-safe operations only; pidfd/handshake/watchdog
cleanup targets just the exact owned unreaped child, never another process.

The [evidence packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/short-fence-20261016/README.md)
keeps the baseline reds, type-adaptation errors and two explicitly truncated
development captures alongside the complete final 178-contract output. Eight
build/strict-Clippy lanes pass. Both Linux compilers pass the 13-test host group,
four scan tests, fourteen preparation tests, five proof-reuse tests, old IPC/lease/
original-fence/host integrations (24/20/5/6), and 99 original-input tests with four
already registered manual exclusions. Both Windows compilers pass the portable
IPC/lease/host groups (21/18/5). These are semantic checks, not a throughput gain;
the earlier five-pair debug result remains pinned to its earlier source.

Raw File error paths before a HostExecutionClaim is constructed were outside
that short-helper fix. The separate construction correction below addresses
them; releasing a cooperative transaction still does not prove autonomous
all-writer cessation or authenticate original-start.

### Ownership must cover construction errors and an absent active claim

The next experiment keeps successful campaign ownership unchanged and tests the
interval before that owner exists. Both named acquisition/recovery and active
recovery acquire a flock before inspecting admission and the active marker.
On failure, or on active recovery returning None, the old raw File simply closed.
The already controlled pre-exec child could extend that lock's lifetime too.

Six preregistered tests reuse the exact private owned-child fixture rather than
introducing another process model. On the baseline, five test groups fail when
an independent open attempts to acquire after constructor return. The sixth,
successful ownership transfer, already passes all three routes. The failures
include an absent active claim and a late refusal after creating the marker:
neither a failed request nor Ok(None) should retain cooperative lock ownership.
Each failing group stops at its first case; the baseline did not execute all
23 successful-path/case combinations later covered by the fixed tests.

The private PendingHostClaim takes ownership only after successful flock and
before fallible admission. On early return it explicitly unlocks the original
description. On success it consumes an Option<File> into the unchanged claim;
there is no clone, reopen, relock or unsafe extraction. Emptying that Option
disarms the temporary owner, so its Drop cannot unlock a live successful claim.
Unlock remains best effort, not a receipt proving resource or writer release.

The enumerated cases cover factory and legacy-admission errors, malformed,
missing and conflicting markers, fixed-context refusal, both None branches,
late refusal on all three routes and successful Created/Recovered transfer.
Existing marker bytes, inode and mode remain unchanged; a newly created marker
survives late refusal. Independent lock probes verify release while the old
child still holds its descriptor. A later old-child unlock/close or failed
contender cannot release a new independent owner. Successful claims stay Busy
to contenders until their existing Drop. Admission ordering, final owner and
terminal marker-release predicates are preserved by exact-source restoration
with negative canaries, layered into the prior static contracts.

Both Linux compilers now pass all 19 host unit tests, including six new tests
covering the 23 cases and all prior short-fence controls. All 179 static contracts,
eight platform/compiler build/strict-Clippy lanes and old Linux/Windows integration
groups pass. Each compiler's ordinary original-input regression passes 99 tests
with the same four registered manual exclusions, without an IPC retry or changed
signed window. Those semantic greens do not requalify the earlier timing screen.

The [construction evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/claim-construction-20261016/README.md)
retains the baseline failures and development overlay separately from the pinned
fixed source. This is a second local ownership correction, not a throughput or
allocation optimization and not attribution of either old natural Host(Busy).
Authenticated original-start and cessation of every writer remain the next
execution boundary; completion, later cells and server admission remain closed.

### A fresh heartbeat is not consent to start

The original causal challenge proves that an authenticated controller answered
a newly generated commitment after Reserved acknowledgement. That does not
express a request to execute. Treating the existing signed Heartbeat as a start
command would change its meaning, even if the signature and freshness checks
were correct. The next boundary therefore starts with a distinct consent format,
not a new interpretation of old request bytes.

The first-cell consent has its own body/envelope schemas and Ed25519 domain.
Canonical LF JSON binds the original controller attempt, retained Reserved and
state, challenge nonce, authenticated response, worker-policy digest/epoch and
collector-unit digest to a revision-two Starting projection. It also signs a new
consent id, original reservation id, fixed controller/source/preset and a positive
signing window of at most sixty seconds. First-cell grammar excludes later cells,
running process/cgroup claims, cleanup success and promotable admission flags.
Body and envelope ceilings are 4096 and 8192 bytes. Old request, collector intent
and challenge domains cannot substitute even with the same signing key.

The implementation deliberately exposes byte/signature inspection, not a trusted
execution object. A supplied verifier key is not enrolled by using it, and a
signed timestamp is not an observed clock. Repeated inspection of the same bytes
succeeds; that is useful parsing behavior, not once-only execution. A future
consuming original owner must compare every claim against its retained kernel
peer/time, live trust/epoch/fence and original durable records, validate the
adjacent transition and retain the uncertain/replay intent before output or
process creation. No old admission deadline is refreshed or silently discharged.

The [consent evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/start-consent-20261016/README.md)
keeps the missing-module red and two test-development mistakes: a private helper
was inaccessible to integration tests, and an invented greater-than-forty leaf
expectation did not match the selected schema. The test now fixes the complete
eighteen-field inventory and mutates all 36 nested scalar leaves under seed
0x0740c0a2. This is a test inventory correction before the successful cohort,
not a performance or admission threshold adjustment. Other checks cover real
signatures, four foreign domains, thirty grammar refusals, duplicate/unknown/
noncanonical/partial/oversized input and four independent concurrent checkers.
The compatibility register describes this opt-in matched-reader contract.

These results establish the explicit signed-data boundary needed by original
start. They do not establish authenticated process creation, durable Starting,
autonomous watchdog or cessation of every writer. No product gain or server
admission follows from a correctly verified consent signature alone.

### Start consent checked against original kernel observations

The next implementation connects that signed-data contract to the original
receiver and ownership chain. It consumes the causal response owner, derives a
first-cell Starting projection from a kernel observation and freezes the body
before requesting a signature. Even validly signed replacement claims must match
every frozen field. The later consent packet must belong to the same receiver,
arrive after preparation and satisfy actual peer/principal/time checks under
the retained controller policy. Original policy/epoch, storage and common-fence
checks remain around authentication; failure retains refused owners and the lock.

This makes an important distinction visible: a once-consumed Rust owner is not a
durable once-only start. A crash after acceptance still requires a journaled
intent and an explicit uncertain-acknowledgement rule before any output or process
can be created. The current consumer writes neither Starting nor a new replay
record, and it cannot publish or launch. Reopening byte evidence cannot recreate
the owner. Root collector ownership, original process/cgroup authentication and
cessation of every writer remain required before completion or later cells.

The first default-debug composition also exposed the cost of nested validation:
the original Heartbeat expired before consent acceptance. The existing ten-second
deadline refused the attempt; it was not raised. A separately declared correctness
lane with optimized Ed25519/curve arithmetic passes the joined cases on both
current and minimum Rust versions, while preserving all observations. That is
not an established production speedup or a default-debug pass. The exact installed
build must still demonstrate budget viability; future reuse of immutable proof
work would need its own attribution and unchanged live revocation checks.

The [original-consent evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-start-consent-20261016/README.md)
records real socket credential/order refusals, 36 frozen-field mutations, id
collisions, trust/storage drift, consuming-API compile failures and the unchanged
integration/static contracts. It establishes a local admission prerequisite,
not authenticated process creation, durable replay safety or server readiness.

### Validation cost before durable publication

Before adding Starting, we tested whether the admitted original consent leaves
time for its publication checks. Each fresh chain performs the real original
admission, then requests nineteen unchanged validations: two for each of nine
planned write boundaries and one final check. This first experiment deliberately
omits the writes and fsyncs. If checks alone expire, adding storage cannot justify
calling the path ready.

All twelve local chains refused. With optimized Ed25519/curve dependencies in an
otherwise dev build, Rust 1.94 completed 0, 1 and 1 checks; Rust 1.88 completed
1, 1 and 1. The separate normal release-profile control completed 4, 5 and 5
checks on each compiler, still short of nineteen. The old challenge or Heartbeat
window expired, and the original owner became sticky-refused while retaining
the common fence. Bytes and the two-file inventory were checked before deliberate
cleanup/failure controls. No new Starting record was created. These are local
correctness-budget observations, not product throughput results or measurements
of an installed server binary.

The tests pass by correctly reporting and retaining that refusal. The publication
budget itself fails. Keeping these two outcomes separate prevents an ordinary
green test receipt from becoming an unsupported execution permission. The
release-profile control also rules out treating optimized crypto compilation
alone as a sufficient local repair; neither the deadline nor the workload was
changed to obtain a green budget result.

A separate diagnostic then checks the original worker, controller, reviewed build
and OIDC owners without creating an intent. Three fresh inputs and three checks
per owner on both compilers consistently report 0, 1, 2 and 4 IPC authentications
per check. The first Rust 1.94 dev sample's single consent check performed
264 IPC authentications before refusing. The nested composition is a concrete target
for further investigation. The recorded IPC signature spans cover only those
signatures, not every crypto primitive or all validation work. Inclusive owner
durations overlap in meaning and must not be added. Current-thread CPU counters
also show coarse quantization, including zeros for short intervals; those zeros
do not mean the checks are free.

The next design question is how to retain immutable proofs while checking every
live trust, epoch, kernel and storage predicate around each effect without
recursively multiplying the same observations. A private per-boundary validation
frame is a proposal, not an implemented optimization. Its observation order and
mutation canaries require architectural review; caching a previous live result
or increasing a window would not satisfy the contract. Durable publication and
real crash tests follow that proof, then original start, whole-writer cessation,
signed installation and bounded nonproduct host rehearsal.

The [budget evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/consent-publication-budget-20261016/README.md)
retains all samples and explicitly keeps publication, server and qualification
admission closed. The useful result is a reproducible blocker found before any
uncertain storage or execution authority was created, not a new performance claim.

### Coalescing validation without caching live authority

After operator review, we implemented a separate consuming validation-frame
candidate. It preserves the original owner, packets, fence and every lower
worker/controller/build/OIDC guard. Instead of recursively invoking the outer
collector wrappers, it performs two explicit rounds: storage, live reservation,
progress authentication, causal binding, prepared policy/transition checks,
original consent authentication, storage again and final clock checks. The
closing round has no fault callback. No signature result or previous live
observation is cached as permission for the next boundary.

This is deliberately narrower than immutable-proof reuse. The frame still pays
for the original lower guards, but no longer multiplies their calls through the
outer recursion. Complete framed checks report 34 IPC authentications; the
earlier diagnostic observed 264 for a refusing old check. Counts explain the
mechanism; they are not an exclusive cost model or a product speedup ratio.

The same three-chain/nineteen-check experiment was retained, changing only the
consuming adapter and diagnostic labels. Optimized-crypto dev lanes completed
6/8/11 checks on Rust 1.94 and 10/10/11 on 1.88: still a negative budget result.
Normal release completed 19/19/5 on 1.94 and 19/19/19 on 1.88. The third 1.94
chain did not simply run out of time. WSL realtime moved backwards by about
four seconds while boottime advanced, so the unchanged kernel clock-order guard
refused it. The fixture's `admitted` field means all nineteen publication-free
checks finished, never that a server process is admitted.

That distinction mattered again in the live-mutation matrix. Five first-cut
cases correctly refused worker/OIDC/controller trust drift, an unexpected
authority-context file and a removed Reserved file while retaining the fence.
The next fresh chain encountered another backwards realtime step before the
next fault cut. It is not a completed forty-cut matrix, reference comparison or
concurrent-revocation proof. Read-only clock observation found further realtime
steps relative to uptime. Enabled WSL timesyncd and stopped Windows time service
are environmental observations, not proof of a unique cause.

The failure remains part of the record. We did not increase any ten-second
window, replace an original timestamp, disable a guard or alter a time service.
A separately declared stable-clock control is needed to finish the fault gate.
Then actual exclusive Starting publication must demonstrate its own writes,
sealing, fsyncs and uncertain acknowledgement under the same live checks, followed
by real SIGKILL boundaries. Original process/cgroup start, watchdog, cessation
of every writer, later cells and signed server rehearsal remain later gates.
The [approved design](../testing/performance/0.74/diagnostic-validation-frame-design-20261016.md)
records those limits; a promising publication-free result is not a release claim.

The separately preregistered environment control then disproved the narrow
working assumption that stopping WSL timesyncd alone would stabilize this host.
With explicit operator approval, the wrapper stopped only that service, retained
the unchanged executable hashes and began a ninety-second clock preflight.
At sample seven realtime went backwards by 3.15 seconds while boottime advanced
by one second. The probe refused before a matrix or budget command could begin.
Its exit handler restored the service; an independent observation confirms it
active and enabled. Windows settings, clock values and clocksource were not
changed. This is evidence of an unresolved environment problem, not a unique
diagnosis of Hyper-V, Windows or NTP, and not a reason to discard the old refusals.

The [clock-control packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/validation-frame-clock-control-20261016/README.md)
keeps that failure separately. Further host clock changes or a stable Linux
test environment needed separate agreement. At that point the full fault gate
was incomplete, the runtime patch was uncommitted and server admission was closed.

### The same fault matrix on dedicated Linux

The operator then authorized the unchanged fault matrix in a private temporary
directory on the dedicated server, without installing a release, stopping the
supervisor or running product traffic. The exact previously built executables
passed once per compiler: forty combinations of validation cut and mutated
input, five independently constructed old-reference cases and healthy-order,
failed-construction and concurrent-mutation controls. Every fault refused while
retaining the original owners and Busy fence. Both final test results passed;
no unsuccessful case was replaced with another attempt.

The server's installed binary and receipt hashes, supervisor PID/start time,
restart count and boot remained unchanged. The fixtures ran as the nonroot SSH
account in their own TMPDIR, not as an enrolled production worker. This is the
specific evidence that closes the frame's fault gate and permits committing
the isolated refactoring. It does not test actual Starting writes, SIGKILL or
lost acknowledgement, and it grants no production execution permission.

The earlier dev expirations and WSL failures remain in their original packets.
Passing the same code elsewhere does not uniquely identify which WSL clock
mechanism caused the backwards steps. Nor can correctness durations on this
host be combined with the old host's timings into a speedup claim. The
[server fault packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/validation-frame-server-fault-20261016/README.md)
retains the exact raw logs and narrow scope; durable publication is the next
separate hypothesis.

### A consistent Starting record is not a durable acknowledgement

After the frame fault gate, the next isolated change implemented only the byte
contract of the new collector Starting record. We first retained the missing-API
compile failure, then added a strict encoder and inspector reusing the original
prior-history parser. The record binds exact canonical LF history and signed
consent bytes to the complete Starting state. It does not replace signature
verification, kernel peer/time observations or the retained original owner.

The tests distinguish byte integrity from authority deliberately: a well-shaped
but invalid signature can describe consistent bytes while the actual signature
validator refuses it. Mutation tests also distinguish the original consent's
state hash without LF from the older Reserved projection hash with LF. Silently
normalizing those two rules would weaken binding rather than improve efficiency.
All 3038 strict prefixes of the golden record refuse, along with 58 leaf,
nine rehashed binding and seven rehashed grammar/state mutations on both compiler
lanes. The implementation leaves the old two-file storage inventory unchanged.

The [byte-record evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/collector-starting-record-20261016/README.md)
retains the red tests, assembly corrections and final 184-contract result. There
is no allocation or throughput claim here: this is a correctness prerequisite
for a separate consuming publisher. Exclusive creation, partial writes, sealing,
file/directory fsync and lost acknowledgement must still be tested with actual
SIGKILL boundaries before the record can become durable runtime progress. A
complete file found after a crash must never recreate the missing live owner.

### Real fsync exposed the remaining anchored validation budget

The next isolated candidate consumed the original framed consent, latched a
private storage phase and exclusively created its own Starting document. It
wrote a prefix and suffix, sealed the original file, fsynced it and its directory,
then attempted acknowledgement under nineteen full frame checks. The old default
reader remained a two-file reader; partial history, descriptor drift and a failed
attempt could not be repaired or adopted. Clock-free storage/API checks, the
unchanged regressions and 185 static contracts passed for this candidate.

The real server fault gate did not. On both compilers, eight independently
injected interruptions passed through DirectorySynced, but the chain intended
for Acknowledging refused before reaching its hook. The runner stopped the full
crash phase instead of treating the unexpected failure as an injected success.
A separately declared diagnostic constructed four fresh publication chains;
all reported Original(Causal(Time)) after DirectorySynced with no acknowledgement,
about 5.1 seconds after publication began. These are correctness diagnostic
observations, not throughput measurements or a product speedup.

That five-second interval does not replace the original ten-second causal
window. Its origin is the earlier challenge issuance, before response admission,
preparation, consent acceptance and frame construction. The approved frame
reduces recursive work only after acceptance; earlier composition still consumes
the same anchored budget. Source order motivates examining it, but does not
by itself attribute every second to signatures or fsync. Renewing the challenge,
resetting the clock origin or acknowledging an expired owner would change the
contract and is not an optimization.

The [negative publication evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/collector-starting-publication-20261016/README.md)
therefore retains the candidate and refusals without promoting them. A complete
sealed and fsynced file is still not runtime acknowledgement; refusal before ack
also does not prove loss of an ack that had already succeeded. The next proposed
change needs a separate review of constant-depth preparation and acceptance,
with the old guards as a functional reference and every live predicate retained.
The full Acknowledging, AfterReturn, lost-ack and uninterrupted controls remain
necessary before this path can be accepted.

The separately preregistered partial crash diagnostic then killed actual owned
children at the eight already reachable pre-ack cuts on each compiler: sixteen
SIGKILL terminal outcomes and thirty-two independent fresh-process inspections.
Retained byte/inode/ownership/mode/time snapshots stayed unchanged, the lock was
Busy while the owner lived and released after death, and fixed-history admission
still refused. Both partial tests pass; Acknowledging, AfterReturn, lost ack and
the successful uninterrupted control remain unproved. The negative publisher is
archived and removed from active runtime rather than admitted on partial proof.

### Move the composition boundary, not the deadline

The next change required explicit approval because it moved constant-depth
validation earlier, into consent preparation and acceptance. The old public
guards remained an independent reference. The new consuming preparation freezes
the same body exactly once from the same original kernel observation and keeps
the original causal, Heartbeat, Reserved and signed-consent time origins.
Each preparation check performs a working round followed by an unhooked closing
round over original storage, live reservation, authenticated progress, causal
challenge, frozen projection and fresh kernel clocks. Acceptance requires the
later actual packet from the same receiver and enters the existing full
consent-authenticated frame directly.

This changes orchestration, not what counts as authority. Signatures are still
verified; peer/liveness, trust, epoch/history, descriptors, inventory and fence
remain live. No immutable-proof cache, extended window, new challenge or caller
timestamp was introduced. A failed construction or check retains refused owners
and the Busy fence; it cannot yield an owner for retry, extraction or execution.

Before reconnecting publication, the
[pre-consent semantic packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/preconsent-frame-20261016/README.md)
passed 48 cases on each compiler: 35 cut/drift combinations, five independently
constructed old-reference refusals, invalid consent and request IDs, an already
refused constructor, a healthy same-receiver control and a concurrent mutation
that only the closing round detects. Source contracts compare the frozen-body
construction and predicates with the old implementation. Seeded age edges,
positive named-owner API checks and negative clone/deserialize/extract/retry/
publish/start examples distinguish equivalent checks from a weakened interface.

Only then did we restore the rejected publisher as a separate candidate.
Its storage, publisher and SIGKILL harness are byte-exact archive restorations;
the fixture changes only its preparation and acceptance calls. The exclusive
create, prefix/suffix write, seal, file/directory fsync, nineteen complete frame
checks, nine cuts, AfterReturn and three repetitions stay unchanged. This makes
the hypothesis specific: can the earlier composition complete the original
publication contract without spending an expired owner's authority?

The [complete process-loss packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/collector-starting-framed-20261016/README.md)
now passes on normal Rust1.94/1.88 GNU release test binaries on the same dedicated
host. Each compiler passes nine interruptions, nine live drifts and a healthy
publication, followed by thirty actual pidfd-targeted SIGKILLs, three uninterrupted
controls and sixty-six independent fresh-process inspections. At AfterReturn
the child has already received and revalidated its acknowledged runtime owner.
Its death loses that owner; fresh inspection preserves the retained bytes and
metadata but refuses to reconstruct permission, including for complete fsynced
records. The lock is Busy while the original owner lives and released after
death, without turning that release into durable replay authorization.

That result supports bounded operational feasibility under the unchanged
windows. It is not a paired benchmark, a measured signature/fsync split,
deadline headroom under load or a RESP/native throughput improvement. Earlier
expiration and partial-crash evidence remain intact. These checks cover process
loss of runtime acknowledgement, not an external wire ACK, power loss, reboot
or storage-device EIO. The nonroot fixtures ran only in owned temporary trees;
the installed binary/receipt, boot and stable supervisor identity did not change.

Durable first-cell intent is therefore one completed prerequisite, not an opened
production route. Independently enrolled trust and original controller admission,
private executable/output/streams/process/cgroup start, autonomous watchdog and
all-writer cessation must still precede completion and cells two through four.
Signed installation and an integrated nonproduct lifecycle rehearsal remain
separate gates before any numerical pilot or release qualification.

### Original pipes are a prerequisite for original start

The next isolated step creates the real anonymous pipe objects before any worker
handoff. It consumes the acknowledged Starting owner rather than accepting caller
paths, descriptors, replacement authority or timestamps. Both streams have
distinct retained kernel identities, close-on-exec descriptors, nonblocking read
ends and blocking write ends. Full original Starting checks bracket kernel
observations; successful preparation neither renews the challenge nor opens an
execution route.

Descriptor identity alone is insufficient. Access/status flags belong partly to
the shared open-file description: changing nonblocking mode through a duplicate
writer affects the retained original too. The joined test changes those flags
on another thread between two inspections. It must obtain pipe Invalid after
successful original validation, not mistake expiration of the original window
for evidence that descriptor substitution was detected.

Review also exposed an ownership-order requirement before the final build was
dispatched. Rust drops fields in declaration order, so pipes must precede the
Starting owner that retains the fence. The static contract checks that exact
ordering; the healthy joined case retains read observers and requires actual
EOF after owner drop. A separate kernel test keeps a duplicate writer alive,
observes WouldBlock rather than EOF on an empty queue, writes late bytes, then
obtains EOF only after the last writer closes. Filling the kernel queue and
checking write readiness separately exercises blocking backpressure.

The [pipe preparation packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-collector-pipes-20261016/README.md)
passes nineteen fresh chains on each compiler: six interruptions, eight
descriptor/flag substitutions, trust and concurrent drift, acknowledgement-time
trust drift, a pre-refused constructor and a healthy drop control. The old
publisher/storage and all time origins remain unchanged. The packet also retains
an invalid first postflight assembly whose zero exit and printed success were
contradicted by a missing-function error; only the corrected strict postflight
is accepted. Neither server matrix was repeated to repair that reporting error.

This proves ownership and closure of private, unexported pipes. Close-on-exec is
not revocation of copies intentionally handed to a manager or worker, and this
owner cannot become a FixtureDrain or manufacture authenticated completion.
The next producer must create the sole-root sinks and bind these same pipes to
the original executable, manager invocation, process and cgroup, with an autonomous
watchdog and proven cessation of every writer. The bounded fixture success is
not a throughput measurement or a guarantee of deadline headroom for that later
composition. Production enrollment and server execution remain closed.

### Attribute the validation walk before changing its schedule

The next [attribution and join packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-collector-sinks-join-20261017/README.md)

Starting takes 5.873–5.884 seconds on Rust 1.94 and 5.788–5.808 on 1.88. Its
nineteen ordinary validations perform thirty-eight complete rounds and 646

The measured signature primitive does not explain that wall time. It contributes

free. Starting uses nineteen rounds; pipe preparation uses six, including fresh
checks immediately before each allocation; sinks use twenty-one. The complete
constructor now performs forty-six rounds. Its single consuming entry retains

and latches the whole original chain. Neither live proofs nor mutable authority
are cached, and no challenge, admission origin or deadline is renewed.

The complete joined mutation/interruption matrices and the subsequent owned-child

### Process loss does not recover an original output owner

The complete follow-up matrix covers twenty-five effect cuts plus death after
successful return. Three exact-source repetitions on each compiler produce
156 real SIGKILL cases, six uninterrupted controls and 324 fresh read-only
inspections. Every expected case passes. The parent retains a pidfd for its own
unreaped child, waits for a bounded logical barrier, checks that the original
fence is Busy and records exact bytes/metadata before sending the signal. A
timeout is only the harness fail-safe, never the correctness oracle.

Starting may be absent, empty, prefix-only, completely written but unsealed,
sealed or synced. Pipes may be only partly initialized. Output directories and
empty sinks may be only partly created or synced. None of these retained states
becomes a recovered permission to continue. Even a fully durable successful
return followed by lost runtime acknowledgement refuses reconstruction in both
fresh inspecting processes. The uninterrupted controls retain the same original
process and close their private descriptors normally.

These are process-loss facts, not power-loss, device-EIO or external wire-ACK
guarantees. The writer descriptors are still private and no worker or pump ran,
so the result does not certify revocation of exported writers. Independent final
postflight checks leave the installed binary/receipt, original supervisor PID
8839/start/restart count, boot and absent production contexts exact. No service,
clock, product workload or qualification setting changed.

The useful result is deliberately narrow: original output preparation now fits
the unchanged admission window and refuses uncertain replay at real process
boundaries. It is not a product throughput win or server-ready release. Real
production trust and authenticated executable/streams/process/cgroup start,
collector writing/watchdog, all-writer cessation and later lifecycle cells still
follow under their own gates. The earlier red oracle and broader legacy audit
failures remain evidence rather than being erased by this completed prerequisite.

### Preserve original pipes through message encoding

The [next isolated slice](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-pipe-transport-20261017/README.md)
addresses a concrete transport limitation: the old systemd property enum has
no Unix FD variant. Extending that general transport would widen an unrelated
execution entry. Instead, a distinct consuming preparation takes the retained
original material and builds an opaque, unsent message. No bus connection or
start method is available. The complete signed collector projection is checked
again, and every one of its 35 typed worker settings must match. Legacy
regular-file output signatures and their transport remain byte-exact.

The message encodes the same original stdout/stderr write ends as Unix FD
values, not integers that merely resemble descriptor numbers. Tests decode the
actual message body and its owned out-of-band table, inspect pipe identities
and flags, and reject swapped streams, duplicate stream identity, a read end,
a regular file, changed settings and malformed headers/body. This verifies
representation inside the process, not delivery over SCM_RIGHTS or acceptance
by the installed manager. Binary bytes and separate streams are exercised with
real anonymous pipes, without running the observer or a product workload.

An important lifecycle consequence is visible even before sending: message
encoding creates two additional writer copies. Closing the creator's original
writer does not produce EOF while the message still owns its duplicate. The
kernel read returns EOF only after the final copy closes. The retained object
therefore drops message copies before the original material and fence. A
construction error retains the whole owner, and later errors permanently
refuse it. This strengthens the reason to count every creator and manager copy
when implementing actual start; a dead worker leader cannot establish cessation.

Three fresh original chains on each normal GNU release compiler pass both
construction and subsequent revalidation. Each phase performs 34 authentications,
two complete fresh original rounds, with the same old leaf predicates and
unchanged origins. The phase spans are about 321–326 milliseconds on this host;
they include live filesystem walks and bundle checks, not just marshalling.
They are descriptive fixture observations, not a paired improvement estimate or
an assertion that collector overhead is acceptable for measurement.

All nine independent refusal cases pass per compiler: fixture entry, bundle
failure at entry, already-refused material, missing message, later bundle,
output, trust, fixture validation and actual progress-age expiry. Each requires
the intended refusal rather than accepting any error. The expiry case preserves
the exact ten-second origin and bound; the others cannot pass through an
incidental timeout. Original intent documents remain unchanged, and the fence
stays held until owner drop. Six healthy chains and eighteen exact refusals
close this message prerequisite, not the execution path.

The retained negative results are tooling failures, not rejected performance
hypotheses: missing API, two incorrect test expectations, a nonexistent test
target, an extra registry blank line and a non-executable transferred test
binary. None requires changing a runtime predicate or a deadline. The corrected
packet passes 190 static contracts and both compiler gates, and verifies its
predecessor at the exact old source without rewriting old proof. Independent
postflight confirms the supervisor and installed binary/receipt are unchanged.

The next producer still must arm an autonomous watchdog before an authenticated
send, derive remaining absolute cell/total deadlines instead of renewing the
signed RuntimeMax ceiling, bind the original executable/effective environment,
manager invocation/process/cgroup, and revoke all writers before releasing the
fence. Only then can authenticated completion, later cells and their new
SIGKILL/lost-ack matrix proceed. Preparing an unsent message is not an installed
production start or another completed crash matrix.

The [next diagnostic](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/controller-syscall-cost-20261017/README.md)

This favors a narrowly scoped composition proposal over an assumed expensive
immutable signature. Any grouping of nonexecuting material/message/alarm

The supervisor and installed artifacts remain unchanged. The rejected alarm,
authenticated start, independent guardian, all-writer cessation and later
SIGKILL/lost-ack boundaries keep their separate admission requirements.
