The useful conclusion is narrower than production readiness: grouped preparation
can survive its healthy reference gate with the original deadlines. All 194
static contracts preserve the old runtime bodies. New real process-loss/ack-loss
tests and a production adaptation are still needed; a retained timer alone is
not an independent guardian. Authenticated original start, cessation of every
writer, completion and later lifecycle cells retain their separate proof gates.

## Real process loss tests refusal after a missing return acknowledgement

The [next harness](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/grouped-process-loss-20261017/README.md)
keeps the grouped candidate unchanged and moves the interruption outside its
control flow. A selected child stops after each of five internal acquisition
steps or just after successful return, before its private acknowledgement.
The parent holds a pidfd opened for that exact unreaped Child before waiting
for readiness. SIGKILL through that descriptor and the resulting signal wait
status distinguish actual process death from a logical injected error. Rust
destructors do not execute in the killed child.

The recovery oracle is not merely that the child vanished. While it is stopped,
the original flock must exclude another owner and the parent independently
checks complete sealed records and empty sinks. After confirmed exit, kernel
cleanup must permit lock acquisition without changing the original ancestry
or authority snapshot. Two separately started inspectors must then reject a
new empty context while preserving retained history. Process death must not
turn an incomplete attempt into permission to adopt, repair or execute again.

Two normal-exit controls keep the ACK conclusion honest. One completes unchanged
reference validation, drops the owner and emits exactly one private ACK. The
other follows the same healthy path but deliberately emits none. The latter is
return-notice loss with zero exit, not a crash, a systemd StartTransientUnit
response or network delivery evidence. Both still leave retained history that
fresh processes refuse. Readiness is an independent test checkpoint, never an
execution acknowledgement or capability.

The original output-join crash harness remains exact after stripping only a
two-line child registration; its ownership, snapshots, lock and output-inventory
checks are reused. The new cases do not relax original time origins or add
production APIs. They cover selected logical cuts, not arbitrary in-syscall
death, power loss, authenticated original start or termination of every external
writer. A retained one-shot timer remains distinct from an autonomous guardian,
and these fault results supply no product throughput claim.

The declared preparation matrix passes on both normal GNU release compilers.
Three repeats each on Rust 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 produce 36 SIGKILLs, six ordinary
ACK controls and six normal exits with ACK withheld. A separate first screen
adds one SIGKILL and one ordinary control. Two fresh inspectors per case total
100 independent refusals with unchanged retained evidence. All 195 static
contracts pass and independent host postflight preserves the supervisor and
installed artifacts. This closes the selected grouped-preparation interruption
gate; authenticated production start, manager acknowledgement recovery,
autonomous guardian and all-writer cessation remain separate unfinished work.

## Fixed origin preparation does not grant execution authority

The [fixed origin adaptation](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/fixed-grouped-preparation-20261017/README.md)
turns the successful grouped schedule into a distinct nonexecuting production
type. Its constructor consumes the acknowledged original sinks and accepts no
replacement path, key, clock, descriptor, timeout or callback. It loads only the
fixed installed bundle with the original checked builder policy and identity.
The fixture loader and mutation checkpoints disappear from non-test builds;
a failed fixed load cannot fall back to the signed test bundle.

Grouping still changes observation frequency, not the admission predicates.
One complete original output/material round precedes construction. The retained
projection and Starting record bind the bundle and unsent two-FD message. A
provisional one-shot timer uses the minimum absolute BOOTTIME boundary derived
from Reserved, Starting and the original progress kernel receipt. Closing
repeats the complete original-chain, build, transition, message/FD and deadline
checks, compares the same bounds and inspects the timer before marking material
ready. Persistent closing drift is rejected; a transient mutation restored
between endpoints is not certified absent.

The rejected separately bracketed alarm and previous grouped fixture stay
unchanged as independent references. The new type deliberately retains its own
small timer primitive and original_round copy. A static guard requires exact
source equality after only the error-type rename, with negative controls for
deadline equality and replacing progress receipt with a fresh time. Other guards
strip only the exact additive registrations before comparing the older bodies.
This avoids turning a reference refactor into an unmeasured admission change.

The first screen and three fresh controls per compiler pass with the shared
grouped construction body. Each construction and subsequent full revalidation
makes 34 IPC authentications and signatures; the original offsets stay
300/60/10 seconds. Repeated construction spans are 361.724–364.171 milliseconds
on Rust 1.94 and 361.386–361.684 on MSRV 1.88. Revalidation spans are
334.937–339.191 and 334.596–335.250 milliseconds respectively. These inclusive
synthetic spans test the new composition's deadline and semantic feasibility,
not cache throughput or a paired performance comparison with the old candidate.

Both compilers also pass fourteen persistent-drift/expiry cases each. Separate
origin controls require the actual fixed constructor to refuse an absent install
without fallback, and a fixture owner to refuse production revalidation. All four
expected origin refusals preserve records and hold the fence while latching the
whole original chain. An initially wrong outer test expectation is retained as a
negative; its two-line test-only correction and new binaries form a separate
cohort rather than a replacement for the original timing evidence.

The distinction between preparation and execution is structural. The new owner
exports revalidation, not a message, timer descriptor, send, start or rearm
capability. Any failure latches the original chain and retains all resources and
the fence until explicit owner drop. Compile-fail checks also keep fixture entry,
cloning and deserialization unavailable to production callers. No service route
uses this type to start a worker. A private retained timer cannot terminate a
writer when its observer dies: independent guardian lifetime, authenticated
original delivery and P2/P3 cessation of every writer must precede that authority.

## Process loss evidence follows the retained owner

The [new process harness](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/fixed-grouped-process-loss-20261017/README.md)
tests the production grouped owner's shared construction body through its closed
fixture entry. Similar method names and an earlier prototype's green crash matrix
are not a certificate for a different owner. Here the actual new type must retain
the original fence, files, message writer duplicates and timer at each selected
interruption point. Static comparisons keep its runtime and the older harness
exact; only private test namespaces and the constructor differ.

The six cuts cover five internal acquisition checkpoints and successful return
before a private ACK. Each case pins the exact unreaped child with pidfd, checks
lock exclusion and independently inspects the sealed original records and empty
outputs before termination. Kernel terminal readiness and wait status signal 9
distinguish actual SIGKILL from a logical refusal. Two separately started
inspectors must then reject existing history while preserving the checked bytes
and identity/mtime/ctime inventory. Normal controls finish full revalidation and
owner drop, either emitting exactly one ACK or deliberately omitting it at zero
exit. The latter is missing return notification, not manager delivery evidence.

That lock result has a precise execution limit. A killed nonexecuting preparer
must release its kernel resources and leave history ineligible for reuse. During
actual execution, by contrast, the fence must remain held independently of the
controller while any worker or collector can still write. The private timer does
not enforce that lifetime. Autonomous guardian ownership and proven cessation of
all writers therefore precede any future original send/start capability; this
matrix does not turn ordinary process cleanup into that stronger guarantee.

Both normal GNU release compiler cohorts pass three repeats of the declared
six-cut matrix. The main cohorts contain 36 SIGKILLs, six ordinary controls and
six zero-exit omitted-ACK controls. A separate first screen adds one SIGKILL and
one ordinary control; together all 50 cases produce 100 fresh-process refusals
without changing the checked retained history. All 199 static contracts and the
independent host postflight pass with the original supervisor and installed
artifacts unchanged. This closes the new owner's selected nonexecuting process
cuts. It is neither a product speedup result nor authenticated execution admission.

## The watchdog must not share the disk writer

An absolute timer does not by itself make a watchdog autonomous. If the same
process drains pipes into regular files and observes the timer, a blocked write
or fsync can also block revocation. The private kernel implementation therefore
separates a collector from a guardian. A one-shot barrier keeps the collector
idle until the guardian has pinned its actual child with pidfd and closed its
own regular-file writer aliases. The guardian can then observe the already
selected absolute deadline without performing disk output.

Ownership is as important as process separation. A duplicate flock descriptor
shares an open-file description: another owner's explicit unlock can release
the lock for both. The private engine transfers ownership and closes the parent
alias without unlocking. It does not attach this mechanism to the existing
original fence, whose explicit-unlock destructor remains unchanged. A later
original-object join must prove that transfer rather than substitute a generic
descriptor or silently change an earlier validator.

The collector's success notice is necessary but insufficient for release. It
follows both pipe EOFs, bounded writes, fsync and explicit sink close. The
guardian additionally checks the actual successful child wait status, terminal
writer pidfds and EOF through its own readers. An unlisted pipe writer keeps
EOF false even when every known process has exited. Error, overflow or absolute
expiry instead produces a distinct failure notice and retains the fence;
disconnect or a missing notice does not grant retry or completion.

This private mechanism is not authenticated original-start or cgroup enrollment.
It cannot establish sole ownership of production sinks from arbitrary file
descriptors, revoke an unknown process tree, or keep a kernel flock after the
last guardian is itself killed. Original-object transfer, live authority and
cgroup checks, durable-history exclusion and external supervision remain
execution prerequisites. There is no product throughput or overhead claim.

The [isolated packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/autonomous-watchdog-20261017/README.md)
passes all twelve cases three times in a WSL debug build and on both normal GNU
release compilers on the server: 36 local and 72 server cases. In particular,
the collector really enters SIGSTOP; its guardian remains runnable, sends
SIGKILL at the selected absolute bound and keeps the fence in a refused state.
The hidden-writer case independently rejects the tempting shortcut of releasing
after known pidfds alone become terminal. All 200 static contracts pass with
original live validators and deadline origins unchanged. No installation,
supervisor interruption or product workload was needed for these kernel facts.

Final review also moved signal blocking before the outer fork. Blocking only
inside the child leaves a window for an inherited userspace handler to run.
The parent now restores its exact previous mask on success and fork failure;
a deterministic failure seam tests that restoration without exhausting host
process limits. The complete local and two-compiler server matrices were
repeated on this corrected source, with the first positive cohort retained
separately. Collector/guardian loops and original validation deadlines did not
change during that correction.

## A shared lock needs an explicit custody transition

The next [ownership experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-fence-custody-20261017/README.md)
uses the actual original common-lock type. Merely duplicating that descriptor
does not transfer protection: its original destructor explicitly unlocks the
shared open-file description. A new regression test first reproduced the defect
by dropping the original owner while retaining its duplicate. Both legacy entry
points should still be excluded; the independent lock acquisition instead
succeeded. That negative remains in the packet.

Removing explicit unlock globally would also change short-observation lifetime.
The isolated implementation instead adds a private, irreversible custody
transition. The unchanged original inspector brackets duplication, and only
successful completion selects close-only destruction. Ordinary owners still
explicitly unlock. The custody owner has no public descriptor or execution API;
dropping it first leaves the original owner healthy, and dropping the original
first leaves custody holding the same lock. A second transfer refuses rather
than mint another authority.

The corrected source passes four new units and ten existing original-fence
units. Its nonexecuting process holder passes three repeats of six cases in WSL
and on each GNU release compiler: 18 local and 36 server cases. The controls
cover both destruction orders, omitted and disconnected private ACK, repeat
refusal and actual holder SIGKILL. A separate structural test barrier follows
the optional ACK attempt; it is not substituted for an original start ACK.
Independent common-lock exclusion, exact retained Reserved bytes, pidfd
readiness and actual wait status are the oracles. All 201 static contracts pass,
with previous live inspector bodies and deadline origins unchanged.

This proves a narrow ownership rule, not an enrolled guardian. The method has
no production caller and still needs the typed original validation frame,
sink/writer transfer and parent alias closure before authenticated start.
Whole-cgroup revocation and durable-history exclusion remain essential: the
last-holder SIGKILL control demonstrates that the kernel itself releases flock
when its final owner dies. No standalone lock can replace that history or
external supervision. The server rehearsal changed neither installation nor
supervisor and ran no product workload; no throughput result follows.

## Compose ownership within the original validation frame

Custody alone does not connect a lock to the exact outputs it must protect.
The next experiment therefore joins the original sinks, pipe and unsent-message
aliases, signed material, original alarm and opaque common-fence custody in one
consuming owner. Neither a caller-provided descriptor nor a newly asserted time
can establish that relationship. Custody must come from the same acknowledged
Starting storage, checked through the unchanged live original chain.

The first composition was intentionally conservative: validate the already
prepared grouped owner twice around acquisition, then do the same on later
revalidation. Its healthy screen failed on both GNU compilers at the original
ten-second challenge age. Acquisition had completed; the added nested frames
made the subsequent healthy validation too late. The complete rejected source
and failures remain evidence. Increasing the challenge lifetime would hide the
composition cost by changing the safety contract, so this candidate was withdrawn.

The replacement does not remove an original predicate or modify the existing
grouped API. It consumes OriginalCollectorSinks directly and inserts custody
acquisition into that constructor's already approved full opening/closing frame.
Preparation authenticates the original chain, binds the fixed bundle and worker
projection, creates the unsent message and arms the original absolute alarm.
It then acquires opaque custody from its own storage and performs the full
closing original round. Custody identity and CLOEXEC checks surround the close.
Only a successful complete close can mark the owner ready.

There is a subtle final boundary: the last custody metadata read can itself
consume remaining time. The implementation therefore observes the same alarm
and unchanged causal-age predicate again after that IO. The challenge issue,
progress receipt, Starting and Reserved origins never move. Revalidation likewise
brackets the unchanged complete grouped frame with custody observations, rather
than appending another pair of full frames. Its expected authentication count
is the baseline's 34 for construction and 34 for revalidation. This is a checked
call-count invariant, not a throughput, latency or safety-threshold claim.

Ownership order is also part of the design. Original message and sink/pipe
writers are fields before custody, so their destruction precedes custody close.
A failure poisons the borrowed original chain and retains the refused owner,
including acquired custody; no retry can reconstruct authority. The healthy
oracle checks exact origins, unchanged retained records, common-lock contention,
closed sink descriptors and actual EOF after dropping the owner. Persistent
faults must fail for their own reason, not because an unrelated late clock check
happened to reject them.

The [join packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-custody-join-20261018/README.md)
keeps rejected and replacement sources separate. Its process harness selects
opening, custody-retained and returned-but-unacknowledged cuts, pins each owned
child with pidfd, checks real SIGKILL wait status and distinguishes normal return
from zero-exit omitted ACK. Two fresh inspectors must refuse retained history
after every case. This is a synthetic return protocol, not actual manager delivery.

The result remains narrower than execution permission. The type exports no
File, message, clone, send, start or completion capability and does not yet enroll
its objects in the independent guardian. Sole-writer descriptor transfer, parent
alias closure, authenticated original start, full-cgroup writer cessation,
durable completion and external guardian supervision still have to follow.
No isolated success can substitute for those boundaries or open product load.

Both GNU release compiler cohorts pass the declared join gates: six repeated
healthy controls, forty persistent refusals and thirty selected process cases.
Those cases include eighteen actual SIGKILLs, six normal returns, six zero-exit
omitted ACKs and sixty fresh inspector refusals. A separate healthy screen also
passes; 32 original-fence/storage units and three protocol/process units pass
per compiler, alongside eight API doc checks per compiler and 204 static
contracts. Independent final host guards preserve the same supervisor PID,
zero restarts and installed executable/receipt hashes, with no surviving fixture
executable. The negative composition remains negative; the corrected result is
an ownership and refusal proof under the original deadlines, not product
performance, full power-loss coverage or production admission.

## Descriptor identity does not establish exclusive ownership

The next original-object audit finds an important interface mismatch. The checked
original sinks are O_RDWR, while the isolated generic guardian accepts O_WRONLY.
Changing its matcher to accept both would establish only access mode, not trusted
origin. The private descriptor plan instead borrows the exact original custodied
owner. It records custody, original selected alarm, readers, sinks and all four
original pipe/message writer aliases. Neither guardian nor collector may inherit
those writable pipe aliases. The guardian's initial list includes the sinks only
so it can fork its collector, then shed its own aliases before releasing that
collector's barrier. That later production join is still a distinct operation.

The plan captures a draft inventory, runs the unchanged complete validation frame,
compares identities, flags and positions after the frame, and observes the existing
original deadline again. Revalidation repeats the full frame. It exposes no public
descriptor, send, start, custody release or completion. A borrowed FD number and
metadata snapshot are not an execution permit and cannot replace live authority.

Two different failures sharpen the experiment. The first healthy screen incorrectly
expected all six reported times to stay equal. Four are immutable origins, but the
latest validation observation and current BOOTTIME must advance. Correcting that
oracle keeps exact first-four equality and checks monotonic observations, without
changing a runtime input or deadline. The failed source and screen remain separate.

The second finding is a real new-boundary defect: an empty file can already have a
nonzero shared file-description offset. Two equal snapshots could preserve that
bad state. A regression using an owned empty O_RDWR file sought to offset 17 first
failed its rejection assertion. The new inventory now requires zero position
before capture as well as exact post-frame comparison; an original fixture also
injects the offset before plan creation. Neither the old sink inspector nor the
generic guardian is changed to obtain that result.

The [descriptor packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-descriptor-plan-20261018/README.md)
uses a separately gated raw holder to test the actual original descriptor lists.
Allocation and sorting precede fork, signal handlers are blocked before inheritance,
and the exact child is pinned before observation. The child closes everything
outside its explicit list and verifies that original writer aliases are gone.
Only then may the parent destroy its complete original owner. Independent common
lock contention and actual pipe EOF, followed by empty-sink fsync/close and terminal
wait status, establish the selected ownership boundary. A hidden writer produces
EAGAIN rather than EOF and must leave custody retained; later closure cannot
retroactively turn refusal into success.

That holder is not the production guardian, and its private ACK is not manager
delivery evidence. Barred original transfer, final live validation, authenticated
message delivery, parent alias closure in the correct order, full-cgroup writer
cessation and external supervision remain required. The experiment isolates
descriptor ownership without installing a release, stopping the stable supervisor
or using product load. It does not establish a performance gain or release admission.

Both GNU compiler cohorts pass the descriptor gates: six repeated healthy controls,
twenty construction/later refusals and twenty-four raw-holder cases. Twelve cases
observe actual EOF after parent alias closure; six exercise holder SIGKILL, and
six demonstrate sticky refusal with a hidden writer before separate owned
SIGKILL cleanup. Four new fast units and the 32-test original storage/fence subtree
pass per compiler, alongside two closed-API doc checks and 207 static contracts.
The corrected first screen passes too. Final host guards retain the same stable
supervisor PID, zero restarts and installed executable/receipt digests, with no
surviving fixture executable. These results establish selected original-object
inheritance and parent-closure facts, not the still-missing production process join.

## Fork does not preserve a validation result

The next boundary is temporal rather than structural. A correct descriptor plan
before fork says nothing about authority or file drift while the child is being
created. The [barrier experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/diagnostic-original-barrier-validation-20261018.md)
therefore pins and isolates the existing nonexecuting holder first, leaves it
blocked before any pipe read or sink synchronization, and runs the complete live
frame in the parent while all original aliases still exist. Identity comparison
and the original deadline probe close that frame. A separate pinned-child check
must then reject a process that died while those checks were running.

Only after these observations does a healthy fixture destroy the parent owner
and issue the private EOF command. Missing optional test ACK does not become
authenticated manager delivery: the structural barrier is only a test oracle.
Conversely, persistent trust, output, writer, message, alarm, custody or offset
drift must refuse without issuing that command. Repeated validation of a poisoned
owner cannot repair the refusal. Parent alias closure then leaves the barred
child holding the common fence until explicit owned fixture cleanup.

The selected SIGKILL cuts distinguish two cases that a successful pre-fork test
would conflate. If the child dies while the original parent owner still exists,
the common lock must stay busy. If that parent owner has already closed, killing
the final holder makes the kernel lock available. Neither outcome authorizes
replay: retained Starting history must still reject a fresh storage entry.
An EOF notice after empty-sink fsync is also not a published completion record.

These ordering checks prepare an actual process join; they do not replace it.
Production must keep the original unsent message until authenticated delivery,
bind guardian and collector to the same original objects, supervise the original
absolute alarm even while barred, revoke the complete writer tree and protect
the final guardian independently. The unchanged test holder deliberately lacks
that autonomous supervision. No production start permission follows from its
private command protocol, and no performance gain is inferred from fault tests.

The [completed packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-barrier-validation-20261018/README.md)
passes twelve repeated healthy controls, eighteen post-fork refusals and
twenty-four selected SIGKILL cuts across GNU Rust 1.94 and MSRV 1.88. Eighteen
additional kills are explicit refusal cleanup and are counted separately. Both
first screens, 32+4 local fast units per compiler and all 210 static contracts
pass. The supervisor, installed executable/receipt and original deadlines remain
unchanged. This establishes the selected order under real process loss, while
leaving production guardian enrollment and authenticated delivery as actual work.

## Autonomous custody cannot depend on the next parent check

A barred holder can prove descriptor inheritance without being a watchdog. The
earlier fixture waits for a private command and does not inspect its alarm while
waiting. The next [custody component](../testing/performance/0.74/diagnostic-original-barred-custody-plan-20261018.md)
therefore creates a private ordinary-build custodian that inherits only the
original fence, the same selected timer and a notice socket. It has no stream or
output writer. After isolation it observes that timer without parent validation,
never reads or rearms it, and keeps the fence after expiry or peer loss. Its
pending notice is not permission to send, collect or start.

The new process and its pidfd are created atomically with clone3. This removes
the interval in which parent code would know only a numerical child PID. Handler
blocking precedes creation; exact-mask restoration occurs only after an owned
pidfd exists. Cleanup never falls back to signalling a numeric PID. The production
wrapper retains an exclusive original-owner borrow until its child field drops;
normal cancellation is tested through an independently duplicated pidfd. That
cancellation is still not successful cessation of an active writer tree.

The first composition exposed another cost boundary. It validated the original
custody, created a separately validated descriptor plan, created the custodian
under another complete frame, then attempted later full revalidation. Both
compiler screens passed construction but refused that final frame with original
Causal(Time). The rejected binaries, full nine-file source capsule and screens
remain reproducible; its larger matrix was not run. Raising a timeout would have
changed the safety claim rather than fixed the composition.

The replacement removes the descriptor-plan construction layer, not checks inside
the complete frame. It captures the same private draft directly from the sealed
original owner, starts the output-incapable custodian, then closes with unchanged
full validation, exact identity comparison, child observation and original deadline
probes. Later revalidation repeats that complete frame. The raw kernel code is
unchanged between candidates. Both new first screens pass construction and later
validation with 34 authentication and signature calls each, under the same four
immutable origins. This is a validated composition boundary, not a throughput gain.

Collector transfer and authenticated delivery remain different responsibilities.
The parent still owns the original unsent message and sinks; there is no ordinary
detach or activation API. Future production execution must bind the real collector,
all writers and controller, supervise the final guardian independently and retain
durable history through uncertain acknowledgement and cleanup. A pending watchdog
with no output capability is useful preparation, not a completed production launch.

The [completed pending-custody packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-barred-custody-20261018/README.md)
passes six repeated controls, sixteen refusals and eighteen selected process
cases across both GNU compilers, with separate constructor-death and cleanup
counts. Both first screens, local 32+5 units per compiler and 213 static contracts
pass. Offline verification checks the full rejected source/input capsule, both
negative screens and the unchanged raw kernel body alongside the new evidence.
Final host checks retain the supervisor and installed digests and find no old/new
fixture process. None of these correctness results is a product throughput claim
or admission to execute an original worker.

## Process death and message loss need different observations

Normal owner destruction exercises Rust cleanup. SIGKILL does not. The next
[pending custody fault packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-custody-loss-20261018/README.md)
therefore places the sealed original preparation in its own libtest process and
kills that exact owner on either side of the closing validation frame. A separate
driver receives only the custodian pidfd over a credential-checked private socket.
It cannot accidentally keep the original fence or notice peer alive. Custody must
survive owner death and the original absolute bound; after the custodian itself
dies, retained durable history must still reject a fresh attempt. Kernel lock
availability and permission to replay are different observations.

Losing the pending P notice needs another distinction. Expired alone cannot tell
whether P was consumed and lost or the observer expired before reading it. The
strengthened fixture checks the first remaining ordered notice after refusal:
it must be exactly E, with the custodian still live. Because the unchanged child
sends P before E, a leftover P fails this control. The observation occurs only
after sticky refusal, under retained custody; its harness fail-safe grants no
new authority time, write permission or resource release.

The attempted syscall observer demonstrated why that distinction matters. Its
matched untraced control passed, but strace refused an upstream original Time
check before pending custody and produced no P observation. The failed trace and
its exact source/binary/script identities remain evidence, not a completed loss
test or a reason to enlarge the window. Reading the already-ordered failure notice
avoids adding a tracer to the live validation path.

Two earlier fixture failures likewise stayed separate from product conclusions.
One expected an unrefused owner after deliberate refusal; the other placed test
authority below a directory rejected by the existing strict direct-/tmp rule.
Fixing the fixture postcondition and giving authority its own private temporary
root preserved the original checks. Neither justified changing runtime authority,
validation predicates, deadlines or qualification thresholds.

These checks concern an output-incapable pending custodian. They do not establish
authenticated original send, collector transfer, active writer-tree revocation
or production completion. The next executable component must join the actual
original readers and sinks while start remains barred and the full live frame
and custody remain intact. No throughput improvement follows from these fault
results.

The final current/MSRV cohorts pass twelve selected owner-death scenarios using
twenty-four selected SIGKILL signals, six lost-P controls with first remaining E,
and both complete-frame healthy screens. All 216 static contracts, local 32+5
Rust units per compiler, six Python units and two private-descriptor compile-fail
doctests pass. Read-only postflight finds no fixture from any retained cohort
and preserves the supervisor, installed digests and frozen qualification input.
This closes the selected pending-only fault boundary, not production execution.

## A barred collector still holds writable capabilities

Joining the original streams and sinks adds a different responsibility. Even
before activation, an O_RDWR sink descriptor is a writable capability. Custody
must cover its lifetime, not merely the interval in which the collector is
expected to write. If the preparing owner and a separate custodian disappear,
the collector must not be left holding sinks behind an available fence.

The next private join therefore gives the barred collector an alias of the same
original fence and alarm, alongside the original two readers and two sinks. Its
seven-descriptor inventory includes its private notice endpoint but excludes all
four pair/message writers and every unrelated descriptor. The parent retains
the original unsent message and original objects: enrollment is not an exclusive
transfer or an authenticated delivery. The child has no activation command and
performs no stream read or sink write.

At original-alarm expiry, unexpected peer activity or peer loss, the child closes
the four I/O descriptors before its best-effort failure notice, then parks with
the fence still held. A failed close is a refusal, never evidence of quiescence.
Even successful closure does not grant completion or release authority. Ordinary
cancellation stops and reaps the collector while the original exclusive borrow
and separate custodian still exist.

The typed join prepares both children before one unchanged closing validation
frame. Construction and subsequent revalidation still perform all 34
authentication and signature calls, preserve the four original time origins and
recheck both process states and the original alarm. No extra recursively
validated descriptor-plan constructor is inserted. This preserves a verified
composition boundary; it is not a measured product speedup.

The [barred collector packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-barred-collector-20261018/README.md)
separates healthy controls, reason-specific refusals and selected child-process
faults. Those tests cannot stand in for the next two-child owner-SIGKILL and
lost-B matrix, authenticated original send/start or cessation of the entire
active writer tree. The installed supervisor and product admission stay outside
this component boundary.

Both current/MSRV cohorts passed: eight healthy controls, eighteen specific
refusals and eighteen selected child-process scenarios. Each process scenario
observed four closed I/O FDs, a fence still busy after exact custodian death and
retained-history refusal after exact collector death. All 219 static contracts
and the focused format/lint/check gates passed. Postflight preserved the installed
supervisor and frozen qualification input. This confirms the selected barred
enrollment/quarantine boundary, not actual owner death in the two-child topology
or a performance improvement.

## Custody after the original owner is killed

Normal cancellation proves an order of destructors; it cannot prove what survives
SIGKILL. The two-child topology needs its own owner-death experiment. The external
driver receives only atomically created collector and custodian pidfds, in fixed
role order, from the fixture's kernel-authenticated sender. It receives no fence,
stream, sink or private notice endpoint. That restriction matters: an observer
holding an original lock alias could manufacture retention, while a peer alias
could hide the owner disconnect that should quarantine the collector's I/O.

The [two-child owner-loss packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-collector-loss-20261018/README.md)
places the kill on either side of the unchanged closing frame. Before it, the
barred children exist but the joint frame has not authorized the prepared owner;
after it, the fixture has asserted all 34 authentication and signature calls.
In either case, losing the real owner must leave both children alive and cause
the collector to close its four I/O FDs autonomously. Killing either child first
must leave the other holding the fence past the original bound. Kernel lock
availability after both die still cannot authorize replay of retained history.

Lost B is a separate observation. The test consumes the actual initial B and
lets the unchanged observer expire on the original alarm. Its first remaining
ordered notice must be E while the children retain custody; a leftover B is a
failed loss experiment. Parser units additionally reject malformed, duplicate,
empty and oversized notices and establish precedence of expiry or terminal
readiness over queued B. Their synthetic readiness FDs test parsing, not process
identity; the owner-death matrix uses real atomic pidfds.

The fixture protocol also needs resource-safe refusal. Its receiver collects all
SCM_RIGHTS descriptors before validating other ancillary fields, so an unknown
field before the rights cannot leak later received FDs. Strict credentials,
role/identity checks, duplicate-field rejection and matched-image checks precede
any selected child signal. All changes remain test-only; the ordinary join,
raw child, original validators and time bounds stay unchanged. These are barred
failure proofs, not authenticated activation or cessation of active writers.

The first matrix stopped at the MSRV healthy prerequisite. Rust 1.94 completed
twelve owner-death scenarios and three lost-B controls, but Rust 1.88 refused
Original(Challenge(Time)) on revalidation after all 34 authentication/signature
calls. Its trace's zero time-refusal counter did not mean no refusal occurred:
that counter does not cover the direct challenge-age guard. Error provenance
and instrumentation coverage must be read together.

A separately retained ABBA diagnostic then ran only the unchanged healthy test
on previous/current/current/previous MSRV images. Statuses were 101/0/0/0; the
previous image also hit the same challenge-age boundary. This demonstrates an
existing unstable healthy boundary, not an attributed compiler or filesystem
regression. The later green observations cannot turn the interrupted matrix
green. The new fault candidate is withdrawn and fully recoverable from its
source capsule; only the independent parser units are accepted. The next
optimization question is preparation cost within the original window, not a
larger window. Grouping custody and barred enrollment changes intermediate
observation frequency, so the subsequent experiment required explicit agreement.

The independent [parser-only packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-collector-notices-20261018/README.md)
passes eight descriptor/notice units per compiler and 221 static contracts,
with the complete ordinary kernel and join frozen. It does not close the
interrupted owner-fault gate.

## Grouping preparation without renewing its deadline

The approved [custody and enrollment experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-enrollment-frame-20261018/README.md)
targets repeated observation rather than an expensive cryptographic primitive.
The old path closes a full custody frame, then opens and closes another full
frame around barred enrollment. The new private path moves both nonexecuting
child enrollments between the first opening and closing observations. Healthy
controls assert 34 authentication calls and 34 signature calls at construction
instead of 68 of each across the sequential path; later revalidation
independently asserts 34 of each.
That count reduction is established, but it is not a throughput, allocation or
wall-time speedup claim for HydraCache product APIs.

Ownership is part of the hypothesis. An owner containing a borrowed join into
itself would create a self-reference. Instead, the new type owns original
preparation and both children directly. Collector/custodian cancellation
attempts precede destruction of original writers and the last custody alias.
Failure retains that complete refused object. Neither the independent generic
O_WRONLY watchdog nor the old original constructors/validators/raw children
changes. The new composition reuses the exact original inventory and checks
custody, both child states/notices, alarm and challenge age around closing.
Readiness is last; P and B remain isolation notices, not execution authority.

The fresh current/MSRV cohorts complete eight healthy controls, eighteen live
refusals, six actual lost-B controls and twenty-four owning-process SIGKILL
scenarios. Either child can die first, on either side of closing, without
releasing the fence while the other survives past the original bound. Owner
disconnect autonomously removes four collector I/O FDs; after both children die,
retained history still refuses admission. All original origins and limits stay
fixed, and the installed supervisor is unchanged. The first stopped matrix and
its ABBA attribution remain separate negative evidence, not a retroactive pass.

This accepts a selected barred composition, not active execution. Another slow
host observation can still legitimately refuse the unchanged deadline. Before
product work can start, authenticated original delivery/start, whole-writer
enrollment and cessation, external active supervision and durable completion
still need their own producers and fault proofs. Fewer redundant observations
are useful only while those live authority checks remain real.

## A job reply cannot prove a safe start or finish

Before connecting original delivery, the [one-shot exchange experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/dispatch-exchange-20261018/README.md)
isolates message mechanics from execution authority. An unsent message is not
a trusted manager channel. In particular, sending the old original message to
systemd's well-known name would not pin the unique owner observed earlier. The
future trusted channel must construct a uniquely addressed original message
inside the complete live frame. The old original preparation stays unchanged
and deliberately unsent throughout this experiment.

The private owner consumes a supplied FD-bearing message and retains it even
when preparation refuses. It checks the bounded request shape and distinct
blocking CLOEXEC FIFO writers, then marks the outcome Uncertain before any
transport side effect could occur. Exactly one reply can be considered: original
serial, selected manager sender and client destination must agree, with no
unexpected headers, flags or returned FDs. A canonical systemd job path is only
observation data. These checks do not authenticate the name claims, signed unit
settings, original ancestry or an actual system-bus connection.

Lost acknowledgement is not evidence that the request was not delivered. The
local socket fixture transfers the real rights, drops the peer without a reply
and explicitly closes the reply window. Ownership of the writers survives;
neither retry nor release is authorized. A separate late-reply test sends a
correct response after that closure and still requires sticky refusal. The
component has no transport timeout implementation; the future bounded driver
must close the window on timeout, disconnect or error without renewing any
original lease. Error payloads also stay out of diagnostics.

The most useful counterexample concerns aliases. A test clones the zbus Message
before preparation, obtains a valid job observation and destroys the exchange.
Both pipe readers still report WouldBlock: the hidden clone holds the same
writers. Only destroying the final clone yields EOF. A job reply and a local
Drop therefore cannot justify fence release, all-writer cessation or completion.
The future active watchdog and writer-tree revocation need their own proofs.

The first implementation exposed an ordinary representation error before any
integration: four tests passed and six refused because the signature comparison
omitted the outer tuple parentheses used by zbus. The existing original message
test already documented that representation. The negative result and logic
snapshot are retained; fixing the literal did not increase a deadline or loosen
the acceptance contract. Intermediate twelve-test results remain development
logs. The final source passes fourteen tests on each GNU compiler, including two
real SCM_RIGHTS socket cases, followed by descriptor/storage controls, compile-
fail tests, strict checks and source-freeze/mutation contracts.

Those socket peers are in the same test process. Kernel credentials and FD
identities are real, but they do not prove PID 1 or production D-Bus authentication.
Received bytes must equal the complete known-valid zbus-built message before
the test's unsafe decoder is entered; it is not an untrusted wire decoder.
No original process starts, no server operation runs and no throughput,
allocation, CPU or wall-time gain is claimed. This accepts isolated reply and
ownership mechanics while keeping authenticated delivery, active supervision,
whole-writer cessation and durable completion visibly unfinished.

Evidence verification also catches harness drift. The old descriptor filter
started selecting the newly nested exchange tests as well: twenty-two passed,
but that did not match the declared eight-control row. The packet verifier
refused it. Excluding exchange tests from that filter while requiring their own
fourteen-test run restores the intended two inventories without relaxing any
runtime predicate. Review then adds oversized/wrong-type/extra-FD request and
missing-CLOEXEC controls in a separate test-only commit. Both compiler cohorts
and all 229 source contracts pass again on that reviewed source. The old broad
filter run and its verification refusal remain evidence, not discarded noise.

## Keeping a live manager channel instead of trusting a snapshot

A helper that observes a manager and then closes its connection cannot supply
the channel for later original delivery. The [fixed channel experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/manager-channel-20261018/README.md)
therefore owns a separate current-thread runtime and live connection. It opens
only the root-selected system-bus socket, retains nonsymlink ancestry and binds
the actual peer with SO_PEERCRED and atomic SO_PEERPIDFD. Opening a pidfd later
from an observed reusable foreign PID would leave an identity gap.

Numeric UID 0/PID 1 also needs a namespace interpretation. Retained procfs/nsfs
objects require the caller, original bus peer and PID 1 to share PID/user
namespaces, with original pidfd liveness around proc lookups. The caller's time
namespace and kernel boot are retained as well. Missing access refuses rather
than turning the numeric reply into authority. Local tests deliberately separate
the nonroot access refusal from a root read-only positive case; the latter runs
only that exact test, not privileged fault fixtures or service operations.

The first real-bus positive stopped at Reply after the ordinary units and
nonroot control passed. Its source, images and partial cohort remain frozen.
Separate test-only tracing found METHOD_RETURN with flags=1 and all other
envelope checks matching. The [D-Bus specification](https://dbus.freedesktop.org/doc/dbus-specification.html#message-protocol-header-encoding)
makes NO_REPLY_EXPECTED irrelevant on replies. The 5.19 builder helper rejected
that flag on synthetic replies, so its convenient defaults had hidden the real
wire form. Safe typed Header/Builder construction now tests both supported
forms without an unsafe byte decoder. Only the new read-only producer changes;
the old exchange and request predicates stay frozen for their own later review.

A fresh two-compiler cohort then passes the namespace refusal, root fixed-bus
positive and sticky failure after closing its own client connection, plus the
unit/regression controls. The whole connect/authenticate/Hello/query observation
shares one absolute BOOTTIME two-second alarm, not a new timeout per query. The
alarm counter is not consumed, and a post-work clock check refuses a late result.
This observation cap does not renew the original reservation, cell, challenge
or progress window.

The accepted object is still not original launch authority. Its selected kernel
view must join the original admitted host, signed material and full validation
frame before uniquely addressed message construction and delivery. Connection
ownership alone does not prove Unix-FD negotiation, unit/cgroup identity, active
supervision or writer cessation. The gain here is a concrete trusted input
producer and a corrected interoperability assumption, not a measured product
throughput or allocation improvement. Installation and product admission remain
closed until those consuming boundaries are proved.

## Keep process management in systemd

A disconnected SSH client is not a reason to invent another process manager.
systemd already owns detached service lifetime, cgroups, resource limits and
stop policy. Both of our workload unit builders already select Restart=no and
KillMode=control-group. The [ownership audit](../testing/performance/0.74/supervisor-boundary-audit-20261018.md)
therefore keeps these mechanisms in systemd. A reconnecting observer should
retrieve current state, not start another execution or reconstruct a process
from checkpoints.

The experiment-specific responsibility is narrower but different. A service
being active does not prove useful progress; a matching unit name does not prove
the original executable, streams or process generation. A successful start-job
reply does not prove that every inherited writer has stopped. The hidden message
alias test demonstrates why: dropping the exchange owner still leaves a pipe
open until its final alias disappears. An empty workload cgroup cannot by itself
account for an alias retained outside that cgroup.

This distinction also limits the watchdog. systemd can detect missing service
notifications and stop a unit. Our controller must separately interpret useful
progress, enforce the original execution authority and retain an uncertain
outcome until cessation is established. A GitHub observer loss may leave a
healthy original process running; expiry of execution authority may not. Neither
event authorizes a transparent restart of measured work.

The audit consequently retains the integrity and admission checks rather than
adding a scheduler or a dashboard to the critical execution path. A monitoring
adapter can remain replaceable and separately budgeted. The immediate code
boundary is the old exchange's reply interoperability, followed by its consuming
join with the original live manager channel. The remaining lifecycle, all-writer
revocation, reconnect and exact-host enrollment gates are still required.

The [next isolated exchange experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/exchange-reply-flags-20261018/README.md)
then applies the already attributed protocol fact to the old one-shot exchange.
The fourteen old units pass on both compiler cohorts. A new typed positive fails
on flags=1 before the correction, exposing the same invalid assumption without
starting any service. The candidate permits 0/NO_REPLY_EXPECTED only on a required
METHOD_RETURN. Exhaustive known-bit combinations and crossed correlation/body/FD
refusals keep request flags, manager errors, uncertainty and no-retry behavior
unchanged. Nineteen exchange tests per compiler and the complete local source
contract suite pass after the correction.

The first exact-source comparison also failed because its new restoration string
did not match rustfmt's line wrapping. That negative is retained separately; the
repair changes the reference string, not the runtime rule. This is a useful
boundary for the conclusion: one interoperability obstacle is removed, but a
passing reply still proves neither actual original process start nor cessation
of every writer. No throughput, CPU or allocation improvement follows from this
correctness result.

## A live connection must retain its original authority

The [next manager-join experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-manager-join-20261018/README.md)
addresses a correctness gap, not a throughput hypothesis. A verified connection
and a verified original frame are not interchangeable snapshots. The connection
must stay owned with the exact frame that admitted the attempt, and its kernel
view must match the original receiver rather than a newly supplied context.

The consuming join therefore retains the original frame and clones only its
actual retained kernel Origin into an opaque context binding. Typed nsfs objects
for user, mount, PID and time namespaces, plus boot identity, connect that binding
to the fixed live channel. Sender/hold checks guard derivation. Later validation
places live channel/context observations around the unchanged full frame and
original deadline observations. There is no cached policy or signature result:
the frame still performs 34 authentication and 34 signature checks. No original
origin, alarm or 300/60/10-second admission window is refreshed.

The tests deliberately separate two claims. A distinct test-only channel
exercises healthy composition and faults against the real original frame; it
cannot construct the production owner. A separate local root read-only case
checks actual fixed-bus/receiver context and closed-channel refusal without
launching a child or enrolling trust. Neither alone establishes a positive
production-enrolled full join or original message/FD delivery.

Negative results determine the scope. The first local fixture cohort stops
before the new join at the unchanged Challenge(Time) check; a later old-frame
screen passes but cannot explain or heal that historical failure. The first
host launcher creates group-writable fixture directories under default umask
0002, correctly refused by the old trust reader. Only the harness is corrected
to private umask 077. A second host cohort reaches the intended fixed-channel
refusal, but its new test wrongly expects the original owner not to be poisoned.
Correcting that test expectation changes no runtime predicate or deadline.
Each stopped cohort remains separate from any later scoped passing gate.

This work yields an owning, fail-closed boundary, not a numerical speed claim.
Unique-owner original-message addressing and FD delivery remain next. Active
watchdog supervision must then account for every writer before completion or
fence release; disconnect/reattach and real host enrollment still need their own
end-to-end evidence. The stable installed supervisor is not modified by these
isolated temporary-directory fixtures.

The fresh host gate subsequently completes on both compilers: six healthy
controls, twenty live refusals and two actual nonroot fixed-channel refusals in
total. Both distinct local read-only channel/context gates pass, as do 238
source contracts and 44 portable controls. These results support the narrow
owning-composition boundary while preserving the unresolved local timing result.
They do not establish production enrollment, active execution or a product
performance improvement.

## Added validation can exhaust the original deadline

A unique manager name is meaningful only on the live connection that verified
it. The [withdrawn message-owner candidate](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-manager-message-20261018/README.md)
therefore consumed the original manager/frame join rather than accepting a name
or an arbitrary prepared message. It keeps the old well-known-addressed message
unsent, preserving its checks and descriptor inventory. The new envelope uses
the held manager's unique name, while body bytes and serial remain exactly those
of the original canonical message. Typed descriptor checks bind the new stdout
and stderr aliases to their original pipe objects, not just two valid FD numbers.

Adding a message also adds two writers. Their ownership and destruction order
matter: extra aliases must close before the original owner's final custody alias.
The new type exposes no message, FD, connection, retry or send operation. A
missing/replaced message, altered manager/client binding or descriptor drift
poisons the same retained owner. The old signed property validator is reused;
byte equality checks the complete encoded canonical body rather than a selected
subset of properties.

Preparation and later validation each perform the unchanged full manager/frame
round both before and after the payload checks. That is 68 authentication and 68
signature calls, not an optimization claim. Original origins, absolute alarms and
300/60/10-second windows remain. If this added work cannot fit a healthy gate,
the result must remain a refusal; a deadline increase is not an acceptable fix.

The test-only SCM_RIGHTS transfer sits inside those opening/closing full rounds
and reuses the existing owned credential/rights receiver. This can establish
that the exact encoded message and both original writers cross a real local
socket. It cannot establish negotiated Unix-FD delivery to the production bus,
systemd authority or execution. Separating these claims prevents a mechanical
transport success from silently becoming original-start permission.

The selected experiment fails its timing contract. On the first host case,
preparation completes but the subsequent validation refuses Causal(Time); later
cases and the MSRV host matrix do not run. The new-path delivery claim therefore
remains unproved. One separate diagnostic, with runtime checks unchanged, records
challenge age 9.301862561 s before the new round and 9.976507282 s after 68
authentication/signature checks. The next call refuses at 10.116451429 s after
17 checks. The first round's observed wall cost is 674639851 ns; this single
diagnostic is attribution, not a product performance estimate.

The useful finding is that most of the immutable challenge window is already
consumed before this boundary. Adding complete traversals can be semantically
conservative yet make the preparation unusable. We preserve the failed sources
and withdraw that runtime candidate, leaving the approved manager/frame join
intact. A future experiment may place only nonexecuting message preparation
inside the existing complete frame with all original predicates and bounds;
that is a changed observation boundary requiring explicit agreement. Extending
the deadline or resetting the original challenge would invalidate the test.

### One full frame can contain pure message preparation

The next [separately agreed experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-manager-grouped-message-20261018/README.md)
tests a narrower hypothesis: place only nonexecuting manager/message preparation
inside the existing complete validation round. It consumes the original frame
directly rather than constructing a fully validated join and adding another
complete preparation boundary. The old join and all original predicate bodies
remain unchanged under source-equivalence guards.

Original observations and the first live channel/context check precede message
preparation. The retained canonical body, serial and original stdout/stderr
objects are checked, followed by one complete original frame. A second live
channel/context check, payload inspection and original observation close the
round. Every original live predicate remains, but the rejected prototype's
duplicate complete traversal is gone. This change is appropriate only for pure
preparation while children remain barred; it does not justify moving a send,
start or durable side effect outside its required guard.

The new owner retains both additional message writer aliases and closes them
before original custody can drop. Any error poisons the same original owner;
missing payloads cannot reconstruct, and no message, FD, connection, retry or
send API is exposed. Original origins, alarm objects and 300/60/10-second bounds
stay exact. The old negative timing cohort is preserved rather than relabeled.

The fresh GNU current/MSRV host gate passes six healthy scenarios and twelve
full rounds, each with 34 authentication calls, 34 signature calls and two
channel/context checks. Six test-only socket transfers carry the exact addressed
message and original writers before closing full validation. Forty mutation,
live-context, child-loss and expiry cases refuse permanently; two real nonroot
fixed-channel constructor refusals retain the original owner. The test probe
cannot construct a production owner, and socket transfer is not negotiated
system-bus delivery or authenticated start.

The BOOTTIME observation deltas of the twelve healthy rounds are 335723919 to
339133566 ns. Maximum successful challenge age is 9974721890 ns, leaving only
25278110 ns, about 25 ms, before the original bound. These are fixture
observations, not product performance estimates or a worst-case safety margin.
The grouping makes this gate usable, but the already consumed preparation
budget remains a critical-path risk before actual dispatch. Further work must
attribute that budget and prove real FD negotiation, one-shot correlation,
original process identity and active all-writer cessation without extending
the deadline. Completion, later cells and reconnect cannot inherit authority
from this nonexecuting success.

### The remaining budget is spent before the manager message

The [next diagnostic](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-preparation-budget-20261018/README.md)
keeps every runtime body and observation boundary unchanged. It copies the
existing fixture orchestration with test-only numeric stage markers; a source
guard must recover the original helper exactly after removing those insertions.
Three fresh scenarios on each GNU compiler follow the same original challenge
through response, consent, output preparation, enrollment and both manager
rounds. Printing is deferred until after the measured path and owned cleanup.

The largest observed bucket is joined outputs: 7.185–7.222 seconds with 782 IPC
authentications in every scenario. Response acceptance takes about 0.542–0.547
seconds, consent preparation 0.590–0.595, consent acceptance 0.308–0.311 and
enrollment 0.362–0.366. Prechallenge reservation is outside the issued window.
Challenge creation also includes pre-issue work: challenge-ready age is only
about 0.268–0.270 seconds, so charging that function's entire duration to the
10-second window would be incorrect. At outputs-ready, the original challenge
is already about 8.90–8.94 seconds old. Maximum final age is 9.975645201 seconds,
leaving about 24 ms. These are scoped fixture observations, not product
performance estimates or a worst-case guarantee.

The output source explains the repeated count: nineteen single eight-step
traversals around durable Starting publication, six through pipe preparation
and twenty-one through sink preparation. Each traversal performs seventeen
authentications, producing 46 × 17 = 782. The number is not itself proof of
redundancy. Those traversals surround distinct effects and checkpoints; reusing
an earlier success across them would change the safety contract.

The measured IPC authentication spans inside that bucket total only
25.938–28.319 ms. Request-signature spans, included in authentication, total
21.804–24.327 ms. They do not cover every cryptographic operation. Subtracting
them from seven seconds would not establish filesystem cost or CPU residency.
Together with the separately scoped component and syscall controls, the result
points toward repeated original worker/kernel/authority walks as the next
attribution target, rather than assuming immutable signature verification is
expensive. No optimization or speedup is accepted from that inference.

All six scenarios preserve the original origins, journal bytes, child FD
inventory, fence and deadlines. Twelve nested manager rounds still perform
34 authentication/signature calls and two context checks each. The actual
system-bus delivery/start, active all-writer cessation, completion and reconnect
gates remain separate. The next change must reduce the cost of a live traversal
without dropping the effect-local brackets, caching mutable authority/context
or extending the original deadline.

### Kernel context dominates the measured live worker walk

The [nested worker diagnostic](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-live-walk-20261018/README.md)
tests that inference on the actual retained validator. Six test-only entry
spans distinguish the worker wrapper, policy, trust source, active authority,
kernel context and local context. Removing the exact insertions must restore
every pre-existing Rust file; the validator is not reproduced as an alternative
implementation. The experiment runs before reservation and challenge issuance,
so its instrumentation cannot consume or renew the ten-second progress window.

Three fresh fixtures per GNU compiler each perform 32 consecutive worker
validations, with full original OIDC validation before and after. All six
fixtures pass without retries; original request and worker/OIDC bytes remain
unchanged and the IPC authentication/signature counters are zero. There are
192 observations, but only six independent fixtures. No output or execution is
created.

The observed whole-worker wall span is 1.490–1.504 ms. Its two kernel-context
calls contribute 1.023–1.033 ms, about 69 percent. The local-context call
contributes 0.211–0.215 ms, while the two worker-policy calls together contribute
about 0.255–0.256 ms. Four active-authority inspections inside that policy cost
about 0.174–0.175 ms, roughly 12 percent of the whole worker span. Four trust
source checks contribute about 0.076 ms inside the same policy span.

Unlike the earlier independent component controls, these measurements are
nested in one real call tree. The numeric tracer accounts for time outside
instrumented direct children, and the verifier checks the parent/child
arithmetic exactly. This prevents adding the policy and its children twice.
That outside-children time still is not exclusive CPU, filesystem or allocation
cost: each span is instrumented wall time and includes uninstrumented work.

The result narrows the next hypothesis, not the server admission boundary.
Profile sender liveness/status, retained origin/namespace/boot walks and clock
sampling inside kernel context before selecting a change. Do not optimize
authority signatures merely because the preparation path repeats authentication,
or reuse mutable observations across an effect. These controls do not decompose
the entire earlier 7.2-second join and establish no speedup or worst-case margin.
The roughly 24 ms observed challenge margin, real authenticated bus start,
all-writer cessation, completion and reconnect remain unresolved.

### Origin walks explain most of the kernel context span

The [kernel call-tree diagnostic](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-kernel-walk-20261018/README.md)
adds ten test-only entry spans and records thirteen direct parent/child edges.
It runs the same retained worker validator before reservation, preserving all
live checks, effect boundaries and original deadlines. All 351 old Rust files
must be recoverable exactly after removing the instrumentation. Six fresh
current/MSRV fixtures pass on first execution, producing 192 worker validations
and 174 checked numeric rows.

One worker validation contains sixteen origin traversals, thirty-two boot
document reads, sixty-four named namespace observations and forty-eight bounded
proc reads. The two packet-context checks together take 1.010–1.017 ms in this
instrumented cohort. Origin's nested inclusive span contributes 0.833–0.836 ms,
82.2–82.5 percent of packet context. The verifier checks incoming node counts
and times, each parent's direct-child accounting and an exact partition of
packet context into outside-children spans. It does not add nested totals.

The disjoint partition places roughly 29 percent in boot-document code outside
its bounded-reader child, 25 percent in named namespace observations, 19 percent
in origin code outside its children and 15 percent in bounded proc reads. The
remaining spans cover sender checks, projection parsing and the surrounding
joins. These are wall-scope contributions, not exclusive CPU or syscall costs.
Destruction of returned files, strings and Vec buffers can occur in the parent
scope, so its remaining time is not simply metadata work.

Time sampling illustrates why nesting matters. Its inclusive contribution is
about 0.208–0.209 ms, but it brackets the clocks with two full origin traversals.
Only 0.000351–0.000420 ms remains outside those children, including clock calls,
string creation and tracer overhead. Weakening clock validation would target
the wrong measured cost as well as change the safety contract.

At that baseline, the bounded reader creates a 65537-byte zeroed Vec even for the
canonical 37-byte boot document. Its timer includes creation, positional read
and truncation, but not the returned Vec's later destruction. This identifies
a concrete small-buffer allocation hypothesis, not a measured allocation win.
The next isolated experiment must first prove equivalent accepted documents and
fail-closed short/EINTR/oversized behavior, preserve single-read and all live
observation semantics, measure allocations and wall time separately, and then
repeat the unchanged full preparation gate. No mutable boot, namespace, sender,
time or authority result may be cached across an effect.

These new timings are not an uninstrumented A/B comparison with the previous
cohort and do not decompose the entire earlier preparation bucket. No speedup
is accepted. The original challenge-margin risk, authenticated bus start,
all-writer cessation, completion and same-attempt reconnect remain open.

### A fixed boot document does not need the generic heap buffer

The [isolated boot-buffer candidate](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/boot-buffer-20261018/README.md)
targets one allocation rather than reducing the frequency of safety checks.
A canonical boot ID occupies 37 bytes including its newline. A 38-byte stack
buffer therefore holds the valid document and one byte that detects an
overlength read. The candidate still opens and checks the same procfs objects,
performs one positional read, closes the document before decoding, and applies
the same lowercase UUID predicate. It never retries a short read or EINTR.
Status and pidfd documents retain the generic bounded reader.

The semantic controls compare the actual reader and decoder with the old
algorithm across 9,472 single-byte mutations, 1,024 seeded documents, empty and
overlength inputs, every short prefix and injected I/O errors. A trailing byte
refuses when observed. Neither implementation proves EOF when a short read
returns only the canonical prefix. For oversized malformed input, the smaller
buffer can change the test-only refusal site from the document budget to boot
syntax; both still return the same public invalid result. Treating those
diagnostic labels as identical would overstate the equivalence proof.

Allocation counting runs in a separate integration image, not in the
supervisor or the plain timing image. Windows and both GNU compilers each run
five counterbalanced scopes of 32 identical reads. The old temporary reader
per scope makes 32 allocations and requests 2,097,184 bytes; the new one makes
zero temporary-reader allocations. The test destroys returned storage before
leaving the counted scope and checks thread isolation, panic restoration and
refusal of nested capture. An old-buffer control first fails both the width
and allocation assertions, so the test distinguishes the proposed change.

This proves a narrow allocation reduction, not a whole-worker allocation total
or a throughput gain. The returned boot String and path allocations remain.
Requested allocation bytes are not copied bytes or RSS. That local packet alone
kept the runtime candidate experimental pending plain matched original-worker
timing and the full preparation healthy/fault gate at the original deadlines. All live
observations and 46 effect brackets remain required; the earlier challenge
margin is not enlarged by source inspection or by this allocation result.

### Plain worker pairs confirm a smaller validation cost

The [next gate](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/boot-buffer-plain-20261018/README.md)
separates that allocation observation from elapsed-time evidence. Baseline and
candidate use identical GNU libtest harnesses and source paths; only the old
versus fixed-buffer boot function differs. All 367 selected inputs agree
within each role. Existing tracing hooks remain inactive, and the counting
allocator is absent. Each fresh fixture times 128 actual retained worker
validations, with full original checks before and after the loop.

Five independently started pairs per compiler run in alternating AB/BA order.
The paired geometric mean candidate/baseline wall ratio is 0.95153 for GNU
1.94.0 and 0.95820 for MSRV 1.88.0: about 4.85 and 4.18 percent lower whole-worker
wall cost. Their preregistered two-sided 95-percent log-ratio Student intervals
are 0.94119–0.96199 and 0.94156–0.97513. Both clear the frozen one-percent
lower-cost criterion and non-regression check. The 2,560 calls are not 2,560
independent samples: the estimator has five pairs per compiler and assumes
approximately normal paired log ratios. These are batch-average validation
observations on one host, not CPU/op, tail latency or cache API throughput.

The mechanism preserves observation frequency. Six subsequent healthy
preparation fixtures pass twelve complete message rounds; forty live refusal
scenarios remain sticky, six same-process rights transfers retain the original
writers, and two real nonroot fixed-channel refusals preserve the owner/fence.
The 46 effect brackets and original 300/60/10-second origins remain unchanged.
All tests pass on first dispatch. This accepts the small buffer for the
nonexecuting preparation path at source `8e7e5da1`.

The maximum successful recorded challenge age is 9.548534663 seconds, leaving
about 451 ms of the original ten-second window. That is an observation across

to weaken the next effect's checks. Real negotiated bus FD delivery and start,
