### Negotiated delivery does not establish descriptor custody

The [private bus component gate](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/negotiated-dispatch-20261018/README.md)
adds an important boundary between preparation and execution. The earlier
socket fixture transferred SCM_RIGHTS directly and explicitly requested
MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC on receipt. It could not establish that the selected D-Bus
library negotiated rights or received them with the same descriptor flags.
The new fixture uses an owned nonroot dbus-daemon and real EXTERNAL, Hello and
Unix-FD negotiation. Its peer PID, UID and GID match the exact owned daemon;
its manager role is only another same-user connection, not systemd.

That distinction exposes a real difference. The pinned zbus 5.19 Unix reader
uses recvmsg without MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC. The new bare-reader control observes
FD_CLOEXEC zero after delivery, while the original sender descriptors remain
CLOEXEC. The existing strict writer-shape check correctly refuses the received
aliases. CLOEXEC is local to a descriptor table entry; successful transmission
does not preserve that bit in a newly received descriptor.

The response is not to relax the writer check or repair the bit after receipt.
Positive fixture cases use a separate test-only receiver requesting
MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC atomically. Its units exercise two rights, excess rights and
actual ancillary truncation with 253 sent descriptors. All installed aliases
must close on rejection, independently confirmed by pipe EOF after the original
writers close. WouldBlock, disconnect and unexpected kernel credentials have
separate controls. This establishes the fixture receiver's behavior, not the
production systemd receiver or the fixed-channel library's default behavior.

The full local matrix passes nine cases on both GNU compilers. Forced 17-byte
fragments attach rights only once; the received body, serial, pipe identities,
descriptor order and flags remain exact. Lost or delayed acknowledgement,
foreign actual sender, wrong serial, disconnect and manager error cannot reopen
the existing one-shot exchange. The private fault bus deliberately allows
unsolicited replies so malformed responses reach that classifier. Its earlier
default-policy rejection is retained separately; no installed bus policy changes.

The strongest result is a counterexample to premature completion. After the
exchange and both connections close, the received Message still writes into
the original pipes. Only dropping that last Message produces EOF. A valid job
reply, connection closure or sender destruction is therefore not whole-writer
cessation. Future execution must retain custody and the fence until every
writer is demonstrably quiescent.

Three stopped cohorts remain visible: unsafe default fixture-directory mode,
the stock reader's descriptor flags and a bus policy that prevented the intended
fault input from reaching the classifier. A later lint-only predicate spelling
change receives rebuilt images and repeated controls rather than being silently
folded into earlier image identities. No cache API performance is measured in
this package. Authenticated original-owner delivery, executable/streams/process/
cgroup binding, active all-writer cessation and new execution-boundary SIGKILL,
completion and reconnect checks remain open at the original admission deadlines.

### Separate reply correlation from request custody

Connecting an existing exchange to the original message owner should not require
cloning its FD-bearing Message or removing it from the live frame. The
[correlation prerequisite](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/reply-state-owner-20261018/README.md)
therefore separates the old state machine from request ownership. ReplyState
contains only names, original serial, phase and reply latch. The owning exchange
still retains the same Message and delegates to that state; it acquires no new
writer aliases. The request predicates and complete old transition/reply block
remain unchanged, with byte-level source restoration and mutation controls.

The new tests make the distinction explicit. A standalone state retains no pipe
writer: after request destruction its readers reach EOF, yet it can still
classify valid reply data. Correlation alone is therefore not custody or start
authority. The owning exchange, in contrast, keeps its original writers through
job observation until the Message itself drops.

An independent phase/latch model checks both representations over 512 seeded
histories and 17,150 operations on each GNU compiler, including early replies,
lost acknowledgement, duplicate operations and manager errors. Both return the
same six outcome counts. Existing dispatch regressions and the nine-case actual
private-bus matrix also pass. These checks establish behavior preservation, not
a speedup or independent process-crash coverage.

The original full frame and fixed channel are deliberately unchanged in this
prerequisite. Their next integration can retain correlation without a second
request owner, but must still perform all live checks at the original deadlines.
Neither the refactor nor its tests open real send/start, prove whole-writer
cessation, or permit completion and fence release.

### Bind prepared correlation inside the original frame

The next integration keeps ReplyState beside the original addressed Message,
not in another exchange owning a clone. A private preparation-only wrapper
borrows that Message and exposes only prepare and check. Its check requires
the original serial and retained manager/client names, Prepared phase and a
closed reply latch, then repeats the existing request and live writer-shape
checks. There is no arm, reply-observation, Message getter or transport callback
at this boundary.

The original payload checks the wrapper before and after its existing complete
validation frame. At both boundaries a sealed channel method compares the names
to the same fixed channel's retained binding and refuses a poisoned channel.
The existing authenticated channel/context checks remain on both sides. These
comparisons supplement the original canonical body, serial and descriptor
identity checks; they do not replace any observation or create a cached
authority decision. Failure poisons the original owner and keeps its custody.

This design avoids a second request owner and another complete validation walk.
It does not establish that execution fits the remaining preparation budget.
The 46 effect brackets and original 300/60/10-second windows stay unchanged.
The [binding evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-reply-binding-20261018/README.md)
separates ordinary ownership tests from the complete-frame gate. Actual original
delivery, manager/process/stream/cgroup authentication and all-writer cessation
are still required before completion or fence release.

Both GNU compiler fixtures pass eleven complete-round scenarios: healthy
preparation, missing/foreign correlation at opening and closing boundaries,
serial drift and channel-name refusal. The closing scenarios retain 34 original
authentication/signature calls and two channel/context checks; sticky refusal
prevents any channel check on retry. The initial healthy harness mistakenly
expected refusal after a successful frame; that failure remains separate from
the corrected test images. No runtime predicate or deadline was changed to
obtain the result. These controls establish preparation binding, not delivery,
process-loss recovery or a measured performance gain.

## Why original delivery needs a held launcher

The direct worker projection combines delivery and execution in one
`StartTransientUnit` request. A lost reply can therefore leave an executing
process before the receiver has pinned its cgroup. Neither a successful job
reply nor connection closure proves that every manager-held pipe writer is
closed. Adding a send operation to the preparation owner would not solve this
gap.

The approved two-phase design requires an independently armed watchdog before
delivery, a launcher held behind a one-shot barrier, original live binding of
its executable/streams/process/cgroup, then a complete validation frame before
release. Its separately signed v2 requirements bind the historical consent and
three artifact roles without changing the meaning of existing signed v1 bytes.
The data inspector authenticates a supplied signature, not production enrollment
or permission to execute. Signed time claims cannot refresh original admission
origins.

The first kernel experiment isolates the barrier from product execution and
evidence ownership. It tests a constant pipe effect, a fixed absolute BOOTTIME timer,
owner/guardian liveness pins and lost acknowledgment. It does not substitute a
live pidfd for actual watchdog readiness. In particular, death after the last
liveness observation still needs independent writer revocation; all-cgroup
cessation, external descriptor closure and actual EOF remain separate gates.

GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 each pass nine ordinary controls and the same twelve
owned kernel scenarios. In the lost-ACK case, the fixture proves its constant
pipe effect, stops before acknowledgment, then receives real SIGKILL through
its retained pidfd. The sender still cannot resend. This demonstrates the
ambiguity to preserve, not permission to replay an incomplete attempt.

The first healthy barrier failed because Linux reports the requested
`MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC` policy in output `msg_flags` even without ancillary data.
A direct kernel probe reproduced that bit. The new predicate accepts only zero
or that policy bit; a 32-bit mutation table and actual rights-transfer refusal
keep truncation, descriptor transfer and every other bit closed. No old
delivery predicate or deadline was changed. These are correctness results,
not a throughput or allocation improvement.

The [two-phase barrier packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/two-phase-launch-20261019/README.md)
retains the committed-source current/MSRV cohorts, original negative results and
exact scope. Actual pre-armed guardian enrollment, original delivery and complete
writer cessation still precede any production start or completion claim.

## Prearmed watchdog ownership and failure controls

The next experiment replaces the sleeping guardian surrogate with an actual
independent guardian, while retaining a deliberately nonproduct target. It must
publish Pending only after isolating its descriptors and retaining the creator
pidfd, original absolute BOOTTIME alarm and exclusive fence. Only then may the
fixture create and enroll its target. Armed is a separate acknowledgement, sent
after the guardian owns the exact received target pidfd. This ordering closes
the local lost-ACK gap: the sender cannot tell whether enrollment succeeded,
but the guardian already has the authority needed to terminate that target.

Enrollment uses a private versioned seqpacket protocol with kernel credentials
and exactly one atomically CLOEXEC pidfd. The receiver rejects a copied socket
used by another process, malformed or truncated ancillary data, ordinary files
and repeat enrollment. Rejected descriptors are closed without signaling an
untrusted process. The parent records uncertainty before its first send and
cannot retry after a missing ACK. These are local process-identity checks, not
proof that the creator is the historical admitted original owner.

The external nonroot driver kills the actual creator process. After release,
the target performs one constant pipe write and parks without observing its
owner or clock, so termination must come from the independent guardian. Actual
SIGKILL status and pipe EOF are checked separately from a Revoking notice.
An additional retained write alias prevents EOF after target death; closing
that alias is a separate observation. Neither notice, target exit nor EOF gives
this prototype an unlock path.

The negative controls are as important as successful owner-loss termination.
Killing the sole guardian after release leaves a live target with its write FD
and releases the last flock holder. Stopping that guardian prevents it from
acting at the original deadline until resumed, although its pidfd stays live.
A live pidfd therefore proves neither readiness nor responsiveness. Independent
original custody, durable history exclusion and an independently enforced
revocation path remain necessary; a final liveness check cannot replace them.

This prototype inspects ambient procfs and admits only a live direct child of
its creating process. A systemd-managed launcher normally belongs to PID 1, so
it cannot be admitted through this check. The next integration must use retained
original kernel, manager and cgroup context, not remove the parent predicate or
promote this local helper into a production constructor. The existing original
collector/custodian owners must remain retained through that integration.

The [prearmed watchdog evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/prearmed-watchdog-20261019/README.md)
separates the preliminary ten-case runs from the committed-source twelve-case
matrix, including these expected negatives. The experiment measures correctness
of ownership and failure ordering, not throughput, allocations or guaranteed
deadline latency. Existing original live checks, all 46 effect brackets and
300/60/10-second admission origins remain unchanged. Original delivery,
all-writer cessation, durable completion and reconnect still require their own
integration gates before server admission.

## Independent custody under a single guardian failure

The single-guardian counterexamples motivate a narrow local experiment: two
existing guardians independently retain the same target and aliases of the same
exclusive fence. Both publish Pending before target creation; both must retain
the target and return Armed before the fixture can pass its closing live check
and release the held target. Each receives exactly the same selected absolute
deadline. Creating another guardian does not extend the attempt's time window.

The composition consumes one global uncertainty latch before sending the first
enrollment. If the second guardian loses its ACK, the first may already own the
target. Retrying the first enrollment would itself trigger its duplicate-message
revocation and cannot reconstruct a known attempt. Instead the pair refuses
permanently, retains its existing owners and offers no retry, replacement or
completion operation. A real partial-enrollment test kills the second guardian
before its ACK, checks that the first still owns the unreleased target, and
verifies that a retry sends nothing.
This is an in-memory latch, not durable replay exclusion after process restart.

Actual SIGKILL and SIGSTOP tests exercise each guardian in turn. After the
creating process is killed, the remaining running guardian kills the released
target and retains the fence. When the creator stays alive, the remaining
guardian still kills the target at the unchanged original fixture deadline.
These results establish independent local revocation for that single-failure
model, not immediate detection of a stopped sibling or a scheduling-latency
guarantee. Separate terminal status and pipe EOF observations remain mandatory.

The scope ends where the fault model ends. Killing both guardians leaves a live
writer and releases the last flock; stopping both leaves a live writer at expiry
until one resumes. An external write-FD alias also prevents EOF after the target
dies. The pair neither revokes that alias nor proves whole-cgroup cessation.
Those retained negatives prohibit promoting redundant pidfds to completion or
durable exclusion authority.

The [redundant watchdog evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/redundant-watchdog-20261019/README.md)
records the seventeen-case matrix, ordinary latch/thread controls and unchanged
single-guardian counterexamples. The experiment leaves the existing guardian
protocol/body and original collector/custodian owners intact. It is not a
production topology decision: original kernel, manager, executable, stream and
cgroup binding inside the full validation frame, all-writer revocation, durable
history/completion and reconnect still need integration. No native/RESP product
path or admission deadline changed, and no performance gain is inferred.

The next boundary is input ownership. A local guardian that accepts a File and

expose descriptors, construct a guardian or release the held target. Its borrow

The fourteen full-frame controls distinguish healthy preparation/revalidation,
retained-context refusal before authentication, closing drift after the complete
round, channel-name refusal and actual original custody loss. Records and fence
ownership are checked independently. Test channels remain separate from the
production owner; these controls do not authenticate an installed system-bus

its consent cannot authorize separately signed v2 held-launcher artifacts.

The [context evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-watchdog-context-20261019/README.md)
retains an initial unchanged-baseline Kernel(Invalid) refusal and the isolated
baseline/candidate runs. Local WSL automatic time synchronization is paused only

Actual original guardian enrollment, v2 artifacts/process/cgroup binding,

GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 both pass those fourteen scenarios, four ordinary context
controls, thirty retained exchange controls and seventeen guardian regression

## Pending guardians inherit the original timer and fence

The borrowed context now has a consuming Pending preparation path. Its kernel
adapter receives the actual borrowed fence and existing timer from retained
original objects. It inherits the fence OFD into two independent children and
duplicates only the existing timer OFD; it does not replace its absolute bound,
consume its readiness or call flock. Acknowledged children retain exactly the fence,
timer, creating-owner pidfd and private channel, shedding unrelated writer FDs.
The existing credentialed Pending protocol and targetless child loop are reused
unchanged. There is no target enrollment operation on the returned adapter.

Creating a process also creates a cleanup obligation. The parent owns the
atomic clone3 pidfd and cancellation object before restoring its signal mask.
If restoration or the second clone fails, cleanup signals and waits through
the exact child pidfd while the original borrow and collector/custodian still
hold the original fence. Cancelling these Pending children cannot declare an
attempt complete or establish that another process stopped writing.

Original admission surrounds this kernel preparation with two unchanged full
context rounds. The healthy fixture retains 68 authentication calls, 68
signature calls and four manager-channel checks. Revalidation retains one
full round with 34 of each and two channel checks, surrounded by Pending
observations. A kernel or context failure refuses that same original chain;
the failure owner retains its original borrow. The low-level borrowed-FD
adapter alone cannot manufacture this original owner or a start permission.

The [Pending evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/original-pending-watchdog-20261019/README.md)
separates four kernel controls from ten full-frame cases. The first checks
actual shared timer OFD status, descriptor exclusion, exact signal-mask
restoration, partial-child cleanup and thread ownership. The second includes
real SIGKILL of either new guardian before closing admission, context drift and
loss of original custody. The OFD-status mutation belongs only to an owned unit
fixture; original frame timers are never modified. These tests establish a
preparation/custody boundary, not a faster native/RESP path.

The repeated old-image baseline supplies a useful environmental refusal:
CLOCK_REALTIME moves backward by about 5.4 seconds while BOOTTIME advances.
The unchanged kernel ordering check stops fixture preparation. A subsequent
local clock observation runs before new receive/admission origins are created;
it changes no clock, renews no window and does not guarantee later stability.
Live frame checks remain active, and local WSL time synchronization is restored
after each approved isolated gate. The backward step's external cause is not
established by this trace.

Pending still does not mean Armed or responsive. A stopped child can retain a
nonterminal pidfd, and a targetless child parks with its fence on creator loss
or expiry. Both-failure safety, authenticated executable/stream/process/cgroup
enrollment, original delivery and all external writer copies remain separate
obligations. The old direct-child predicate is not removed to admit a systemd
worker. New timer aliases and child/channel owners also have a real resource
cost; no zero-allocation or numerical performance improvement is claimed.

Both GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 pass ten new Pending and fourteen retained context
frame cases on source `4b946bbe`. The full source suite passes 274 controls,
preserving all 376 previous Rust bodies and old protocols/harnesses. Earlier
clock-preflight failures remain refused evidence, not accepted cohorts. The
final recipe adds bounded environment settling before the exact previous strict
clock probe; all actual admission origins are created afterward, and every live
frame predicate remains. This does not repair or establish the external clock's
trust. Best-effort destructor cancellation is likewise not a completion receipt;
future writer enrollment must provide independent, observed cessation proof.

Evidence tooling exposed another boundary: a culture-sensitive BOM-prefix check
treated ordinary ASCII as matching an ignorable Unicode prefix and removed the

mismatch. The corrected local inventory uses ordinal BOM comparison and six
prefix/encoding controls, including a mutation of the first byte. Its eight
inventory mutations remain separate. The failed inventory is retained, and an
append-only audit binds all 182 unchanged files in four historical packets to
their full Git baseline without rewriting them. Those legacy verifiers are not
safe for new inventories; neither old nor corrected checksums grant runtime or
release authority. Product signatures and binary digests did not use this helper.

## Original arming needs a revocation topology decision

The next transition exposes a dependency that another ownership wrapper cannot
solve. The unchanged private guardian accepts only a live direct child of its
creator and retains that target before Armed. A worker created by systemd has a
different parent and appears only after delivery. Meanwhile, the separately
signed two-phase requirements put independent Armed before the first held
launcher delivery. The original Pending pair therefore cannot become production
Armed just by accepting the eventual worker pidfd.

The [arming boundary audit](../testing/performance/0.74/original-arming-boundary-audit-20261019.md)
separates actual capabilities from read-only observations. A retained process
generation and consistent cgroup tree do not authenticate original-start
provenance or confer kill authority. A unit's KillMode setting does not connect
the autonomous guardian to complete cgroup revocation. The original message
still carries the v1 worker projection; its consent cannot authorize a different
held executable.

The recommended design to review is an attempt-specific empty revocation root,
possibly a dedicated systemd slice, enrolled before held delivery. A new guardian
protocol could arm against its pinned kernel identity and the unchanged original
timer. Actual executable, process, streams and descendant cgroup would still be
bound under the full validation frame before release. Creating that root changes
the host topology and requires explicit approval, a separate versioned projection
and trust/epoch binding. It is not implemented or proved by the existing tests.

Even that topology cannot close writer copies outside its root. Creator and
manager aliases, both actual pipe EOFs after drain, exclusive collector
finalization and durable attempt exclusion remain mandatory. Moving Armed after
delivery instead would change the signed ordering contract and introduce a
delivered-FD window without an armed target revoker. Neither weakening the old
parent check nor changing a readiness label is an acceptable substitute for
resolving this architecture boundary.

## An attempt root separates revocation from a future worker PID

The approved next component introduces a distinct root enrollment packet and
private pinned-cgroup mechanics. Its fixed 104 bytes bind an attempt digest,
original-context digest, root device/inode and selected absolute BOOTTIME bound.
Unknown versions, kinds, reserved bytes, field violations or size changes
refuse; the old direct-child guardian packet remains unchanged. A one-shot
claim tracker consumes its send before the future syscall boundary and refuses
a second send after failed delivery or uncertain acknowledgment. These are
expected bytes and per-instance accounting, not a runtime Armed capability or
durable replay exclusion.

The kernel handle opens one child of a retained parent without following a
symlink, requires a root-owned empty unfrozen cgroup2 domain, and retains the
directory and original type/events/procs/kill descriptors. Observation checks
their named and retained identities and refuses drift permanently. The kill
operation writes only the retained original control descriptor; a later name
replacement cannot redirect it to a new root. A kill submission cannot return
an EOF, completion or fence-release receipt.

The [kernel interface](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html)
provides recursive `cgroup.kill` and hierarchical populated observations.
Neither prevents a new writer from being admitted after an empty observation,
nor closes a pipe alias outside the tree. The owned local tests retain those
limits explicitly: a newly populated root needs another revocation, and an
external write alias blocks actual EOF after the scoped writers die. The old
direct-child predicate has not been generalized to arbitrary systemd PIDs.

The [local evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/cgroup-root-enrollment-20261019/README.md)
separates parser/mutation controls, private kernel-root checks and real process
cuts around kill submission. The before-write kill-caller SIGKILL is deliberately
negative: without an autonomous guardian, its target remains live until exact
fixture cleanup. Later cuts verify actual target SIGKILL, not invented recovered
success. These cuts concern the private kill operation; authenticated enrollment
ACK loss and joined launch/release/completion still need their own matrices.

Next, actual creator credentials and three atomic-CLOEXEC FD roles must be
checked by the new transport, then retained by independent guardians under the
same original fence/timer. Original policy/epoch/artifact/channel/frame binding
and the separately projected held unit remain necessary before Armed can enable
delivery. Local root privileges in this package belong only to fresh temporary
cgroup fixtures; no unit is installed, no supervisor is stopped and no product
workload is run. Functional case counts are not an allocation or throughput gain.

On source `593e5148`, GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 each pass seven new ordinary

and 24 actual SIGKILL cuts of the private kill caller in total. The complete

Windows passes 54 ordinary and eighteen compile-fail controls; affected strict
lint passes on both GNU compilers and Windows. These results close the local
packet/root-mechanics package, not authenticated FD transfer, an autonomous
root guardian or the original-start gate.

### Credentials identify a message but do not arm a guardian

The next hypothesis concerns enrollment integrity rather than throughput:
receiving the right-looking packet must not allow the wrong process or the
wrong kernel objects to become the revocation root. Source `65b02f3b` adds a
private ordinary-process sender and receiver to test that boundary independently
of the original runtime. It does not alter the old guardian or weaken its
direct-child predicate.

The pair captures the actual creating process and thread and its real/effective
credentials. Each request then needs matching per-message kernel credentials
and exactly three atomic-CLOEXEC rights in directory, kill, events order. The
reader checks actual cgroup2 ownership, access modes, directory identity, named
document correspondence and repeated empty unfrozen domain observations.
Correct packet bytes cannot substitute another root or swap the file roles.
These checks follow the Linux
[UNIX socket](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html) and
[recvmsg](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/recvmsg.2.html) interfaces; they
do not claim protection against a privileged adversary controlling the host.

Refusal must also release received aliases. Ordinary controls transfer pipe
writers as unwanted rights and require actual EOF after rejection, including
ancillary truncation. A separate exec process sends through an inherited
endpoint to verify that possession of the socket does not make its PID the
creator. Both operation objects consume before their first syscall, so failed
send, early receive, bad input or missing confirmation cannot reopen the same
attempt. The local root matrix additionally substitutes each role with another
real root and changes directory permissions after send.

The [evidence packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/cgroup-root-transport-20261019/README.md)
keeps these request checks separate from guardian readiness. No ACK is emitted,
and the received object offers no kill, launch, completion or unlock method.
It allocates in an ordinary process and must not run inside a raw post-clone
guardian. Original live process-pidfd/fence/timer custody and a reply from the
actual independent guardian still need their own join. The selected root
SIGKILL regression cuts concern the older private kill caller, not this future
authenticated reply or original-start boundary. This package supplies no
allocation, latency or throughput claim and opens no server execution.

On the selected source, GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 each pass six new ordinary

### Independent notification cursors keep late revocation active

Source `72f53806` adds a local active root-guardian pair rather than promoting
the earlier ordinary-process reader into original admission. Two clone3
children isolate their descriptors, retain the existing fence and timer open
descriptions, and monitor actual creator process pidfds. Their new request
handling uses bounded stack buffers and syscalls, without the allocator-based
Rust reader after clone. The parent submits both requests before waiting for
either reply, then checks the real child credentials and live pidfds. A missing
ACK cannot reopen the consumed attempt.

The useful distinction is which open descriptions should be shared. Sharing
the fence preserves its lock until the last holder closes it; sharing the
existing timer preserves its unchanged expiry without renewal or counter reads.
Sharing the events notification cursor is unsafe for independent observers.
Linux [kernfs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.6/fs/kernfs/file.c)
tracks acknowledged events per open file. One observer could consume another's
notification. Each guardian therefore retains the authenticated original events
descriptor but opens its own read-only watcher on the same bound inode.

The other ordering decision concerns late writers. Revocation acknowledges its
own event before kill, never kill followed by acknowledgement and sleep. A
writer admitted between those latter two operations could otherwise be observed
and cleared without being killed. The local fixture admits eight later waves
after the first descendants are dead and requires actual SIGKILL each time.
Only the original retained kill descriptor is used; reopening a replacement
target is not a recovery strategy. Observed frame drift refuses readiness and
does not erase an already retained revocation obligation.

Timer inspection also needed a narrower primitive. The initial unit screen
refused the kernel's space-separated clockid line because the prototype expected
a tab. That was a parser error, not grounds to widen the absolute-bound check.
Reviewing Linux's [timer implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.6/fs/timerfd.c)
also showed that gettime can forward an expired periodic timer. The final
mechanics use fdinfo under opening/closing BOOTTIME samples and never call that
getter. A negative expired-periodic fixture requires the event and expired
value to remain unchanged after refusal. The bracket checks consistency with
the selected bound; it does not reconstruct expiry identity or grant authority.

The [local evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/root-guardian-20261019/README.md)
separates actual channel disconnection from still-untested creator SIGKILL.
Positive cases close all parent copies of the original fence and require a
surviving guardian to retain its lock. Killing both guardians loses that lock;
stopping both leaves writers alive despite the retained lock. An outside pipe
alias likewise prevents EOF after the scoped writers die. These negatives
remain necessary gates, not inconveniences removed from the model. Local v2
Armed replies therefore do not enable original delivery, durable completion or
server execution. The original full-frame/trust/manager join and whole-writer
cessation still precede those actions; no throughput or allocation gain follows
from this functional package.

GNU 1.94 and the accepted MSRV 1.88 repetition each pass five new ordinary
controls and three sixteen-case active-pair matrices: 96 selected scenario
executions. Old transport, root SIGKILL and seventeen-case guardian controls
remain green in the accepted cohorts. The complete source suite passes 283
controls and preserves all 389 prior Rust bodies; Windows retains 54 ordinary
and eighteen compile-fail passes. Strict affected lint passes on both GNU
compilers and Windows. The first MSRV cohort remains separately failed: a live
fd-directory entry disappeared before readlink in the unchanged old guardian
harness. Repeating the same source and checks passed, but does not resolve that
snapshot race or turn the failed first cohort into evidence of success. Its
descriptor role was not captured, so the exception does not establish lost
fence custody or a product regression. This tooling reliability risk stays
visible alongside the still-closed original constructor and creator-loss gates.

### Real creator death is a separate boundary

The next [local package](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/root-creator-20261019/README.md)
distinguishes three events that must not be conflated: closing a control socket,
dropping an ordinary Rust owner, and killing the actual creator process. Its
external Python subreaper receives exact guardian pidfds through a
credential-checked test carrier, then kills its exec-created creator through
the creator's own pidfd. It checks SIGKILL status and adoption of the same
guardians. The Rust implementation, not a copied enrollment routine, pauses at
the selected boundaries.

The cuts cover the first ACK read, second ACK read, local armed assignment,
API return and both ACKs queued but unread. Controlled direct and nested writers
must still be alive immediately before the creator is killed. Surviving
guardians must then kill those writers before the unchanged fixture alarm,
retain the original flock after every creator alias closes, and revoke later
population. This prevents an expiry or an already dead writer from masquerading
as proof of creator-loss handling. Both-dead and both-stopped controls remain
explicit negatives; an outside pipe alias still blocks EOF after scoped kills.

The original validation join is a separate change. Its opaque owner supplies
the original fence and existing timer. The packet digest binds actual owner
IDs, original state, origins and bounds, all retained descriptor roles,
collector/custodian pins, fixed manager names, original serial and addressed
writer aliases to the pinned root identity. No caller supplies a replacement
deadline or context digest. Preparation and enrollment each bracket their
kernel work with complete original validation rounds. Closing failure poisons
both sides; possible enrollment never becomes permission to retry.

The testing boundary matters as much as the type boundary. Existing nonroot
original-frame fixtures keep their restriction and use a distinct simulated
kernel to exercise the same join. Root-only fixtures exercise the actual kernel
adapter separately. These results cannot be multiplied into a claim that a
privileged original manager exchange has passed end to end. Pinning a real
cgroup also does not authenticate that it is the production attempt root.
Binding holder pidfds identifies them; it does not establish confinement of
every holder and descriptor copy to that root. An outside writer can still
keep the stream open after the scoped processes die.
Protected host enrollment, the combined original privileged fixture and
whole-writer cessation remain necessary before held-unit start or completion.
No throughput or allocation improvement is claimed from these functional gates.

### Returning a borrow must not reopen an attempt

The creator and frame baseline passed its local gates, but a final source audit
found a different lifetime boundary. Dropping the new root wrapper closed its
channels and requested independent revocation, yet left the borrowed original
owner unrefused. Per-pair consumption prevented reuse of that pair; it did not
exclude preparing a fresh pair after the exclusive borrow returned. This was
an internal preparation gap, not a demonstrated production replay: production
original-root admission and execution were still closed.

The [retirement follow-up](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/root-retirement-20261019/README.md)
adds unconditional refusal in wrapper Drop, before its fields release. It first
refuses the original owner, then the kernel controls. Targetless Pending cleanup
remains exact; possibly enrolled guardians are not cancelled and keep their
revocation/fence obligation. Refusal neither reads nor renews an admission
clock, and no completion or unlock path is introduced.

A source regression first fails on the missing destructor. Callback controls
check owner-before-kernel ordering for both pending and consumed states. The
full original-frame regression then retires the owner and creates fresh
simulated controls for a new attempt: rejection must come from the original
owner, not merely from the old controls' refused bit. The existing kernel
refusal controls remain a separate concrete gate. This closes the owner
retirement boundary without pretending to prove the combined privileged
original constructor or confinement of every writer.
Normal wrapper retirement is not itself the durable enrollment/replay protocol;
that production admission boundary remains separate.

The follow-up also retains a negative result. GNU refuses during the unchanged
output-preparation path with Causal(Time), before the new retirement callback
can run. A same-source retry after the heavy source suite finishes refuses at
the same boundary. Passing unit/static/kernel controls cannot turn this into
a passing full-frame gate. The error distinguishes neither a ten-second causal
age from BOOTTIME rollback nor a boot change without the issued/now tuple.
A separate preflight observes a backwards CLOCK_REALTIME step before creating
an attempt, but that does not identify the BOOTTIME failure's cause. Attribution
of this original preparation boundary remains required; its threshold is not
adjusted to obtain a green result.

The confirmed creator/frame baseline retains 72 creator-SIGKILL scenarios,
24 real kernel-adapter scenarios and 48 original-frame scenarios across GNU
1.94 and MSRV 1.88. After retirement hardening, both compilers pass its ordinary
ordering control, additional twelve-case creator and four-case kernel smoke
matrices. MSRV also passes three fresh-controls retirement-frame repetitions
and the eight-case prior frame regression. GNU's corresponding frame gate stays
red before the new callback. The full source suite passes 292 controls, but this
cannot substitute for the missing GNU dynamic receipt. Evidence records that
mixed disposition, not an averaged score or a production-readiness claim.

### Measure freshness from issuance rather than test entry

The [preparation attribution](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/gnu-preparation-20261019/README.md)
copies issued and observed BOOTTIME values and both boot identities at the
existing causal comparisons. These test-only copies do not sample a new clock,
renew an origin or participate in admission. The original comparisons and all
live validation remain unchanged; source guards remove only exact test hooks
before comparing the prior bodies and protocols.

Three fresh GNU 1.94 preparations and three MSRV 1.88 controls complete without
the earlier Causal(Time) refusal. The last observed challenge ages after
enrollment are 7.73–8.23 seconds on GNU and 7.57–8.26 seconds on MSRV, below the
unchanged ten-second limit. Both boot identities agree throughout the observed
points. The overall tests take roughly eleven to thirteen seconds because
challenge issuance happens after test entry. Comparing total test duration to
challenge freshness would therefore diagnose the wrong interval.

This series does not retrospectively explain the older failure: its original
issued/now tuple is unavailable. Neither temporary local clock stabilization
nor the new instrumentation is demonstrated to have fixed it. The earlier
negative packet remains closed, and preparation success is not the separate
retirement-frame callback proof or privileged host admission.

The attribution does locate substantial cost in the unchanged preparation.
Each fresh attempt uses 640 authentication/signature calls through consent,
782 through output preparation and another 34 through enrollment preparation.
GNU output preparation takes 5.90–6.62 seconds, while authentication occupies
only 79–91 milliseconds, including 59–63 milliseconds of signature verification.
About 65–66 percent of output wall time falls inside existing nested kernel
spans. Boot and namespace checks are the largest individual categories outside
their instrumented direct children. Each output phase performs 4,232 worker
revalidations, 153,088 Boot spans and 306,176 Namespace spans.

Those counts identify validation amplification; they are not permission to
remove observations or cache a live decision. Authentication, live-walk and
kernel spans overlap, and wall attribution is neither exclusive CPU time nor
a syscall census. Instrumentation also has overhead and can change code
generation, so these results do not establish a compiler speedup or a product
throughput improvement. The next isolated hypothesis should reduce measured
leaf work while preserving every live predicate, observation boundary and
original deadline. It must then pass the actual GNU functional gate, not use
the diagnostic harness's successful collection as a substitute.

### Fixed paths: allocation cost is not wall speed

The next isolated proposal changes path construction, not validation frequency.
Boot lookup still opens `sys/kernel/random/boot_id` relative to the retained
proc root, checks each filesystem, performs the same bounded positional read
and closes the document before decoding. Four compile-time C strings replace
four temporary `CString` values. The four known namespace names use borrowed
literal paths; unknown names keep the old formatting and error behavior. Every
namespace is still opened afresh, checked as nsfs and identified by metadata.
Neither file descriptors nor observations are cached. Original full rounds,
46 effect brackets and the 300/60/10-second origins and deadlines remain intact.

The timing experiment did not establish a reliable small-effect endpoint.
Reference and actual functions initially used equivalent source in one image;
an A/A control nevertheless attributed a positive interval to one leaf. An
opaque shared caller and balanced ABBA/BAAB order did not remove all false
attribution. Finally an external crossover invoked the actual entry in two
byte-identical images. GNU namespace results included zero, but the MSRV
namespace control produced a spurious negative interval. These are calibration
failures before runtime optimization, not evidence for adopting or rejecting
the path candidate. Their raw logs remain separate, and no wall-speedup claim
or timing-rule waiver follows. The experiment does not identify which mixture
of host noise, layout, compilation or scheduling caused those differences.

Before changing runtime paths, a separate allocation-cost protocol was recorded.
An opt-in test-only observer forwards Rust allocator requests unchanged to
`System` and counts successful requests in the current capture thread. It
checks nesting, unwind restoration, thread isolation, zeroed allocation and
reallocation. Three baseline samples per leaf and compiler each execute 1,024
fresh real-kernel calls; their actual and frozen-reference counts must agree
exactly. Acceptance requires fewer allocation/reallocation requests for both
leaves on both compilers, no request or requested-byte increase, differential
identity/error/flag checks and the unprofiled GNU retirement gate. Requested
bytes are not retained memory, and Rust requests are not a libc malloc census.
The observer is absent from ordinary test and production binaries; it never
supplies retirement evidence or authority to start a workload.

GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 reproduce the same counts in all three samples. Each
fresh boot call drops from five Rust allocations and 62 requested bytes to one
allocation and 36 bytes; each known namespace call drops from one allocation
and 42 bytes to zero. Reallocations remain zero, no counter increases and the
frozen reference retains its original counts in each candidate image. The
remaining boot allocation owns the validated UUID. This supports a narrow
allocation-cost reduction, not faster kernel syscalls, lower retained memory
or higher HydraCache throughput. All the expensive live observations remain;
the failed wall calibration cannot be turned into a performance claim simply
because a different, deterministic endpoint improved.

The [retained evidence packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/fixed-leaf-path-20261019/README.md)
also separates functional acceptance from cost attribution. Before implementation
the old unprofiled GNU image passed three retirement callbacks and the existing
eight-case full-frame regression. After implementation the new ordinary image
passes the same controls, with the original bounds and zero retired retry work.
Local clock service restoration and unchanged fixture hashes are verified.
The path change is retained for its measured allocation reduction and preserved
semantics, not credited with fixing the unobserved historical failure. Root
controls in this particular frame gate are simulated; combined privileged
original host admission, all-writer cessation, completion and reconnect remain
separate work. The results do not authorize server installation or product load.

## A refused owner can still hold a writer

The next [ownership audit](../testing/performance/0.74/owned-root-manager-design.md)
found a lifetime distinction that profiling cannot settle. The original guardian
adapter borrowed its manager message. Retirement made that owner unusable, but
the caller still owned the message and its output aliases. An empty cgroup and a
refused API therefore did not establish that writing had ceased. This was an
ownership gap, not a reason to remove live checks or lengthen a deadline.

The separate consuming adapter takes the exact original manager message and
retains its entire frame. It derives the guardian binding through the same full
validation rounds and uses the existing root preparation/enrollment algorithms.
Retirement first refuses the original owner; field destruction then closes its
aliases and cancels/reaps its original collector and custodian. Enrolled root
guardians remain independent with the original fence and alarm. A failed
preparation retains the original owner rather than returning a reusable message.
The borrowed implementation is unchanged, so existing behavior is not silently
reinterpreted. No original delivery, completion or unlock capability is added.

The test now combines a real fixed manager channel, numeric-root retained
ancestry, actual kernel sender credentials and root cgroup guardians in one
original frame. Synthetic issuers and a copied signed bundle are explicitly
fixture inputs. Three harmless writers produce bytes through the original
streams from direct and nested groups, including duplicated stdout/stderr roles.
Before revocation the harness verifies their live pidfds and actual cgroup
membership. Afterward it requires exact SIGKILL waits and drained EOF, not merely
a successful kill call or an empty subtree. An intentionally external writer
can still write and blocks EOF until closed. That negative prevents the test
from presenting cgroup control as revocation of arbitrary external descriptors.

Normal Rust destruction and creator death are measured separately. In the latter
an external subreaper sends SIGKILL to the exact creator and keeps dummy stdin
writers open; natural EOF exit cannot masquerade as watchdog revocation. The
original collectors must shed output descriptors while retaining fence custody.
The original deadline is observed without rearming it. The
[evidence packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/owned-root-manager-20261019/README.md)
records which boundaries actually pass, including preliminary refusals. None of
these local safety checks is a product throughput result or production host
admission. Authentication of original delivery and durable lifecycle/reconnect
remain distinct gates even when this ownership boundary is green.

The actual result is deliberately narrower than the intended gate. Both ordinary
seven-case combined matrices pass, and the external GNU screen and six creator
cases pass. MSRV passes creator loss and first-guardian loss, then refuses its
next attempt during the unchanged closing validation frame with `Challenge(Time)`
before the named fault can be injected. Its last enrollment observation was
9,724,276,622 ns after challenge issuance, with matching boot identities. That
observation precedes the failing closing comparison; it is context, not a captured
explanation of that later error or the earlier GNU `Causal(Time)` refusal.

The packet therefore records nine selected real creator-SIGKILL successes and
an incomplete cross-compiler gate, not thirteen passes. It retains both refusals,
does not create a positive run receipt and rejects metadata which promotes the
MSRV result. The secondary fixture double-wait was fixed and regression-tested;
the later refusal cleans up without a destructor panic. Original deadlines and
all complete live rounds remain unchanged. The next question is the cost and
exact time observations of closing validation, not which threshold to relax or
how many retries eventually produce green. This is a local safety and attribution
result, not a product speedup or permission to launch the server.

## Closing validation can consume the last part of the freshness window

The next [attribution](../testing/performance/0.74/closing-validation-design.md)
identified a comparison missing from the earlier report. After the complete
grouped validation, custody inspects its existing alarm and calls the original
challenge-age predicate with another BOOTTIME sample. The alarm and challenge
freshness checks are independent; a healthy earlier sample is not permission
to omit either later check. Test-only recording now copies the actual age
arguments and caller location without reading a replacement clock. Removing
the exact observation hooks recovers all 418 earlier source bodies, and all
303 source contracts pass.

Six fixed cost attempts use the existing authentication, live-walk and kernel
observers around one unchanged closing call. A new GNU attempt reproduces the
custody error at age 10,003,292,291 ns, after the last earlier final-clock sample
still reported 9,985,119,124 ns. Closing validation took 261.749 ms. Another GNU
attempt refuses at the causal-window comparison at 10,068,131,423 ns; its round
ends early and must not be averaged with completed rounds. The original
exclusive ten-second guard makes both decisions. These new tuples explain the
error mechanism, not the exact missing tuple of the historical MSRV attempt.

All three MSRV cost rounds complete in 218.287–303.411 ms. Each performs 34
authentication/signature checks, 6,688 Boot and 13,376 Namespace observations.
Authentication occupies 2.457–2.742 ms; kernel-context inclusive wall spans
occupy 106.285–152.244 ms. These are instrumented, overlapping wall spans, not
exclusive CPU or syscall counts. The evidence points toward the cost of repeated
fresh live/kernel work rather than treating signature verification as the
dominant target. It does not establish a product speedup or justify caching a
live result, removing an observation or changing the deadline origin.

The [separate evidence packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/closing-validation-20261019/README.md)
retains every cost refusal and keeps its functional gate false. A separate
facts-only cohort checks the previously missing MSRV creator faults with the
original real-writer SIGKILL, EOF and busy-fence requirements. Cost observations
and actual fault receipts remain separate, as do local fixture success and
production host admission.

All four previously missing MSRV fault cases pass in facts-only mode, along
with owner loss as a regression. The final first-guardian-loss regression
refuses before closing validation: its actual enrollment observation reaches
10,024,697,034 ns after challenge issuance. No named fault is injected into that
expired attempt, and no positive complete-cohort receipt is produced. Five
actual SIGKILL proofs are kept separate from the refused sixth case. This places
the next optimization question across the full preparation/enrollment budget,
not just closing latency. The new diagnostic evidence never refreshes an old
attempt, changes its ten-second window or turns local fixture success into
permission to install or launch the server.

## Fresh boot comparisons do not need a temporary String

The next [isolated change](../testing/performance/0.74/boot-comparison-design.md)
uses the kernel attribution without treating its overlapping spans as exclusive
CPU costs. Revalidation repeatedly reads and strictly validates the boot UUID,
then compares a newly allocated String with the retained identity. Equality
does not need temporary ownership. The candidate therefore borrows the just-read
stack bytes for that comparison while preserving owned boot IDs in retained
origins and returned time points.

Every observation is still fresh: the same path components, open flags,
filesystem checks and positional read run each time. The document is still
closed before decoding, strict UUID and UTF-8 checks remain, and read errors
are not retried. No file descriptor, boot result or namespace observation is
cached. The original module retains the actual decoder predicates so its old
mutation tests remain effective. The first version's relocation failed that
structural guard; the correction preserves the guard rather than teaching it
to ignore the missing predicates.

The [new evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/boot-comparison-20261019/README.md)
first measures three baseline pairs, then repeats three pairs on each GNU and
MSRV candidate, with 1,024 complete calls per operation. All pairs agree.
Revalidation falls from two Rust allocation requests for 72 bytes per call to
zero. Sampling falls from five requests for 180 bytes to one for 36 bytes; the
remaining request owns the returned boot ID. Differential cases cover every
single-byte mutation, malformed lengths and seeded documents, and actual kernel
tests retain the original fresh-observation counts and refusal sites.

This is a confirmed reduction in temporary Rust allocation requests on a path
used throughout preparation and enrollment. It is not a measured reduction in
elapsed preparation, libc allocation, RSS or product latency. An unchanged
ten-second window can still expire because of the remaining live/kernel work.
The separate unprofiled MSRV creator-SIGKILL cohort therefore remains a necessary
functional check; allocator counts cannot stand in for actual writer cessation,
completion or permission to launch the server.

The new unprofiled MSRV cohort passes all six fixed cases once, including the
previously refused first-guardian-loss regression. Each actually kills the
creator, stops three dummy writers before original expiry, drains both readers
and keeps the fence busy. Last observed custody ages span 8.273–8.764 seconds
within the original exclusive ten-second window. This is not a paired timing
experiment against the old failures, so the successful gate is not attributed
to the allocation change. The allocator reduction and this complete local
functional result stand independently. Historical partial outcomes remain
unchanged; original delivery, production trust, lifecycle/reconnect and server
admission remain separate work.

## A signature does not put the worker inside the revocation root

After the local MSRV fault gate passed, the next audit asked what would happen
if the prepared original manager message were actually delivered. Its old
specification still runs a direct worker in system.slice, while the guardians
pin another attempt-specific root. The dummy fault fixtures explicitly move
their writers into that root. Their success therefore does not establish
confinement of the original worker, and sending the old message would also
execute it before the held-launcher barrier.

The [isolated next package](../testing/performance/0.74/held-placement-design.md)
binds the exact root Enroll packet and complete nested launch claims under a
new signature domain. Expected slice and child names derive from the same
attempt identity rather than accepting caller-supplied paths or commands.
The original device/inode, context digest and absolute bound are signed without
renewing them. Old readers and signatures are not upgraded.

This is deliberately a data-reader result. Seeded identities, changed packet
bytes, wrong domains/keys and malformed documents test what the signature
actually covers. They do not observe a live slice, select a production issuer,
construct a complete held unit or grant execution. The six admission fields
remain false. The next proof must join these expectations with the same live
owned manager/root and full validation frame, then establish actual held
placement before any send or release. No throughput, allocation or preparation
speedup is asserted for this package; it addresses a concrete execution-boundary
gap without weakening the original checks or deadlines.

All 309 source contracts pass. Both GNU and MSRV ordinary images pass the new
reader cases and unchanged selected kernel/root regression, with 247 Linux doc
tests each; Windows passes 60 unit and twenty doc tests. The first wrapper
incorrectly expected the Windows doc count on Linux. Its two refused results
and exact recipe remain in evidence; fresh final runs correct only that count,
not test predicates or a runtime deadline. A green wrapper is not allowed to
erase its earlier diagnostic mistake or promote these reader checks to start
authority.

## Bind signed constraints to the owner that still holds the resources

The next [local join](../testing/performance/0.74/owned-placement-design.md)
does not accept a caller-selected key or a reconstructed root. It consumes the
same manager/root holder, selects the retained controller-policy key, compares
the complete original consent and requires the exact already Armed enrollment.
The independently derived original context, root identity and absolute bound
must all match. A valid signature for another root or consent is insufficient.

Pure comparisons surround the unchanged complete live round inside the old root
join. Revalidation repeats both signature checks and the full round; its retained
hash prevents changing constraints rather than replacing live authorization.
Errors poison both owners and retain the complete consumed holder, whose old
destruction order closes the original aliases while independent guardians keep
fence/timer custody. No successful check releases the barrier or the fence.

This binds constraints to actual local custody, not to proven systemd placement.
Temporary fixture roots need not have the expected slice ancestry, and the v2
declared artifact hashes are not admitted executable objects. Those must be
checked before a separate held-unit projection. Production enrollment, a fresh
authenticated peer exchange and original delivery remain distinct gates. The
package tests this ownership boundary without asserting a throughput, allocation
or preparation-wall improvement.

The first actual cohort reveals a mistaken test oracle rather than a reason to
change the runtime fence policy. A never-Armed pair has no independent enrolled
keeper after its full failed holder is destroyed. The corrected test therefore
requires Busy and non-EOF while that failed holder is retained, then EOF and dead
custodians before checking raw-lock availability and fresh typed replay refusal.
All already-Armed cases still require Busy after destruction. The original timer
must remain live on intended refusals. The failed cohort remains a partial
negative; no deadline or numeric acceptance threshold is relaxed to replace it.

The corrected selected-source run passes healthy, revalidation and never-Armed
custody/replay checks on GNU. The fourth fresh attempt instead refuses the
original Causal(Time) guard during root preparation, before it can test the
wrong-key binding. MSRV is not executed in that cohort. The full live gate is
therefore still false despite all 312 source contracts, selected ordinary
Linux regression, strict lint and documentation tests passing.

The final observed ages in the two completed positive calls are 9.097 and
8.236 seconds. Those values do not recover the failing preparation tuple or
prove a speedup. The current facts capture begins at the later join; the next
attribution must encompass preparation and copy its existing issued/now/boot
and raw age observations, including unwind. This is a concrete observability
gap to close before choosing a cost optimization, not a reason to extend the
ten-second window or rerun the matrix until a fortunate pass. Both partial
cohorts remain in the [evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/owned-placement-20261019/README.md).

The [next capture](../testing/performance/0.74/placement-preparation-design.md)
wraps the entire unchanged fixture, catches unwind inside the existing causal

It adds no clock or retry. Kernel-time facts carry their actual boot IDs;

The new GNU attempt now proves the refused predicate: issued 884474515163 ns,

The independent MSRV run passes all seven scenarios once, including the binding

## Separate preparation phase cost from a healthy functional result

The [fixed phase probe](../testing/performance/0.74/placement-stage-cost-design.md)
adds only exact test markers to the original fixture and uses existing bounded
authentication, live-walk and kernel-walk counters. Disabled markers read no
diagnostic timer. Three independent GNU probes complete on the selected source,
with outputs taking 4.311–4.684 wall seconds. Its 782 authentication calls take
60.361–64.721 ms; signature time is included in that figure, not additional.
That gap does not justify calling the remainder I/O, but it does not support
prioritizing signature optimization either.

Every probe records 320831 Boot, 641664 Namespace and 160415 Origin observations.
Whole-probe resource usage is 6.83–6.98 system seconds and 3.22–3.45 user seconds,
with zero major page faults. Those scopes include pre-challenge work and waited
descendants; they are neither syscall counts nor CPU/op. Together they identify
repeated context/kernel work as the next cost direction, without proving an
exclusive cost for one predicate. Any candidate should first measure and trim
per-observation cost while retaining every fresh check and refusal boundary.

One preregistered normal regression follows the three probes with cost capture
disabled. All seven scenarios pass on GNU 1.94 and all seven on MSRV 1.88, once
each, including intended binding/trust refusals, original timer readiness, EOF,
custody/fence and typed replay refusal. All 318 source contracts and compiler
regressions pass; clock/root cleanup and signed fixture identity are verified.
The local same-owner functional gate is now complete on that exact source.

No runtime optimization caused this positive result: runtime code is unchanged,
and prior probes ran on the same boot. Cache/load/sample variation was not isolated
by an A/B experiment, so neither faster preparation nor repair of the historical
expiry follows. The measured GNU refusal remains a correct expiry refusal, while
the older unobserved tuple stays unknown. Cold or contended admission still
needs attention. Actual slice/artifact admission,
held projection, original delivery, durable lifecycle and reconnect remain distinct
from this local success. No server, supervisor or product workload was used.

## Bind the revocation root to its actual named path before projecting a unit

The same-owner matrix established consent, original context, deadline and
guardian custody. It did not establish where that retained kernel root lived.
A signature over system-hc074 plus an attempt digest does not move a temporary
root into that slice, and does not place the old direct worker underneath it.
That difference matters: a watchdog can kill exactly its pinned root while
leaving a worker outside it untouched.

The [fixed-path observer](../testing/performance/0.74/fixed-slice-design.md)
therefore compares actual directory objects rather than accepting a caller's
path string. It derives the name from the original enrollment attempt, retains
the path anchors, refuses symlinks and unsafe ownership/modes, and requires the
named child, original root and original parent to agree on their identities.
Revalidation compares both retained descriptors and fresh named traversal.
It never replaces the existing kill descriptor with a newly opened target.

The new holder consumes the complete original placement chain. Path checks
surround the unchanged signed placement join and full validation round; a failed
opening, closing or original predicate retires both owners while retaining the
failed holder. This is an additional invariant, not an optimization or permission
to resend. It creates neither a clock nor a fresh relative deadline.

Read-only path observations still cannot prove that a systemd manager owns the
slice, prevent privileged later population or admit signed artifact hashes as
actual executable objects. Those checks must join the held-unit construction
before delivery. Model acceptance and reading the host's existing system.slice
are not a successful actual attempt-root admission. Keeping that distinction
explicit prevents a green low-level check from opening original start too early.

The selected source passes 321 source contracts, and both GNU compilers pass
77 selected ordinary controls, 247 doc tests and one actual read-only anchor
check. This supports the new observation and composition boundaries, not a
positive admission of a real attempt slice. No performance gain is claimed.

A broader Windows integration invocation also exposes a pre-existing test
assumption: its synthetic root lock is reconstructed from the moving workspace
lock, then compared with an immutable production hash. The current and baseline
reconstruction both differ from that pin, while the lock from the pinned worker
source still matches exactly. Preserve this red instead of calling the entire
suite green because scoped library/doc controls pass. The separate repair is
to feed the synthetic test the exact frozen bytes, not weaken the hash check.

## Make synthetic build inputs follow the frozen worker source

The [separate fixture repair](../testing/performance/0.74/frozen-lock-fixture-design.md)
uses the exact 175300-byte root lock from the worker's already-pinned source.
Removing two dependency edges from the moving workspace was not a reconstruction
of that immutable file. Updating the expected hash to fit the workspace would
have hidden the defect by weakening the production boundary. Including the
original Git blob, preserving its LF bytes and retaining the same hash check
instead repairs only the synthetic input. Tests need no runtime Git or network.

The first corrected artifact target passes, allowing the broader invocation to
reach a second stale consumer in the receipt fixture. It directly hashed the
workspace lock and was correctly refused by the same production verifier.
Changing only its include path to the identical frozen fixture preserves every
old receipt assertion. New controls still reject 32 seeded corruptions, the
workspace-lock substitution and even a re-signed statement with its digest.
Valid test data must satisfy the existing boundary; it must not redefine it.

The completed ordinary Windows monitor package now passes 296 tests and twenty
docs with zero failures or ignored cases. GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 each pass all
31 artifact and nine receipt cases. The first Linux runners report refusal even
though those tests passed: they incorrectly expected only the eight portable
receipt cases. The ninth is an existing Linux-only spool/offline check. Retain
that runner error and require an enumerated complete nine-case repeat, rather
than treating an invocation failure as a product failure or dropping the extra
case to make a summary green.

Four source-scope guards show that both old test files reconstruct after reversing
only the explicit input changes; all 437 runtime files and production pins remain
unchanged. This is not a new run of the previous 321-check suite or the whole
Linux library suite. The [new evidence](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/frozen-lock-fixture-20261020/README.md)
keeps the original reds, intermediate lint/runner errors and final source/image
receipts separately. It establishes reproducible ordinary test coverage, not
faster product code or real installed executable trust. Actual slice ownership,
held artifacts, original delivery, writer cessation and reconnect still require
their own live evidence before server admission.

## Check retained paths against real cgroup objects

A model can show that two inode values differ without proving that the actual
open-descriptor and named-path observations behave as expected. The
[private namespace fixture](../testing/performance/0.74/fixed-slice-namespace-design.md)
therefore uses real empty cgroup2 directories with the unchanged FixedSlice
observer. A fresh test child creates its own mount namespace and makes its mount
propagation private before presenting the temporary tree at the fixed path.
The parent keeps its original namespace, mount anchors and host system.slice.
This allows kernel identity substitutions without creating a systemd unit or
changing a production mount.

The first refusal exposes an important measurement detail. Rust runs the test on
a thread other than its thread-group leader. Unshare changes the calling
thread's namespace, while /proc/self/ns/mnt still describes the leader. The
fixture must read /proc/thread-self/ns/mnt to measure the thread that will mount.
The inequality check stays before that mount; it is corrected, not removed.

Healthy pin/revalidation then succeeds on both compilers, but a later mutation
tries to rename a cgroup2 directory and receives EPERM. Counting that error as
an inode-substitution refusal would falsely credit a predicate that was never
evaluated. The replacement test instead removes only the exact empty fixture
cgroup and recreates its name while retaining the original descriptors. Parent
replacement also requires a different parent inode. All nine cases remain;
the unsupported mutation and earlier thread error remain separate raw results.

A successful private kernel pin still cannot certify manager ownership or
exclusive population. The synthetic system.slice is deliberately not owned by
the original systemd manager, and this test supplies no original controller
frame or executable admission. In particular, the existing worker build receipt
does not authenticate the newly declared launcher, watchdog and collector roles.
Those actual objects and the complete held-unit projection must join the original
trust and live frame before delivery. This is evidence about control-path
correctness, not an allocation or throughput improvement in HydraCache.

The completed local gate on 2f27453f passes the same nine kernel cases on GNU 1.94
and MSRV 1.88, with nine ordinary controls and 247 docs per compiler. Six exact
source guards and the Windows sixty-unit/twenty-doc selection pass separately.
The old 321-contract image also passes across the documented fixture-only HEAD
advance; it is not relabeled as stable-source qualification. The
[evidence packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/fixed-slice-namespace-20261020/README.md)
keeps these scopes, failed mutation recipes and final image identities distinct.

## Artifact roles do not define executable topology

The [next boundary audit](../testing/performance/0.74/held-artifact-boundary-audit-20261020.md)
separates three logical launch roles from their actual producers. Current root
guardians and the barred collector are private clone continuations, so their
executable identity is inherited from the original host image. The collector is
still quarantined, not an active drain/finalization service. The held launcher
has no production binary target. Creating three new files with the role names
would therefore be an execution-topology change, not an artifact-hash check.

The proposed minimal design keeps those existing keepers in the original host
image and adds one held launcher. A separate purpose-bound build policy/receipt
must attest the actual host and launcher with explicit role mapping. The old
worker receipt stays bound to its frozen source and recipe; it cannot be
relabeled as helper provenance. Equal watchdog/collector hashes alone supply
neither role identity nor original custody, and an active collector still needs
an admitted handoff.

The new signed contract must also distinguish before and after exec. Before
release, the held process is the launcher and retains the admitted worker's
executable FD. After one-shot pinned-FD exec, the same process generation must be
observed as the actual worker before publishing Running or completion. Calling
both observations the same executable check would hide a transition that needs
its own original-frame and lost-ack coverage. This topology and build-authority
proposal needs approval before implementation; it does not enroll a key, choose
an install path, extract a library or authorize a server run.

## Separate build purposes without expanding execution authority

The operator subsequently approved the minimal local contract. Its
[first implementation](../testing/performance/0.74/held-build-authority-plan-20261020.md)
keeps the old worker authority intact and adds a separate policy, constrained
signer and receipt/content verifier. The useful hypothesis here is about a trust
boundary, not speed: a worker receipt should not become authority for new helper
roles merely because all artifacts belong to the same release.

Two independent policy pins must authenticate the same controller, and the worker
builder, held-runtime builder and controller keys must all differ. The new policy
selects exact source/tree/root-lock inputs and an expected epoch. Its receipt
binds clean isolated-build observations, an exact GNU release recipe, distinct
host/helper images, raw build log and the fixed role map: launcher from the
helper, watchdog and collector from the original host image. Cargo log inspection
requires both exact binary records and one successful final event, rejecting
wrong packages, profiles, features, missing/duplicate targets and trailing events.

Sixteen synthetic integration cases include valid controls followed by altered
policies, re-signed invalid statements, content/role substitutions and 128 seeded
binary corruptions. They pass on Windows, GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88. Opaque checked
results have no start or unlock method. Exact source adapters preserve all 437
previous source files rather than relaxing the old live predicates or deadlines.
The [separate packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/held-build-authority-20261020/README.md)
records these tests and their limited scope; they are not a throughput claim.

What remains matters as much as what passes. Invented ELF headers and Cargo
events test the contract but cannot certify real images. A signature attests a
trusted build job's observations; it is not independent reproduction of that
build. The expected epoch is reviewed configuration, not a live original epoch.
Matching expected hashes is not descriptor custody or process identity. The next
package must implement the real held launcher and its inherited-FD, one-shot
worker-exec boundary, then join retained role objects to the original owner and
full validation frame. No production key, installation, server operation,
original message or workload is authorized by this component.

The selected-source gate also passes the complete old artifact/receipt selections
on each compiler, eight exact source guards, three predecessor bridge controls,
strict lint, fmt, registry/docs and the local non-promotable contract. The sealed
packet contains sixty hashed members plus inventory and refuses 26 in-memory
receipt metadata mutations. It preserves earlier evidence and the frozen
qualification digest; this package does not rerun the full 321 controls or a new
kernel/live/SIGKILL matrix.

## Verify the executable transition without changing the process generation

The next [local helper](../testing/performance/0.74/held-launcher-plan-20261020.md)
tests the distinction that signed artifact hashes could not close. Before
release the process must be the held launcher retaining the worker descriptor;
after exec the same process generation must execute the worker. Its PID alone
cannot identify the executable, and an expected image hash cannot prove either
observation.

The implementation accepts only fixed inherited descriptor roles. A sealed
bootstrap binds content and kernel identities; Ready/Release packets bind its
digest and token, with exact kernel sender credentials. The existing absolute
alarm and owner/guardian pidfds are revalidated, never renewed. One execveat uses
the worker FD, fixed arguments and empty environment, with only stdio/config
retained. There is no pathname fallback or positive execution ACK: a closed
channel remains uncertain rather than permitting another release.
