uses a tiny synthetic ELF, not HydraCache. Its marker and signal stop make the
transition observable: PID/start ticks remain, executable device/inode changes,
and the exact FD set, full argv and empty environment are inspected. Real SIGKILL
cuts cover the held process, post-exec process and external fixture owner, with
precise orphan cleanup. Other cases test expiry, both guardians, foreign same-UID
senders, packet/rights mutations, descriptor/content substitution and exec refusal.

The first 26-case cohort passes but does not cover every descriptor semantic.
The added O_PATH stdin test finds a real gap: access-mode bits alone classify a
path-only descriptor as read-only. It reaches Ready instead of refusing. The
fix adds O_PATH to the mask without relaxing a predicate or deadline. A separate
compiler error in the expanded argv oracle is retained and corrected; final
source 68b71834 has 27 cases. This is a concrete correctness gain from a failed
regression, not an allocation or throughput result.

The helper still supplies mechanics, not original authority. Guardian liveness
does not mean Armed, a pre-exec guard is not post-exec all-writer termination,
and the local marker is not a product receipt. Actual purpose-bound role builds,
retained original objects and the complete policy/epoch/root/manager frame must
join this path before original delivery. Active collector, durable lifecycle and
same-attempt reconnect remain separate gates; server installation stays closed.

At the final selected source, GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 each pass two complete

unchanged build-authority cases and two capability examples per compiler pass.
Ten source guards, three predecessor bridge controls, strict lint, fmt,

packet plus inventory binds exact source, recipe and image hashes, verifies
32 receipt metadata refusal controls and preserves the earlier packets and

## Retain the checked role files without mistaking content for authority

The next [local package](../testing/performance/0.74/held-role-files-plan-20261020.md)
tests a smaller prerequisite than original launch. A signed receipt plus caller
bytes does not retain the object whose content was checked. PinnedRoles consumes

and their kernel stamps. Four exact immutable seals, read-only access, CLOEXEC
and rejection of O_PATH are mandatory. Receipt hashes, bounded ELF headers,
distinct role identities and signed lock/log must agree.

Full hashing uses a fixed 64 KiB buffer and positional reads rather than seeking
the shared open-file description. Tests change an alias's offset concurrently
with revalidation and verify that checks still read the entire intended content.
A writable alias of the same sealed file cannot modify bytes. Metadata changes,
swapped roles, missing seals and changed expectations refuse; restoring a correct
argument cannot revive the refused object. Thirty-two seeded content corruptions
exercise both roles. These are kernel/content correctness observations, not
throughput, CPU or allocation measurements.

The verification harness itself also needs a failure model. GNU 1.94 panics in
its diagnostic renderer for one short compile-fail example, but rustdoc reports
the example as successful because compilation failed. That result cannot prove
the intended missing capability. Multi-line formatting reproduces the panic.
The FD-extraction control instead tests the absent IntoRawFd trait with explicit
E0277, while start requires E0599. The recipe also refuses compiler-panic output.
An independent xtask lint failure concerns two source-list helpers unused by an
older bridge; narrow test-only annotations preserve strict warnings elsewhere.

Content, provenance and authority remain different facts. The new owned files
contain synthetic ELF fixtures authenticated by synthetic test keys. They are
not the running host, installed helper or evidence of protected build production.
No descriptor extraction or launch API follows from PinnedRoles. The following
join must consume the same original FixedPlacement and admitted policy/epoch,
with original role claims and the complete unchanged validation frame. Only
after that join can bootstrap/process binding and authenticated delivery advance.
All-writer cessation, durable completion and same-attempt reconnect remain
separate gates; this package performs no server or supervisor operation.

At selected source 82570db8 each Linux compiler passes two rounds of all 26

Windows retains sixteen controls in two rounds and two older examples. Twelve
source guards, three predecessor bridge checks, strict lint, registry/docs and

## Bind provenance to the signed attempt without inventing live authority

Retaining immutable role files closes a content race, but the old placement

signature does not make a mismatched epoch, policy, receipt or role acceptable.
Another valid attempt remains valid data but cannot match the retained original
placement bytes. This is a binding check, not a new replay permission.

The audit keeps two authority sources distinct. Original validation obtains the
active policy epoch from the retained registry/kernel input and checks original
clock bounds. The portable inspector sees signed claims and reviewed input
assertions only. The current reviewed module has no held-runtime builder/policy
pin, so this change cannot enroll one or manufacture a successful live join.
That admission, the consumed original frame/object join and real-image hashing
attribution remain required before delivery. No server, supervisor, product
execution or numerical performance claim follows from the new format.

At selected source c24f460a, Windows passes two rounds of 28 tests and four

## Select held trust independently, then borrow the original authority

The next boundary is verifier selection. Correct v4 signatures prove only what
the selected keys signed; accepting a held-policy pin supplied with that same
packet would let the packet choose its own trust. The
[fixed-input implementation](../testing/performance/0.74/held-runtime-trust-plan-20261020.md)
instead reads a separate protected root configuration. There is no public path,
UID, key or pin override, no compiled held-key default and no configuration
writer. The reviewed controller, old builder and worker issuer stay fixed; the
root-selected held builder must be distinct from all three. Actual production
selection and enrollment are not performed by this package.

The source retains descriptors for the root, ancestors and bounded canonical
file, not just parsed strings. Every revalidation compares held and named kernel
objects, ownership/modes, stamps and bytes. Replacing a leaf with identical bytes
is still replacement. Restoring the original file or permissions after refusal
cannot revive the owner. The implementation reuses the unchanged trusted-input
walk/read checks; it does not invent looser filesystem rules. A development test
incorrectly treated existing permitted group-read mode 0640 as unsafe. Correcting
that test to group-write mode 0660 preserves the actual contract rather than
tightening a fixture until it accidentally tests a different policy.

OriginalHeldTrust then borrows the same SignedControllerInput and held source.
Policy inspection observes the actual controller key and active worker authority
digest, epoch, revision and trust snapshot, plus the original request digest.
Both sides are freshly revalidated around verification. No cached checked policy
replaces these observations, and any error poisons both the new source and the
original controller/kernel/authority chain. The held key and held-policy digest
come from the retained root source, never from incoming v4 contents.

The adversarial control is not merely a corrupted signature. Synthetic fixtures
produce correctly signed v4 documents for another reservation request,
controller run, identity or worker policy. Static inspection accepts those
documents as well-formed signed data, while the early original-request join
refuses each one. Healthy controls use a real local kernel packet and retained
active authority, but synthetic keys and owned temporary configuration roots.
They do not enroll the machine or execute the represented build artifacts.

This closes an early read-only selection/request boundary, not the later
consuming join with FixedPlacement, retained role files and the complete original
frame. The returned Inspection remains static data, not a policy/FD original or
start capability. Protected production build, role-image hashing attribution,
authenticated delivery, both guardians Armed, active collector custody and
all-writer cessation are still distinct gates. No clock origin, live check,
46-bracket contract or 300/60/10 bound is changed. No numerical CPU, allocation,
throughput or server-readiness claim follows from these correctness tests.

At frozen source d2cfdf23 GNU 1.94/MSRV 1.88 each pass two rounds of the 26 new
controls and 38 preceding integration controls, plus five new and six preceding
capability examples without compiler panic. Windows retains two 28-test rounds
and four examples. Sixteen exact source/adapter guards preserve all 442 preceding

[separate packet](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/held-runtime-trust-20261020/README.md)

This is an early authority-selection correctness result, not an end-to-end

The separate sealed packet contains 59 hashed members plus inventory. Forty

and the qualification digest remain unchanged. This verifies the scope and

## Consume placement and role custody without exporting a retry owner

An original request inspection and retained role files are still separate facts
until one owner retains both with the actual placement/frame. The
[consuming implementation](../testing/performance/0.74/held-consuming-join-plan-20261020.md)
moves FixedPlacement, PinnedRoles and the independent fixed held source into a
private holder. The constructor cannot replace these with hashes, a caller's
snapshot or another key. Failure keeps the consumed objects in an opaque failed
holder instead of returning a fresh attempt. On Drop, explicit retirement comes
first; the old placement/original custody drops before the role descriptors and
new trust source. No send/start, replay, original extraction or unlock follows.

Each new validation uses two constant-depth rounds. An unchanged complete
FixedPlacement frame opens the round; fresh held trust/provenance inspection and
full checks of the retained role files follow; another unchanged complete frame
closes it. Final original clocks therefore follow hashing. This adds four frame
calls rather than removing any live leaf, and keeps the original 46 brackets and
300/60/10 origins/deadlines. Its cost still needs attribution on the privileged
path; a correctness-only model is not evidence that the extra work fits a live
admission window. No deadline is enlarged to accommodate the composition.

The provenance check deliberately compares more than executable hashes. A second
valid receipt can describe the same two images but a different signed build log.
The private adapter matches the full consumed VerifiedBuild statement against
the receipt freshly verified through the fixed held source. It then reuses the
unchanged seal, descriptor, positional hash and metadata checks. V4 must preserve
the exact signed v3 placement bytes, tying it to the same original consent/root
constraints. Actual request and authority revision/epoch/policy/trust snapshot
remain stable across rounds; no cached evidence substitutes for fresh checks.

The local tests distinguish three levels. The production type and exact original
owner projection compile. Orchestration probes exercise eight stage cuts and
184 modeled leaf refusals across four frames, consuming signatures and failed
holder/drop ordering. Separate tests use actual kernel input, active authority
and sealed memfds to check healthy revalidation, exact placement bytes, source
replacement, real metadata drift and different valid receipt provenance. These
tests use synthetic signers and documents and do not construct the complete
privileged FixedPlacement holder. Its end-to-end healthy/fault run, attribution
and later SIGKILL/lost-ACK checks remain distinct gates before server admission.

The first frozen GNU cohort adds a separate caution: both new 16-test rounds
pass, but a preceding trust test fails its exact expected-error assertion on the
second round. That assertion did not log the unexpected value, so its cause
cannot be assigned retrospectively to a clock, scheduling or product defect.
The implementation preserves the assertion and every runtime check. A test-only
wrapper calls the same old function under the existing first-kernel-refusal
recorder; eight fresh samples pass without a recorded kernel refusal. They do
not explain the earlier failure. First logs and recipe remain distinct from the
later confirmed cohort, and the unclassified refusal remains a qualification
risk rather than a reason to enlarge a timeout or accept another error kind.

The next diagnostic does capture a specific refusal: two original realtime

kernel guard correctly rejects clock-order. Temporarily stopping only the

The follow-up fixture holds one continuously observed WSL process through the

That single-session experiment still fails the original clock-order guard even

The final result therefore has a deliberate split. The consuming production

The next hypothesis was environmental: can the same binaries satisfy the

The next local fixture constructs the actual consuming holder rather than

product worker is sent or executed.

This composition first caught a fixture error: its historical builder document

retains custody and the fence; restoring trust bytes cannot repair a poisoned
holder. Dropping original custody terminates the observed collector/custodian
processes and yields pipe EOF while the independent fence stays held. These
are useful end-to-end ownership observations, not completed SIGKILL/lost-ACK,
later-cell or production-admission gates.

GNU's evidence remains different. A corrected-input cohort overlapped the full
contract suite and refused original time checks during preparation. That
overlap is not proof of causation. A separately registered serial control passes
healthy, revalidate and role-before, then sees an unclassified Kernel(Invalid)
before the next mutation. The final trace records a same-boot clock-order
refusal: original boottime moves forward while the two retained realtime
samples are out of order. A separate healthy attribution passes, but cannot
replace the failed matrix. Identifying that sample's predicate does not identify
the sole WSL clock actor or explain every previous untraced error.

Cost observation is separated from functional execution. Individual phase
measurements record placement, fixed-slice and consuming wall time and CPU of
the current process, excluding child CPU. The fixture uses two 128-byte ELF
images, so these measurements cannot establish production-image hashing cost,
product throughput or allocation improvement. Original admission clocks and
deadlines remain authoritative; an observer never rescues a refusal.

The report vocabulary also matters for recovery design. The first marker said
guardians_terminal, although the assertions polled collector/custodian pidfds.
It is corrected to custodians_terminal without changing those assertions or
rewriting raw logs. Independent root guardians may remain alive to retain the
fence after writers have stopped; their process exit must not be inferred from
custodian exit or from later test cleanup. That distinction prevents monitoring
from announcing completion or releasing resources on the wrong observation.

All preceding source bodies and original checks are retained, and the combined
local gate stays red despite the successful MSRV matrix. Stable native Linux
privileged control is the next environment boundary; joined real SIGKILL,
lost acknowledgement, delivery, all-writer lifecycle and reconnect verification
must still follow before launch permission can be considered.

## Native placement expiry before the consuming join

The authorized privileged native Linux control changes the diagnosis of the
next blocker without erasing any WSL evidence. It uses the same hash-bound
GNU and MSRV release test images, a root-owned temporary staging directory,
a uniquely owned cgroup subtree and a private mount namespace. No clock or
service setting changes, release installation, manager start message or product
traffic is involved. Each compiler receives one full matrix invocation, with
unchanged checks, original origins and admission deadlines; there is no retry.

Both invocations stop on the first healthy case while binding signed placement.
GNU records the causal window expired at age 10,120,568,145 ns. MSRV records
custody expiry at 10,014,035,477 ns. These are single diagnostic observations
against the original ten-second bound, not latency estimates or optimization
claims. The captured kernel-refusal reports are null. Unlike the traced WSL
sample, the observed refusal is expiry; the result neither establishes global
clock stability nor identifies one implementation cost as the cause.

The first custody observations already occur at ages 9,126,504,822 ns and
9,165,257,066 ns. Much of the window has therefore elapsed before the observed
placement operation can finish. Crucially, this run never constructs the new
FixedPlacement or enters the consuming held-role join. Attributing its failure
to that join's four frames or full-role hashing would be unsupported. The next
measurement must separate earlier preparation/enrollment and placement costs,
including their existing full validation rounds. It must preserve the original
checks and cannot turn a profiling clock into an admission clock.

Failing at this boundary is the correct safety behavior. Extending a deadline,
resetting an origin or treating a partial matrix as a pass would hide the cost
instead of explaining it. The raw streams, exits, image identities and failed
healthy reports remain a separate negative server packet. Independent postflight
finds the same running supervisor, installed executable and receipt, unchanged
host mount table and no remaining owned fixture cgroups or roots. Passing those
safety and evidence checks does not close the execution gate. Joined SIGKILL,
lost acknowledgement, all-writer lifecycle and reconnect remain behind a healthy
complete composition rather than being attempted on this refused owner.

## Separating preparation cost from allocation requests

The next local experiment measures the actual holder after the original challenge,
with separate phases for consent preparation/acceptance, outputs, enrollment
frame, fixed manager message, root guardians, enrollment and placement. Each
original call remains in place. An inactive observer reads no profiling clock;
an active observer records wall time, current-process CPU and the existing
authentication/live/kernel spans. Descendant CPU and cold setup are outside
these per-phase CPU totals. Overlapping spans are not additive exclusive CPU,
and their unexplained remainder cannot be assigned to I/O.

This observer must preserve refusal as carefully as a fault harness. Tests verify
one original call, the same value/error and panic identity, balanced nested
counters and restoration of an outer capture. A missing or out-of-order CPU
observation produces no CPU value; it cannot replace the original panic or
rescue an admission refusal. The profiling clock is never a guard clock.

The retained-image local baseline refuses on both compilers. GNU reaches the
consuming method but later reports causal expiry; MSRV records clock-order
earlier in preparation. Three subsequent instrumented attempts per compiler
return GNU 101/0/0 and MSRV 0/0/101. These are independent cost observations,
not successful replacements for either baseline or the refused native cohort.

In all six instrumented outputs phases, the decoder of freshly read proc status
enters 39,744 times. Its inclusive instrumented wall span is 251–335 ms, while
outputs process CPU is 5.397–6.606 seconds. This identifies a repeatedly reached
piece of work without establishing it as the main cause of expiry. These clock
observations describe their own domains; they are not a CPU-utilization ratio
or an exclusive cost decomposition.

The first isolated allocation hypothesis is deliberately narrow. The status
decoder formats five strings for the constant prefixes Pid, Tgid, Uid, Gid and
Groups on every call. Replacing those strings with borrowed literal prefixes
does not reuse any proc value. Both status reads, parsing, numeric/cardinality
and group-budget checks, field order, first-refusal behavior and all original
live frames remain unchanged. A frozen complete decoder is the differential
reference, with seeded malformed inputs and matching refusal sites.

Before implementation, paired controls with identical decoders record ten Rust
allocation requests and 120 requested bytes per decode of the same two-group
fixture on both arms;
the new reduction assertion correctly fails. After implementation, all three
paired samples per compiler record five requests and 80 bytes for the candidate,
versus the same ten/120 reference. Reallocations remain zero. Equal warm-up and
alternating arm order are used, and timing runs separately with allocation
counting disabled. Five vector allocations remain: this is not an allocation-free
decoder or a measurement of libc allocation, RSS or total preparation memory.

The confirmed effect is removal of five temporary allocations and 40 requested
bytes per decode in the diagnostic tool. It is not a numerical latency or
throughput claim for HydraCache's RESP/native API, and it does not explain away
the much larger mandatory context-validation cost. No deadline is extended,
origin reset, predicate skipped or cost shifted into a cache API. Full phase
and functional observations remain separate from this leaf acceptance.

Historical-source checks also need honest failure attribution. Linux Git first
cannot follow this Windows worktree's absolute gitdir pointer. Explicit read-only
Linux Git context fixes access without editing the worktree metadata. The old
20 guards then pass, but a new audit correctly refuses its mistaken expected
count: the snapshot contains 462 files, not 450. Correcting that metadata covers
all 446 runtime and 16 support files; it changes no runtime or admission limit.
The reviewed GNU/MSRV executables remain byte-identical across that correction.

Exact reversible adapters reconstruct every preceding source body and holder
assertion outside the named observation wrappers and literal-prefix substitution.
This is stronger evidence of unchanged guards than a green timing sample alone.
It still cannot substitute for a new authorized native control, authenticated
delivery, joined SIGKILL/lost-ACK, all-writer lifecycle or reconnect. Those gates
remain distinct from a useful but limited allocation improvement.

The reviewed cost attempts return GNU 0/0/0 and MSRV 101/0/0, but neither
unprofiled five-case matrix passes. GNU refuses healthy before completion; MSRV
completes healthy and refuses while preparing the separate revalidate case,
before that case's target held revalidation. Both retain a same-boot clock-order
observation at the original kernel predicate. No cost sample is spliced into a
missing functional case, no matrix is retried and no window is extended.

Boot identities also differ between separate local invocations. Passing a warm
cost probe therefore cannot establish one stable clock context or diagnose the
sole WSL clock actor. The earlier native expiry remains a separate unclosed
observation, not a result that this local allocation change has corrected.
The honest next boundary is cost attribution of the remaining fresh kernel
observations and a separately authorized native control, with the same live
checks and deadlines. Original delivery, joined process-death/lost-ACK, lifecycle
and reconnect work must not inherit a launch permit from this leaf improvement.

## Attributing fresh kernel observations without caching them

Fresh kernel checks are not interchangeable with repeated parsing of a retained
snapshot. A sender can exit, a namespace can change, a pathname can point at a
different object, and an originally pinned descriptor can become uncertain.
The next [local attribution](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/fresh-kernel-cost-20261020/README.md)
therefore keeps the actual origin and sender validators intact and measures
their nested operations. Separate controls observe pidfd liveness, bounded status
reads, metadata and filesystem type checks. They execute no product or original
start and grant no admission authority.

Three baseline batches per compiler use 64 iterations each. Every sender batch
still performs 128 origin checks, 256 boot checks, 512 namespace opens, 128 pidfd
checks, 128 projections and 512 nested document reads. The nested origin spans
occupy 2.14 to 2.67 ms across the six baseline sender batches. Their boot and
namespace spans overlap the enclosing origin span: adding them would count the
same work twice. Standalone leaf timings are also not extra components to add
to a sender batch. Current-process CPU is observed separately and includes all
threads; it is not exclusive kernel CPU or a syscall trace.

This attribution confirms that fresh context validation is a substantial part
of sender validation. It does not justify replacing live reads with cached values,
opening fewer namespace objects, omitting retained-versus-named comparisons or
resetting a deadline. The small confirmed avoidable cost is different: both
literal status open sites construct a new `CString` for the same seven bytes,
including the NUL terminator. The already existing fixed opener performs the
same openat and proc filesystem verification using a borrowed C string.

The single runtime candidate routes those two sites to that helper. The
dynamic PID pathname remains dynamic; document buffers and projection vectors
remain owned as before. O_NOFOLLOW, O_CLOEXEC, O_NONBLOCK, object identity,
fresh reads, numeric/group parsing, pidfd checks and the original validation
order are unchanged. A red test first establishes that the runtime sites have
not yet adopted the measured helper; it must become green independently of
the paired allocation control.

Each compiler compares three alternating pairs of 1024 opens after equal warmup.
The dynamic primitive makes 1024 Rust allocation requests for 7168 bytes; the
fixed primitive makes none, with zero reallocations on both arms. That is one
temporary request and seven requested bytes removed per explicit status open,
not a zero-allocation sender. Timing uses a separate uncounted loop. Its mixed
baseline directions do not support a numerical latency improvement, and these
short local batches must not be extrapolated to placement or API throughput.

The post-candidate controls repeat the same allocation result on both compilers;
the two runtime bindings pass and all 72 before/after phase rows preserve their
fresh call counts. Twelve allocation pairs are retained across the two cohorts.
The 347 source/contract tests and both compiler lanes' targeted functional/lint
checks pass. These checks accept the isolated pathname allocation removal, not
the earlier refused full execution matrix.

The preservation argument combines live differential tests with source guards.
The tests compare the opened object and descriptor flags, preserve missing-name,
symlink, non-directory and non-proc refusals, and show that repeated document
reads observe changed bytes. Exact adapters reconstruct the preceding runtime
by reversing only the two calls, helper visibility and named test hooks. No
whole validator body is excluded; unrelated changes to liveness, filesystem,
projection or packet-hold checks remain visible.

Allocation acceptance remains separate from execution readiness. The earlier
clock-order and native expiry refusals remain retained; these controls do not
rerun the full lifecycle, SIGKILL/lost-ACK or reconnect matrix. The next larger
optimization needs evidence for another avoidable cost, not permission to skip
fresh observations. All original deadlines and independent launch gates remain
in force.

## Formatting each process key without retaining it

The next [local control](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/pid-path-cost-20261020/README.md)
tests a different temporary object: the process-directory pathname. Each
original credential PID becomes a decimal String, then a CString, before the
fresh proc directory opens. This is key construction, not evidence of process
identity. Reusing a previously validated process object would change the safety
argument; constructing the same decimal key anew in stack storage does not.

The baseline and stack prototype use the same proc root, actual PID, directory
flags and checked openat/fstatfs/close path. Equal warmup and three alternating
allocation pairs are measured per compiler. For the baseline three-digit PIDs,
GNU records two requests and 14 requested bytes per open; MSRV records two and
12. The prototype records zero in all six baseline pairs, with no reallocations.
The byte difference between compilers is precisely why a guessed universal byte
budget would be misleading. Every result retains its actual PID, digit count
and standard-library lane. Allocation requests are Rust-thread observations,
not libc allocation, RSS or total attempt memory.

The candidate derives the key on every call in twelve bytes: up to ten
magnitude digits, an optional minus and one terminal NUL. `unsigned_abs` handles
MIN safely. Generated digits and minus are nonzero and fit before the untouched
terminal byte; the CStr conversion remains checked. Edge cases and 16384 seeded
i32 values compare the full decimal/sign/NUL representation with the standard
formatter. This is not an exhaustive traversal of every i32 value.

Adoption moves the complete measured formatter body into runtime without
rewriting it. Both private callers pass their same original credential PID;
neither pathname nor observed process state is retained as a cache. The generic
string opener stays as the differential test reference, with no remaining
production string caller. Identity, FD flags and missing/non-directory/symlink/
non-proc refusals are checked independently. Existing open, filesystem,
metadata, status, projection and pidfd checks keep their original ordering.

The preservation proof is deliberately mechanical. An audit compares the new
formatter with the frozen baseline prototype byte-for-byte. Exact reverse
substitutions recover the preceding method, both caller expressions, reference
annotations and named test hooks. Every other preceding validator statement
must still match; no old body or assertion is excluded. The actual runtime
binding first refuses before adoption and must pass after it.

Separate uncounted timing and unchanged fresh-kernel phase controls remain
observations, not an accepted speedup. Removing two pathname allocations cannot
establish that a ten-second placement window now passes. Full functional
composition, original delivery, joined writer-death/lost-ACK and reconnect still
need their independent gates. This experiment performs no server, installation,
supervisor/clock service or product workload operation.

The post-candidate controls confirm two to zero requests and the same 14/12 to
zero requested bytes for their three-digit keys. Both runtime bindings pass,
all 72 phase rows preserve their original call counts, and all 12 allocation
pairs are retained. The 350 source/contract tests and both compiler lanes'
functional/lint checks pass. These results accept the uncached pathname
allocation change while keeping the independent execution gates closed.

tests whether the large Boot and Namespace wall owners still allocate. It calls

complete Origin revalidation. The existing opt-in allocator observes Rust
allocation requests on the current thread. A separate pass reads kernel I/O
counters, and a third pass checks the original kernel observation counts;
none of these captures overlap. Each case has 32 warmups and three batches
of 1024 operations on GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88.

The negative allocation result is useful: boot comparison, every namespace
opener and full Origin request zero Rust allocations/reallocations on both
compilers. Replacing another temporary Rust buffer cannot reduce requests
already absent from these successful paths. Their fresh filesystem checks
remain required. Boot reads once per comparison and Origin twice per complete
revalidation; namespace opens have no read requests, but still open and inspect
kernel objects. With no installed strace or perf, these counters cannot count
all syscalls or assign time to open/stat/close.

The authority control uses the actual shared journal inspection engine with
synthetic signed policies under a private nonroot temporary root. One journal
contains one active generation; the other ends active after three explicit
refuse/advance pairs, giving seven generations. Setup and durable publication
are outside capture. All three samples on each compiler give identical counts:

| Fixture authority inspect | Allocations per operation | Reallocations per operation | Requested bytes per operation | Read requests per operation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| One generation | 68 | 11 | 3014 | 4 |
| Seven generations | 184 | 59 | 13292 | 28 |

Requested bytes include realloc sizes and do not measure retained memory.
Read counts subtract the independently observed empty counter bracket; raw
character counters are not converted into workload or disk bytes. No measured
batch writes. Fixed production ancestry and WorkerTrustInput's surrounding
checks are absent from this fixture, so the table cannot establish the cost
or a potential saving for the entire ActiveAuthority step. Two depths also
cannot establish a general linear scaling law.

The result narrows the next experiment to authority representation work:
issuer-key formatting, temporary leaf names, inventory sets and context
ownership. Each needs its own control before a candidate is accepted. It does
not justify retaining a previous authority result or skipping any inventory,
metadata, pin or epoch check. No runtime candidate or latency gain is adopted.

Both lanes pass 47 focused tests, check and strict clippy; 361 historical and
two new source/contract controls pass. The initial report parser rejects a
harness-prefixed origin line, then reprocesses the original successful logs
after an exact-prefix repair; no measurement is repeated. The existing live
clock-order failures remain independent closed gates. There is no server,
installation, supervisor control, clock/service change or product workload.

## One issuer key encoder with a conserved allocation reduction

The [authority issuer-key experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/local-runs/authority-key-hex-20261020/README.md)

owned lowercase key. The existing `crate::hex` reserves the final capacity and
fills one string. Both return the same owned 64-byte public key representation;
neither changes which issuer is trusted or how often its pin is checked.

The baseline remains unchanged while tests compare 256 seeded public keys,

refusals. One healthy binding and 12 altered issuer/policy/epoch/host/namespace

change to `crate::hex`; no inventory, path ownership or context clone is changed

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| Complete fixture inspect with 1 generation | 68 to 37 | 11 to 8 | 3014 to 2710 |
| Complete fixture inspect with 7 generations | 184 to 153 | 59 to 56 | 13292 to 12988 |

## Reopening journal leaves without cloning their names

The [leaf name control](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-leaf-name-plan-20261020.md)
first separates parse-time ownership from repeated inspection. `history` parses
records while opening the journal. The retained `ActiveAuthority` path calls
`inspect`, which reopens and compares original leaf objects but does not parse
them again. Removing a context clone in `Record::parse` would therefore not
remove requests from this measured repeated-inspect owner. That parse candidate
is deferred for this owner, without claiming it is irrelevant to cold opening.

Inside actual inspection, `Leaf::revalidate` clones its retained name only to
call an opening routine that stores another owned name. The temporary object
is then used for its fresh stamp and bytes, not its name. The single candidate
extracts the checked synchronous read into a private borrowed-name helper.
Initial opening still owns the name; repeated validation retains the fresh
File through both comparisons. It keeps original metadata-before-open order,
ownership, mode, device, byte budget, bounded read and final metadata checks.
Directory inventory and all other validation rounds are unchanged.

Frozen owned-open/reference, borrowed-read proposal and actual arms cover
record and commit leaves separately. An early metadata refusal must avoid both
the name copy and reopening. A synthetic wrong retained-name assertion isolates
the failed-open path; it is not a claim that unlinking a real leaf leaves its
original inode stamp unchanged. Independent filesystem faults cover unlink,
rename/replacement, symlink/hardlink, unsafe mode, changed content, ownership
and over-budget reads. A 64-case seeded name/payload corpus includes empty and
full-budget files. Complete inspect must conserve the record-plus-commit leaf
reduction at both tested journal depths, with unchanged fresh observations.

Three samples of 1024 operations on each compiler give identical results:

| Operation | Allocations Before to After | Reallocations Before to After | Requested bytes Before to After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| Commit leaf revalidation, 65-byte payload | 3 to 2 | 0 to 0 | 112 to 89 |
| Early original metadata refusal | 0 to 0 | 0 to 0 | 0 to 0 |
| Synthetic missing retained name | 2 to 1 | 0 to 0 | 43 to 22 |
| Complete fixture inspect with 1 generation | 35 to 33 | 8 to 8 | 2642 to 2598 |
| Complete fixture inspect with 7 generations | 151 to 137 | 56 to 56 | 12920 to 12612 |

Record and commit name clones cost one allocation each, requesting exactly
21 and 23 bytes. Their sum survives complete inspection at both depths: two
allocations/44 requested bytes at one generation and fourteen/308 at seven.
All read counts remain four and 28; every non-authority leaf and fresh kernel
count remains equal. The fresh CString and content allocations still exist.
This locally accepts a specific representation saving, not a claim that fewer
checks or an allocator replacement improved the result. Two depths do not
establish a general scaling law, and requested bytes are not retained memory.

The final compiler lanes pass 191 authority tests each with 12 manual/privileged

constructor accepts no replacement inputs and returns an opaque owner whose

objects explicitly but does not fabricate their identities. It is therefore
not a runnable systemd spec and supplies no send or release permission. Next
materialize and bind those objects under the same owner and an expanded exact
inventory before joining durable transport uncertainty and process binding.
This is a correctness boundary, not a CPU or product throughput improvement.

### Reduce bounded collection growth while preserving the decoder

The next [fresh-check leaf](../testing/performance/0.74/projection-groups-20261021.md)

that iterator directly into Vec grows capacity several times for longer lists.

the number of proc reads nor the retained identity type or caller conversions.

numeric error before the group-budget check, while a valid 33rd integer reaches

field, live predicate, error path and deadline under the earlier source guards.

Before implementation, GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 each measured seven lengths and
256 pure collections per length. Across those 1792 calls, the reference made
1536 allocations, 2560 reallocations and 237568 requested bytes. The candidate
keeps 1536 allocations, requests no reallocations and totals 93184 bytes. The
empty list still allocates nothing; nonempty results keep the same owned values.
Reference counts after wiring agree with the earlier baseline.

This result supports an allocation-only candidate, not a speed claim. The local
scratch and final copy also have cost, and these controls do not time it or the
full validator. CPU, RSS, retained memory and ten-second admission headroom are
not inferred from requested bytes. No original-owner attempt is repeated, and

Ownership matters as much as the byte count. The actual helper supplies the

The result supports keeping this allocation leaf, not a claim that preparation

### Separate peer vector growth from canonicalization

The [collector peer baseline](../testing/performance/0.74/collector-peer-baseline-20261021.md)

and deduplicated. The final value remains owned and retains uid. Even when
primary is already present or duplicates collapse to one group, the current
push first grows a nonempty exact-capacity copy. The empty case instead makes
its first allocation at push.

GNU 1.94 and MSRV 1.88 agree on 7936 allocations, 7680 reallocations and
1798144 requested bytes across the same 31 cases and 256 constructions each.
A separate one-construction stage control for each case conserves those
requests between to_vec and push. Sort/dedup makes no allocator request on the
corpus; that is not a claim that canonicalization takes no CPU. At input length
32, growth leaves capacity 64 even when dedup shortens the result. An absent
primary still produces a complete 33-group union, not a truncated value.

The controls compare canonical values with an independent BTreeSet oracle,
including 1024 seeded cases, integer extremes, unchanged inputs and independent
owned outputs. Generic cases beyond the 32-group input limit test the helper,
not admission. The complete surrounding wrapper is frozen separately with
synthetic sender/time/hold receivers: first errors, peer work between both
sender checks, final time extraction, latching and refused reentry all retain
their order. Source reversal recovers the entire production body; no actual
KernelPacket or clock is exercised.

First test compile and capability-canary failures remain in evidence. Explicit
usize and owned labels outside measurement repair those tests without changing

windows/refusals remain. The result supports a later isolated capacity-reserve
experiment, not a runtime change or saved preparation time. No live/server run
or material/fault/readiness promotion follows from this allocation baseline.

### Reject an allocation saving that makes the getter more expensive

The [owned inline boot experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/sample-boot-inline-20261022.md)

higher getter medians on both compilers reject adoption despite allocation

they are 54800/2183900 ns. Getter loops allocate nothing, and capture is inactive
during timing. The inline path repeatedly validates UTF-8, while String already
offers a valid str view; that is a plausible explanation of the leaf overhead,
not an instruction-level attribution or measured full-path regression.

The candidate is therefore not adopted. A lower allocation count alone does not

### Separate retained evidence from temporary fresh read storage

The [fresh authority read audit](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-read-audit-20261022.md)

The surrounding read protocol constrains that hypothesis. Before metadata must

and drop need their own baseline. Pure generic-reader measurements cannot stand

Eleven offline mutation controls enforce the source boundary; a development
mutation also improved the auditor by separating stamp declarations from their
constructor fields. Sixteen earlier seals and 928 members preserve the rejected

### Reuse fresh-read storage without reusing the observation

The [owner-bound scratch experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-scratch-reuse-20261022.md)

cohort: eight releases/4776 bytes. Fragmented, binary and Interrupted reading

The tradeoff is explicit: an additional successful body allocation remains live

Seven first paired wall intervals per case retain every slower pair and outlier.

Semantic evidence includes 64 warm-cache first-error masks, 1512 IO schedules,

controls preserve the source/error/evidence boundary. The original no-clobber

### Put the allocation saving back into its owner graph

The [scratch owner audit](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-scratch-owner-audit-20261022.md)
finds why a successful leaf experiment is not yet an integration patch. The
journal owns two Leaves per generation and keeps all prior entries through
append and refusal. Fixed, trust, kernel and signed readers borrow that original
journal rather than duplicating it. There is no demonstrated process-wide owner
limit behind the per-journal generation bound.

At 128 generations, 256 successful caches filled to their individual budgets
would retain up to 270464 additional bytes per journal. The previous standalone
32-byte wrappers would add another 8192 bytes, but that is not an embedded Leaf
layout measurement. Original bytes, parsed history, allocator overhead, transient
growth and OS residency remain separate. Allocations saved over many calls must
not be reported as memory that no longer exists.

The borrowed prototype cannot become a field of its own Leaf or persist across
entries Vec relocation without a different ownership design. Per-round scratch
would lose cross-round amortization. An owned-storage candidate needs explicit
mutable receivers/split borrows and its own layout measurement; interior
mutability or a cross-owner pool is not an automatic substitute.

Leaf-local eviction is also narrower than journal refusal. A directory/inventory
error, later trust bind or external latch can occur without revisiting every
cache. A future multi-entry model must clear all temporary caches while keeping
original expected bytes/descriptors and every fresh validation bracket. It must
also preserve the distinction between durable refused data with an explicit
operator epoch transition and a permanently failed original owner.

The offline audit and ten mutation tests retain nineteen prior seals/1076 members
and all first scratch observations without rerunning the measurement image.
Next test owned storage and whole-journal eviction in isolation; the runtime is
unchanged, and no full-path or server admission follows from capacity arithmetic.

The [unapplied owned-storage candidate](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-storage-source-20261022.md)

### Exercise the installed storage candidate on the real filesystem

The [runtime integration](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-20261022.md)
now installs the exact guarded fixture and mutable observer rather than only
parsing a proposed patch. Each Leaf owns optional scratch, but still opens and
reads the named file freshly and checks original metadata, stamp and bytes.
Reuse changes storage selection, not the truth source. All five refusal
boundaries evict every retained slot while preserving original authority objects
and history; publication order and fsync boundaries remain intact.

Native correctness matters separately from source equivalence. Rust 1.94 and
MSRV 1.88 each compile/check/lint the actual engine and pass 33 exact filesystem
tests. Seven new tests exercise poisoned storage, bounded retention, ten leaf
refusals, whole-journal cleanup, successful transitions, reopen and publication
cuts. Reopen inherits no buffer, while its unchanged final validation may warm
a new one. Logical publication cuts establish no real process-loss or lost-ACK
proof by themselves.

Integration exposed more source-test coupling than the first guard list showed.
The complete development cohort first passed 290 with 31 failures; adapting
those readers exposed fifteen older consumers of the changed root/support
sources. A focused cohort then found the remaining custody dependency chain.
The final boundary covers fifty exact single reader edits and root imports.
Every complete approved current file is verified before a pinned predecessor
reaches the old assertions; independent raw-current checks still validate the
installed candidate. No assertion is weakened or failed test removed. The
frozen final cohort passes all 321 contract tests, with the earlier negative
results retained under their original phases.

This step also makes the memory tradeoff explicit. Retaining a successful read
may remove later allocation churn, but it keeps additional storage alive per
Leaf. Capacity bounds and eviction are correctness properties, not evidence of
lower RSS or faster preparation. A fresh current-runtime attribution must
measure both sides before claiming a gain; old synthetic model timings cannot
be attached to the newly installed engine.

The evidence identifies committed source, exact test selection, executable
hashes, raw logs and stable per-cohort metadata. Development and final WSL boots
differ, while both final compiler lanes share one boot; they are not described
as a single timing session. The nineteen-step Windows gate, 79 historical
canaries and native results close local integration only. Original live checks,
deadlines, first refusals and qualification remain fixed. Full SIGKILL/lost-ACK,
all-writer revocation, reconnect and server enrollment remain distinct gates;
no server, service/clock, supervisor or product action occurred.

### Fewer allocations can mean more live memory

The [installed-engine experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-allocation-20261022.md)
measures the actual owned-storage implementation against its exact pre-install
engine, not the old model. Five fresh-process pairs per compiler, Rust 1.94 and
MSRV 1.88, use the same signed synthetic corpus, seed, filesystem history and
32 full inspections per cell. Reopen, warm checks, refusal, sticky refusal,
maximum publication and owner drop are separate accounting phases. Existing
runtime/test bodies and all live checks stay intact; common instrumentation
is added only to isolated source overlays.

Both compiler lanes repeat the same allocation and layout counts in every pair.
At depth 127 a warm inspect changes from 1,353 to 1,099 allocations and from
132,606 to 45,346 requested bytes. The count reduction is exactly two buffers
per generation, one per record/commit Leaf. Fresh files, metadata, stamps,
content comparison, inventory and parsing still execute; the remaining 1,099
allocations are not hidden or classified as free. This is evidence of storage
reuse, not evidence that validation became proportionally faster.

The price is measurable. Live owner requested layouts rise from 197,223 to
290,627 bytes at that depth: 87,260 retained scratch bytes and 6,144 additional
bytes in the entry vector. Leaf grows 136 to 160 bytes and Entry 272 to 320;
spare vector capacity costs memory too. Cold reopen has the same 10,708
alloc/alloc_zeroed calls in both roles and increases cumulative requested bytes
from 1,621,196 to 1,633,292. Its original closing validation already warms the
new scratch slots. The mechanism helps subsequent checks; it does not make a
new owner cheaper to construct or reduce its live memory.

Accounting realloc correctly is essential: a successful realloc requests a
new layout and releases its old one. Across open, warm, publication, refusal,
sticky inspection and final drop, every measured owner balances to zero.
All five refusal boundaries clear scratch, including binding/transition and
partial publication errors. This supports cleanup of requested layouts, not
the stronger claim that malloc returns every freed page to the OS.

RSS tells a different, weaker story. At depth 127 the Rust 1.94 paired RSS
differences are negative, while Rust 1.88 spans both signs. Executable/runtime
pages, fixture production, reporting and allocator residency belong to those
whole-process samples. Their unstable direction cannot overturn the directly
measured increase in owner retention, and it supports no lower-RSS claim.
Keep allocation requests, retained layouts and process residency distinct.

The harness itself needed provenance review. Cargo initially treated installed
as fresh in a shared target and returned the baseline executable. Passing
semantic controls alone did not make that a valid comparison. The attempt
was blocked before measurement; independent role targets, fresh compilation
and different image paths/digests now guard the cohort. Earlier missing fixture,
lint, output-format and cache-copy failures remain visible instead of being
folded into a successful measurement. All twenty first measured processes pass.

The result justifies a narrow statement: repeated full checks allocate less,
at a known retention and cold-construction cost. It does not settle CPU or
end-to-end preparation value, original-start/all-writer revocation, real
SIGKILL/lost-ACK recovery or server admission. No runtime was changed in response
to these results, no old timing claim was carried forward, and all original
windows, live predicates, first refusals and qualification identities remain.
No clock/service change, server, installation, supervisor or product load ran.

### Allocation reuse does not yet establish a CPU or elapsed benefit

The [next actual-runtime experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-cpu-20261022.md)
removes the allocation-counter wrapper and measures fresh release images with
thread CPU and monotonic raw elapsed clocks. Seven counterbalanced pairs on each
of Rust 1.94 and 1.88 retain the exact synthetic signed corpus and full inspections.
Phases separate reopen, 32 inspections, publication, refusal, sticky refusal and
drop. A second cell family times that owner lifecycle continuously, without inner
timers or reporting, so final cleanup cannot disappear from the comparison.
It is a local authority-registry lifecycle, not complete production preparation.

The point estimates are tempting but insufficient. At history depth 127, median
paired warm CPU ratios are 0.888 and 0.733 installed/baseline. Their fixed intervals
are 0.764–1.458 and 0.530–1.193. The complete-cycle elapsed ratios are 1.053 and 0.925,
with intervals 0.554–1.375 and 0.520–1.677. The same data allow both improvements
and costs. Neither primary clears the five-percent descriptive boundary fixed
before measurements; this is not a narrower equivalence or no-regression result.

Phase attribution also preserves the work that buffer reuse cannot remove.
Depth 127 reopen CPU medians (baseline/installed) are 2.783/3.961 ms on 1.94 and
2.643/2.423 ms on 1.88. Publication elapsed medians are 19.488/23.500 ms and
12.967/17.634 ms, larger than
their thread CPU medians, with the original durable work still present. Scratch
eviction costs CPU at terminal refusal, and drop remains inside the continuous
cycle. These observations explain why fewer malloc calls cannot be multiplied
into an assumed whole-path percentage; phase medians are not additive estimates
of the separate cycle's median.

Fixed child affinity did not eliminate paired variability. Empty timer brackets
are retained without subtraction, all seven pairs and both compilers remain,
and before/after load/pressure context is descriptive rather than a filter.
The min/max interval has 98.4375% nominal median coverage for seven IID pairs;
a shared WSL host may violate that assumption. A favorable median is not a
license to discard slow pairs or switch to another depth after seeing the data.

All 28 first measured processes, eight native clock/semantic controls and 23
source controls pass. The result leaves a useful distinction: allocation reuse
and increased live layouts are confirmed mechanisms, while practical CPU and
elapsed value remain unconfirmed here. Runtime is neither optimized nor rolled
back from these observations. Another timing study needs its own frozen method;
original checks, windows, first refusals and qualification identities stay fixed.
No live preparation, clock/service change, server, installation, supervisor or
product workload occurred, and the production delivery/recovery gates remain.

### Saved timing variability separates observations from causes

The [offline follow-up](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-variance-20261022.md)
uses the same sealed 28 processes and 336 rows, not another measurement cohort.
It keeps every pair and reproduces both mixed primary conclusions. Within each
role, depth-127 warm thread CPU maximum/minimum ranges from 1.329 to 1.769. The
spread is therefore not only an elapsed-time wait added to stable CPU work.
That observation still cannot distinguish frequency, kernel/cache effects,
virtualization accounting or a particular runtime cause.

Order sensitivity is another warning against trusting a point estimate. On Rust
1.88 the four baseline-first warm ratios have median 1.163; the three installed-
first ratios have median 0.716. On 1.94 the first three pairs have median 0.817,
the last three 1.245. These are small post hoc diagnostic groups, not alternative
acceptance cohorts. Selecting the favorable group would turn an inconclusive
comparison into a misleading improvement claim. The full lifecycle does not
show the same uniform order pattern, so order is a design concern, not a proven
single explanation for both endpoints.

The elapsed-minus-thread-CPU residual is kept signed. Sequential clock reads and
current-thread scope make it different from pure scheduler or storage waiting.
For the lifecycle, CPU and residual variance can partially cancel: Rust 1.88
baseline has normalized variance terms 1.095 for CPU, 1.431 for residual and
-1.525 for twice their covariance; the unrounded terms sum to one. Treating them
as independent causal percentages would be wrong. Switch/block counters remain
descriptive; a large publication residual does not identify fsync latency or
permit removing a durability operation.

Even within the phased fixture, the largest CPU phase is not always the largest
variance contributor. The 32-inspection batch has median CPU shares of roughly
81–86%, but installed 1.94 has warm/publication covariance contributions of
0.430/0.455 to the measured phase-sum variance. This sum excludes untimed gaps
and is not the independently measured continuous lifecycle. Keeping that
distinction avoids explaining one occurrence with another fixture's medians.

The [next local protocol](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-variance-method-v2-20261022.md)
is prepared, not run: fixed balanced BIIB/IBBI blocks, interleaved compiler order,
unchanged probe/checks/corpus and a finite stopping rule without replacement
samples. Read-only context is timestamped around each child instead of inferred
from file mtimes. Any inner cycle profiling remains a separate instrumented
study with an untouched control. Existing evidence is not retried, reweighted
or promoted; the allocation/retention tradeoff remains confirmed while practical
CPU/end-to-end value and the separate production gates remain unresolved.

### A measurement runner needs refusal tests before measurements

The [balanced runner](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-balanced-runner-20261022.md)
implements the revised 64-process design without collecting another timing
cohort. A complete synthetic schedule checks all positions; mocked preparation,
subprocess and reader tests exercise the surrounding control path. The old probe
and source guards remain unchanged, so improving experiment organization does
not silently reduce the work being compared.

The controls verify that a bad corpus, changed image or context, timeout,
interruption or budget overrun stops the cohort and retains its prefix. A partial
attempt cannot be resumed into a favorable complete result. Reader tests reject
synthetic mode and incomplete/mutated receipts. Boundary ties are compared with
exact squared geometric products, avoiding a floating-point promotion at the
unchanged five-percent boundary. No new performance claim follows from these
control-flow and arithmetic checks.

Even the tests needed boundary review: an initial image/deadline injector fired
on the preceding child's closing guard. The first failures remain retained; the
injector was corrected without removing those checks. The final twenty new
controls pass, but mocked process cleanup is not kernel process-cleanup proof.
Actual native validation and the later measured cohort remain separate steps;
neither the old inconclusive timing result nor server readiness is upgraded.

### Native validation can reveal a portability defect without a benchmark

The [next limited gate](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-native-validation-20261022.md)
builds, lints and checks four fresh Linux images on Rust 1.94 and MSRV 1.88,
but executes none of them. Both 1,869-file dependency seeds retain their sealed
membership/bytes. A separate synthetic leader and descendant exercise the real
timeout adapter; both original pidfds report exit after the owned group is
killed. This validates that ordinary cleanup case, not production all-writer or
cgroup revocation, and supplies no new timing benefit.

The first preflight failed for a different reason: a Windows-sealed inventory
and a Linux Path enumeration ordered README.md and collect.ps1 differently.
All 183 names, lengths and hashes matched. Rewriting the seal would erase the
boundary failure. Instead, the versioned reader explicitly uses the historical
inventory order while preserving safe membership, byte/source/facts checks,
all raw receipts, predecessor and qualification checks. The first refusal stays
visible; no measured observation is reordered or discarded.

The native subset now passes, while compiled-image clock/semantic controls and
the actual balanced cohort remain separate authorizations. Compile receipts,
seed integrity and an ordinary process cleanup proof should not be described as
a performance result or a green production/server release gate.

### A complete balanced cohort can still leave the speed hypothesis unresolved

The [authorized 64-process experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/authority-runtime-balanced-20261022.md)
tests whether the installed scratch reuse has practical CPU and lifecycle value
after balancing role position and interleaving compiler blocks. It changes
neither runtime nor probe: the same full inspections, signed corpus, publication
and refusal semantics remain. Four fresh independent release images pass strict
clippy/check and all eight clock/semantic controls before measurement. Every
scheduled child passes on its first execution; all 768 cell rows are retained.

The result does not turn the known allocation reduction into a speed claim.
Depth-127 warm thread CPU has median installed/baseline block ratios of
0.855 on Rust 1.94 and 0.976 on MSRV 1.88, but ranges of 0.656–1.214 and
0.678–1.055. Continuous lifecycle elapsed ratios are 1.016 and 0.937 with
ranges 0.722–1.313 and 0.731–1.345. Each interval crosses 1. The unchanged rule
requires every block below 0.95 on both compilers for practical benefit, or
every block above 1.05 for cost. Neither primary endpoint meets either rule;
this is also not proof of equivalence or a green release non-regression gate.

The balanced design addresses one concern from the first timing study, not all
sources of variation on a shared WSL machine. Before/after load, PSI and cgroup
samples describe the surroundings; they do not prove a causal scheduler,
frequency or virtualization explanation and cannot justify discarding a block.
The finite experiment therefore ends as planned after one complete cohort.
Collecting more until the median or interval looks favorable would change the
question after seeing its answer. The older cohort stays separate and unchanged.

Cold open, durable publication and terminal work remain part of the assessment.
Refusal clears the scratch and has marginal CPU medians near six microseconds
installed versus roughly one microsecond baseline. That is visible cleanup,
not free work; tiny ratios are also sensitive to clock observation. Lifecycle
timing includes refusal and drop instead of hiding them after the bracket.
The confirmed mechanism remains fewer warm allocation requests at a larger
retained owner-layout cost. Its practical CPU/elapsed value is still unconfirmed
by this method, so neither automatic acceptance nor rollback follows.

Preserving first failures applies to experiment operations too. The operator's
first freeze validation used Windows Python with a WSL-only Git helper and
stopped before publishing a method. Running that same step in the required WSL
context within its original deadline launched the sole cohort. A later offline
collector expected a size field absent from seed manifests; its first source
and refusal are kept with the corrected collector. No build, semantic control
or measured child was retried, and neither mistake rewrote observations.

The packet preserves raw receipts, context, calibration and source inventories;
355 files match their staged Git bytes. Original live checks, deadlines, first
Causal refusals and qualification remain unchanged. No time/service mutation,
server action or product workload occurs. Production original delivery,
all-writer cessation and recovery still need their separate integration gates;
a complete local performance experiment cannot substitute for them.

### Test the real descriptor transport before claiming an execution gate

The next [local manager control](../testing/performance/0.74/held-manager-compat-20261022.md)
finds a compatibility blocker rather than a performance problem. The held owner
already retains release, worker/config, pidfds, alarm and bootstrap roles, but
those objects are not automatically a systemd launch specification. The actual
WSL systemd 255 manager rejects the native ExtraFileDescriptors property. A
single uniquely named transient-unit request confirms the rejection; its unit
is absent before and after. No writer rights or product worker are delivered.

Allowing private temporary services removes a permission boundary, not an API
limitation. Treating a private bus model, version string or empty descriptor
probe as authenticated original delivery would skip the very process/stream/
cgroup binding being tested. The negative control therefore leaves original
delivery and all-writer cessation false and stops before the joined fault matrix.
Existing services/systemd, clocks, original deadlines and live checks stay intact.

The tooling itself exposed two earlier mistakes: scalar-versus-argument-array
JSON decoding and a wrong fixed property interface. Both stopped on read-only
queries, before any unit submission. Their raw failures and sources remain;
captured-response and exact-argv regressions accompany the fixes. Eleven final
offline controls pass per platform, while the one real mutation still ends in
the manager's refusal. These are not retries of a failed launch or evidence of
successful execution.

A separate compatible environment could preserve the native transport design.
A new FD bootstrap receiver could instead support an older manager, but adds
another authenticated peer and extra descriptor copies outside the attempt
cgroup. Its identity, lifetime, deadlines and closure must join the same full
frame and all-writer proof; it is an architectural choice, not a silent fallback.
Neither option by itself supplies durable one-shot delivery, active collection,
safe completion or recovery. Those gates remain explicit.

### Separate transport observations from whole-gate success

The authorized [separate local environment](../testing/performance/0.74/held-wsl-native-20261022.md)
keeps the current Ubuntu/systemd, default WSL and global configuration intact.
A pinned Debian rootfs supplies systemd 257.13; time-agent masks are applied
before its first boot, rather than booting an unreviewed time service and
stopping it afterward. The first preparation rejects an absent Python package.
That is retained as a tooling prerequisite error; a versioned preparation then
separates systemd environment needs from a future Python harness dependency.
No package upgrade or new bootstrap receiver is hidden in this step.

The synthetic descriptor control shows why a binary pass/fail alone is not
enough to explain an experiment, while still keeping release gates boolean.
The first CLI invocation rejects a helper argument as its own option before
delivery. An offline failing regression and explicit option terminator fix that
mistake. The next version makes one real native FD transfer: a fixed nonproduct
helper confirms slot/name/hash, stream identities and its private service cgroup.
It exits successfully. But the harness then reads ControlGroup on the wrong
interface, so the **whole control fails**. Its exact service is stopped and
observed inactive. The query fix is offline only; there is no fresh delivery to
turn the same observation into a favorable result.

The helper's retained output is useful partial evidence that the native API
transfers these synthetic descriptors. It is not evidence of the unobserved
property, nor of a consumed original owner, same retained manager connection,
held executable, release barrier or autonomous all-writer closure. A partial
observation may guide the next implementation without silently promoting a red
gate. No numeric performance gain is measured or claimed here. Original checks,
deadlines and first failures stay fixed; server admission and the complete
SIGKILL/lost-ACK matrix still depend on their actual end-to-end runtime path.

### Bind descriptor roles to the owner before enabling transport

A descriptor inventory and a launch layout answer different questions. The
inventory records which objects are still owned and unchanged; the layout says
which original object would occupy each inherited role. The next
[partial runtime join](../testing/performance/0.74/held-material-role-binding-20261022.md)
binds eight concrete material roles inside the existing inventory snapshot.
It deliberately leaves worker and Armed guardian transport descriptors unresolved
rather than substituting newly opened objects or exposing raw-FD getters.

The complete original context remains beside those bindings: manager/client
names and serial, root identity, signed documents, origins and absolute bounds.
Both inventory observations still execute between the same full validation
rounds. The new leaf computes only values from the fresh census; it makes no
new kernel or bus observation and transfers no descriptor. Retained or closing
role drift therefore refuses under the same owner instead of producing a
reconstructed capability or refreshed deadline.

Tests must inspect the intended candidate too. The first new source canary
accidentally used a historical reader, so it continued to reject the missing
hook in old frozen source after the implementation was present. Correcting only
that canary to read current files separates historical compatibility checks
from actual runtime admission. The first red result remains; current-source
checks reconstruct the unchanged prior full-frame and retirement bodies.

Real local kernel component tests and deterministic model substitutions verify
this partial binding, not original delivery. The next boundary is still concrete:
join the remaining original FDs, prove retained executable addressing and handle
the activation environment without removing the launcher's empty-environment
guard. The synthetic systemd helper's LISTEN_* variables make that mismatch
visible. No timing gain, writer-cessation proof or server readiness follows from
a value-only map; those require their own complete execution path and fault gate.

### Complete role identity without creating a delivery capability

The [next closed census](../testing/performance/0.74/held-complete-role-census-20261022.md)
binds the three remaining inherited roles from the original owners themselves:
the retained worker image and the ordered Armed guardian pidfds. Neither provider
returns a file or descriptor. Instead, it contributes directly to a private
value collector, whose complete result is compared inside the same material
inventory and original validation brackets. No process or manager message is
created by completing the map.

The first kernel component result exposed a useful mistake. The new constructor
assumed distinct tasks must have distinct pidfd inodes. Here two real owned-child
pidfds had different FD numbers and fdinfo PIDs but the same inode. Requiring
inode inequality rejected the healthy fixture before its live checks. Removing
that unsupported new assumption does not remove task identity: exact ordered
PIDs, original descriptors and expected metadata, fresh procfs fdinfo, poll and
closing stamps still have to agree. The first failed candidate remains recorded;
the corrected component tests are not a retry of an original admission attempt.

All eleven role numbers now join 23 specified descriptor entries. That number
does not mean every writer has been enumerated or stopped. It also says nothing
about how the held executable is addressed or whether the manager's activation
environment satisfies the unchanged empty-environment guard. These are the next
delivery prerequisites. A complete layout must not become an implicit permission
to send, renew an expired context, publish completion or release a fence.

Local model/kernel tests cover refusal and retained identity, not speed. There
is no new timing or allocation claim. Preserving the old full-frame observations
and deadlines while adding the census keeps the remaining original-send,
all-writer cessation and fault-matrix gates explicit.

### Validate activation metadata without weakening the launcher

The [explicit activation entry](../testing/performance/0.74/held-activation-ingress-20261022.md)
separates metadata consumption from the held launcher's security contract. It
accepts only the exact current PID, descriptor count and ordered names, refuses
unknown or malformed environment fields, then removes only the three validated
LISTEN variables. The original launcher still sees an empty environment and
runs every old privilege, content, peer, guardian, release and deadline check.
The legacy entry does not silently learn to accept activation metadata.

Local synthetic processes prove this boundary without executing a worker: valid
metadata reaches the old core's expected missing-descriptor refusal, while bad
metadata stops before that core. This is useful evidence of adaptation, not
authenticated systemd delivery. Likewise, post-exec validation cannot prove
what a dynamic loader saw before the program started. Complete pre-exec
environment admission belongs in the future unit boundary.

Executable lookup also cannot be inferred from a completed descriptor map.
The upstream manager orders lookup and descriptor placement differently from
the tempting FD-path shortcut. A stable alias for the retained sealed image or
a separately enrolled bootstrap therefore needs its own lifecycle/trust design.
The implementation keeps that decision explicit instead of enabling an unproved
path. No performance gain, original launch or server readiness is claimed.

### Reject an address design when its original object cannot be mounted

The [sealed launcher bind experiment](../testing/performance/0.74/held-bind-bootstrap-20261023.md)
overturned the earlier recommendation on the actual local kernel. Its first
open_tree refused the original sealed memfd before any publication. A regular
file would be easier to mount, but substituting one would answer a different
identity question. The incomplete prototype is retained as rejected source text,
not installed runtime, and the original bind gate remains red.

The distinct regular-file control also illustrates why partial observations must
not replace a whole result. It observed the same readonly inode after source FD
closure and real creator SIGKILL while an external process retained the namespace.
Its cleanup then failed because ismount did not recognize a same-filesystem bind
mount. The whole control therefore failed. An offline regression corrects that
cleanup assumption without repeating the experiment or turning an unsealed file
into evidence about the original launcher.

The user approved a separately trusted bootstrap instead. Its first implementation
adds independently protected key, policy and image selectors, bound to the same
held policy and epoch. Fresh retained-file validation and shared sticky refusal
prevent an input from repairing itself after failure. These selectors are not a
completed enrollment or execution proof: purpose-bound build evidence, original
owner/frame admission and the child's one-shot execveat still have to join.
No file copy, relaxed seal, refreshed deadline or silent fallback bridges that gap.

### Bind build assertions to ownership before enabling execution

The [bootstrap provenance join](../testing/performance/0.74/bootstrap-build-owner-20261023.md)
now makes the next distinction executable in code. A protected selector chooses
the complete signed policy and independent key. Separate signature domains bind
the policy and build receipt without allowing either to masquerade as the other.
The receipt states exact source/toolchain/profile/content observations; a valid
signature authenticates that assertion, not an independently witnessed compiler.

Static provenance alone still cannot select an attempt. The new wrapper consumes
the already materialized original owner and compares policy/receipt/host/launcher
digests from that owner's actual context. It retains both the protected source
identity and the same sealed bootstrap image. Complete existing frames bracket
new checks and close after positional hashing, so the additional work does not
refresh an admission deadline. Any refusal retires that owner rather than
returning a reusable execution handle.

Unit signatures, actual retained-file checks and deterministic owner fault models
establish different properties. None is a real original-start or all-writer
cessation observation. The bootstrap executable, child credentials/FD protocol,
expanded inventory and one-shot execveat remain the next execution boundary.

### Close image descriptor roles before defining a child protocol

The [bootstrap image census](../testing/performance/0.74/bootstrap-image-census-20261023.md)
closes a concrete gap in the preceding ownership join. A verified image and a
retained File were not enough to show that host, launcher and bootstrap occupied
distinct roles relative to the entire old descriptor set. The extension now
binds all 26 descriptors and fourteen semantic roles under the same observation.
It checks descriptor collisions, inode aliases, exact seals and readonly/CLOEXEC
state, including metadata and offset drift, without exporting an FD array.

The original full frames still authenticate the old prefix and close the new
value checks. No extra hash round or clock query is needed; the existing check
count/order and admission origins remain. Actual private memfd tests exercise
the added kernel properties, while modeled old-prefix/provider inputs exercise
mapping and sticky refusal. Neither becomes an original child-start observation.
The next step remains sealed entry materialization and an authenticated fixed
child protocol before any one-shot execveat or all-writer completion claim.

### Immutable entry bytes are assertions, not authenticated authority

The next [entry binding component](../testing/performance/0.74/bootstrap-entry-binding-20261023.md)
addresses a different question: which exact attempt would a future child entry
